Title: Speech at Finance Denmark's Conference on Governors 2019
text: SPEECH BY GOVERNOR LARS ROHDE AT FINANCE DENMARK'S CONFERENCE OF DIRECTORS THE SPOKEN WORD APPLIES 2. september 2019 Planche 1: Home Thank you for the invitation to speak here today. Today I have chosen to talk about a topic that is very much in focus at the moment. It is a topic that raises a number of issues for the financial sector. Namely, the low interest rates. Planche 2: All government bonds now have negative yields Not many people had predicted that we could find ourself in a situation like this. Interest rates are historically low, and there's no indication that that's going to change any time soon. In Denmark, the certificate of deposit rate has been negative since July 2012, if you exclude a few months in 2014, when the interest rate was marginally positive. In other words, we have had a negative policy rate for the majority of the past 7 years. We have now come into the situation that all Danish government bonds are traded at a negative interest rate. The yield curve has shifted significantly since the end of 2018. Planche 3: Mortgage rates also continue downwards Danish mortgage rates have also fallen to the lowest levels ever. Falling government and mortgage rates have followed European interest rates. The current uncertainty in financial markets is due, inter alia, to the US-China trade conflict and the risk of recession in the US and euro area. The final outcome of the Brexit negotiations is also very uncertain. Page 1 of 8 Planche 4: Historically high conversion wave in October 2019 The continued decline in mortgage rates has led to the introduction of new bond series with ever lower coupon rates. New bottom records on fixed-rate mortgages have prompted a record number of homeowners to restructure their loans. In July, mortgages worth DKK 111 billion were converted, but the continued fall in interest rates has meant that conversions in October will be even higher  a whopping DKK 183 billion. It is the vast majority of mortgages with a coupon rate of 2 per cent, which are converted to October. Since then, interest rates have fallen further and mortgage bonds are now being issued with a coupon rate of 0.5 per cent. The conversion wave can thus continue to the next due date. Planche 5: Low interest rates are due to both cyclical and structural conditions The nominal interest rate is historically low, partly due to low inflation. But also purged of inflation, interest rates are very low. The size "natural real interest rate" indicates the level of the real interest rate when the actual activity of the economy is in line with the potential one. That is, the activity that is compatible with stable price and wage developments. The natural real interest rate is not directly observable, but must be modelled. The natural real interest rate has been declining since the early 1990s and is now by all accounts negative. We see the same development in other advanced economies. It has both cyclical and structural causes. The main reason is a large global savings. Average life expectancy is increasing in these decades across most of the globe, and longer lifespans provide increased incentives for savings, even in emerging economies such as China, where negative savings would otherwise be expected. In addition, the financial crisis has put a scare in the lives of many, and it has also led to more savings and more moderate growth in consumption. The size of the natural real interest rate, also called r* in the economic literature, has an impact on monetary policy transmission. The policy rate must be seen in relation to r* when assessing whether monetary policy stimulates or is contractive. This means that, despite the low policy interest rates, monetary policy is less expansionary than one might think. Page 2 of 8 Whether it is high savings or low investments that lead to the low interest rate is difficult to say. In addition, there is a paradox: Saving for a purpose, e.g. to secure a certain income as a pensioner, low interest rates mean that even more must be saved. The level of interest rates is offset across countries as a result of free international movement of capital. In Denmark, the fixed exchange rate policy links the Danish interest rate to the interest rate in the euro area. There are no expectations that the situation with low nominal and real interest rates will change any time soon. An example of this is that at the end of June this year, Austria has successfully issued a nearly 100-year bond at a rate of 1.17% p.a. But since its issuance, a lot has happened. The interest rate has subsequently fallen by 50 basis points, corresponding to a capital gain of more than 30 per cent. Planche 6: Who contributes to the high global savings? Global private financial wealth is concentrated in the richest people in the United States, China and Japan. The plaque shows who contributes the most to the global "savings glut", as it is also called. Savings glut is an expression of a situation where the savings exceed what there are of profitable investments to invest in. It is noteworthy, among other things, that an emerging economy like China contributes so much to global savings. The world's households especially increased their savings in the wake of the financial crisis and have had high savings since (about 5% of global GDP). The assets of the above groups correspond roughly to the total public debt of the world. In recent years, there have been savings surpluses in both companies, households and the public sector  this has not been seen before at the same time. The counterpart of the high savings in households is a historically low consumption ratio. In recent decades, the chronic current account deficit of the past has turned into large surpluses of currently around 6% of GDP. However, it is a level that is likely to decline in the long term. Planche 7: Banks' earnings cannot be expected to return to historically high levels If we turn to the banks, I can see that the largest banking groups continue to have high earnings. Earnings were lower in 2018 than the historically high levels in 2016 and 2017, but still considerable. Earnings have been buoyed by very low loan impairments due to low interest rates and favourable business cycles. The low write-down- Page 3 of 8 2016-17 levels cannot be expected to return to 2016-17 levels. The falling interest rates have led to changes in the composition of banks' earnings, with net interest income taking up a relatively smaller share and net fee and contribution income a relatively larger share. The outlook for 2019 looks nice so far, as earnings are positively impacted by the large conversion volume. Planche 8: Earnings and policy interest rates There has been some talk about banks' costs of negative certificate of deposit rates. I'd like to make a few comments on that. First of all, I would like to make it clear with seven-inch nails that certificates of deposit and folio accounts are monetary policy instruments, not instruments to support bank earnings. Folio accounts must ensure that the daily liquidity exchange can be done in a safe and smooth manner. In the current situation, an increase in the folio framework would reduce the pass-through from the certificate of deposit rate to money market rates. A significant increase in the folio framework will therefore require a reduction in the certificate of deposit rate in order to ensure the same pass-through to money market rates and thus keep the krone price fixed. Overall, nothing has been gained from this. Today we are in a situation of structurally low interest rates at European level, which looks set to continue for some time to come. It is a situation that affects the entire financial sector, including banks and central banks. Danmarks Nationalbank has a system whereby Danish banks up to a certain amount are exempt from negative interest rates. But let me stress that it is not Danmarks Nationalbank's task to exempt Danish banks from structurally low interest rates. Incidentally, I would like to remind you that Danmarks Nationalbank's surplus accrues to the State. If banks are to be further compensated, it will mean a transfer of funds from the state to the banks. It is difficult to defend in the current situation, where the earnings of banks remain neat. In addition, let me quantify the effect of the negative certificate of deposit rate on banks' earnings. In 2018, the banks' holdings of certificates of deposit yielded a negative return of approximately DKK 1 billion. In comparison, the total earnings in the Danish banking sector amounted to approximately DKK 40 billion in the same period. If you look at the entire period from 2012-18, where the certificate of deposit rate has been negative most of the time, the negative Page 4 of 8 returns on certificates of deposit amounted to approximately DKK 4 billion, while the banks' earnings amounted to approximately DKK 218 billion. Another much-debated topic has been the introduction of negative deposit rates for wealthy private customers. In this connection, let me make it quite clear that the deposit rate for private individuals has no bearing on fixed exchange rate policy. It is a decision for the individual bank whether it chooses to set negative deposit rates for its customers. Planche 9: The number of banks continues to decline As a bank, one must be ready to continuously adapt the business model to changing conditions. The number of Danish banks has been declining for several years. Whereas in 1980 there were almost 300 Danish banks in Denmark, in 2018 the number was reduced to 65. There are a number of factors that play into this development. One aspect is the ongoing wave of digitalisation, which places significant demands on individual banks for investments and adjustments to keep up with developments. Digitalisation can lead to greater diversification between small and large players, as large banks can take advantage of economies of scale. Digitalisation also opens up a number of new players who can influence the future business areas of the traditional banking groups. Competition from new players is welcome. But it is important to keep in place that actors acting as a bank must also be regulated as a bank. Increased regulation since the financial crisis also places demands on the banks' technical capabilities, including not least the area of money laundering. It also contributes to the trend of fewer banks. As a bank, you must be ready to continuously adapt the business model to the increasing demands for regulation and digitization, but also to deal with challenges such as the low-interest rate environment and geopolitical risks such as trade war and Brexit. The future will show whether banks are doing enough to keep up with developments. Planche 10: Credit quality of banks' business lending is significantly better in the big banks The continued low level of interest rates naturally leads to a search for returns. In banks, competition for customers increases due to the modest loan demand and abundant liquidity. Banks continue to report that increased competition negatively affects credit standards for professions. Competitive pressures have primarily been expressed in lower requirements for interest margins and fees. Page 5 of 8 Banks' credit standards determine the credit quality of the loan portfolio. If we compare the credit quality of business lending in the large and medium-sized banks, there is a distinct difference. The profitability of the loan portfolio is significantly better in the large banks than in the medium-sized banks. Lower profitability may help explain the higher interest margins on business lending in medium-sized banks. However, whether banks' lending rates are set high enough to cover risks is only known with certainty when the cyclical situation changes and write-downs and losses begin to rise. Since interest rates are already at historically low levels, banks need to prepare for a recession without significant interest rate declines. It is therefore important that banks are robust before the trend reverses. Planche 11: Building the countercyclical capital buffer It is therefore now, while times are good and risk building is underway, that the countercyclical capital buffer needs to be built. When risks eventually materialize and stress occurs in the financial system, the buffer can be released. This reduces the risk that insufficient capital adequacy will lead institutions to tighten credit to such an extent that a credit squeeze arises. The countercyclical capital buffer is an important macroprudential tool. The aim is to counteract a negative effect on the real economy of a future financial crisis. The buffer should not  and cannot  slow down sharply rising house prices or excessive loan growth in times of upturn. Rather, it must build resilience in institutions. The Systemic Risk Council expects to recommend a further increase in the countercyclical capital buffer rate at its meeting in September (from 1.5 to 2%). The goal is to reach 2.5% before the trend reverses. That goal is set to ensure that the buffer is of sufficient size to make a difference. Planche 12: Moderation of growth in house prices  signs of soft landing in Copenhagen The housing market has helped to support the boom with rising prices and high turnover. The price development in the metropolitan area for a while gave rise to concerns with growth rates on especially condominiums of more than 10 per cent per year. Over the past year, upside price pressures have lessened, and prices have flattened and even fallen slightly. In other words, it promises to be a soft landing for the Copenhagen housing- Page 6 of 8 market. We see the same development in other major cities. Prices of houses nationwide continue to rise at a steady pace. Many factors are at play when it comes to home prices. Developments in disposable incomes, interest rates, new construction, migration patterns and property taxation. A significant increase in interest rates could trigger a downward correction in the housing market, and the decline could potentially be frenzied. This is especially true if the rise in interest rates comes after a long period of very low interest rates, which has been embedded in the price level. This must be borne in mind, although  as I have argued  there is no immediate prospect of a significantly higher level of interest rates. There has been some talk that the Growth Guide  or "Guidance on prudence in the credit rating when mortgageting homes in growth areas, etc.", which is the more precise term, prevents young, creditworthy families from buying a home in Copenhagen. Let me make a few things clear here about the ongoing debate. First; if restrictions on access to floating rate loans had not been introduced for indebted households, house prices would probably have continued to rise. It wouldn't make it any easier for young families to enter the housing market. Second; The growth guidance ensures that homebuyers in growth areas who want a variable loan can withstand a house price drop. In my view, that's a good thing. Next year, there will be (hopefully) new property valuations, and from 2021 a new housing tax regime will take effect. After this, housing taxes will be increased by an increase in house prices and eased by a fall in house prices, i.e. an automatic stabilizer. It will help smooth out cyclical fluctuations. The new assessments could provide a correction in the market for condominiums in the major cities with very high square footage prices. Danmarks Nationalbank has estimated that the new property valuations and the new tax regime in isolation may result in a decrease in the price of expensive owner-occupied flats of almost 10 per cent. It is a correction that the market will be able to bear after a long period of large increases. The change in the housing tax has been known for a while, and the prescient condominium buyer must be expected to have taken it into account in the deals that have been made in the past few years. Planche 13: Housing stock adjusts downward in parts of the country Despite general progress, the housing market is challenged in parts of the country. New construction by today's standards can hardly be done at prices of DKK 10-15,000 per square meter. It is above the price of existing properties in many Page 7 of 8 parts of the country (indicated by blue in the plank). These are also the areas with a very weak or directly declining population growth, mainly because the young people are moving to the city. In parts of the country, there is a need for declines in housing stock to make the market clear. The poorest properties must be demolished. Thus, low prices are to some extent structural in nature rather than cyclically conditioned. Of course, this must be taken into account in lending. Planche 14: Is your bank prepared? To sum up, the financial sector faces a number of issues in the coming period in the form of macro-financial uncertainty, low interest rates, digitalisation, regulation and compliance. In my opinion, there are 3 areas that are particularly important to focus on. Credit policy must not be relaxed in pursuit of increased business volume or to retain customers. While it may be tempting in good times to increase earnings, the consequences of too accommodative credit policy will show when write-downs and losses begin to rise in a recession. Building up capital in good times. The requirements for the banks' capital structure will be noticeably tightened in the coming years. It is important to build up sufficient capital in good times so that banks do not have to tighten credit policy when the business cycle turns. Prospect of lower earnings: Write-downs will increase as the cyclical situation worsens and push earnings downward. In addition to the cyclical, as a bank you must adapt your business model to the low-interest rate environment and the increasing demands for regulation and digitization. If it doesn't work out, it's going to be hard. One solution might be consolidation. text_original: TALE VED NATIONALBANKDIREKTR LARS ROHDE P FINANS DANMARKS DIREKTRKONFERENCE DET TALTE ORD GLDER 2. september 2019 Planche 1: Forside Tak for invitationen til at tale her i dag. Jeg har i dag valgt at tale om et emne, som der er stor fokus p i jeblikket. Det er et emne, der rejser en rkke problemstillinger for den finansielle sektor. Nemlig de lave renter. Planche 2: Alle statsobligationer har nu negativ rente Der er vist ikke mange, der havde forudset, at vi kunne komme i en situation som denne. Renterne er historisk lave, og der er ikke noget, der tyder p, at det kommer til at ndre sig lige forelbig. I Danmark har indskudsbevisrenten vret negativ siden juli 2012, hvis man fraregner nogle f mneder i 2014, hvor renten var marginalt positiv. Vi har med andre ord haft en negativ pengepolitisk rente i hovedparten af de seneste 7 r. Vi er nu kommet i den situation, at alle danske statsobligationer handles til en negativ rente. Rentekurven har rykket sig markant siden slutningen af 2018. Planche 3: Realkreditrenter fortstter ogs nedad De danske realkreditrenter er ogs faldet til de laveste niveauer nogensinde. De faldende stats- og realkreditrenter er fulgt med de europiske renter ned. Den nuvrende usikkerhed p de finansielle markeder skyldes bl.a. handelskonflikten mellem USA og Kina og risikoen for recession i USA og euroomrdet. Det endelige udfald af brexit-forhandlingerne er ogs meget usikkert. Side 1 af 8 Planche 4: Historisk hj konverteringsblge i oktober 2019 De fortsat faldende realkreditrenter har frt til introduktionen af nye obligationsserier med stadig lavere kuponrente. Nye bundrekorder p fastforrentede realkreditln har fet rekordmange boligejere til at omlgge deres ln. I juli blev der konverteret realkreditln for 111 mia. kr., men det fortsatte fald i renterne har betydet, at konverteringer i oktober bliver endnu hjere  hele 183 mia. kr. Det er langt overvejende realkreditln med en kuponrente p 2 pct., som konverteres til oktober. Siden er renterne faldet yderligere, og der udstedes nu realkreditobligationer med en kuponrente p 0,5 pct. Konverteringsblgen kan dermed forstte til nste termin. Planche 5: Lave renter skyldes bde konjunkturmssige og strukturelle forhold Den nominelle rente er historisk lav, bl.a. som flge af lav inflation. Men ogs renset for inflation er renten meget lav. Strrelsen "den naturlige realrente" angiver niveauet for realrenten, nr den faktiske aktivitet i konomien er p linje med den potentielle. Dvs. den aktivitet, der er forenelig med en stabil pris- og lnudvikling. Den naturlige realrente er ikke direkte observerbar, men m modelberegnes. Den naturlige realrente har vret faldende siden begyndelsen af 1990'erne og er nu efter alt at dmme negativ. Samme udvikling ser vi i andre avancerede konomier. Det har bde konjunkturmssige og strukturelle rsager. Hovedrsagen er en stor global opsparing. Den gennemsnitlige levetid stiger i disse rtier over det meste af kloden, og lngere levetid giver get incitament til opsparing, ogs i vkstkonomier som Kina, hvor man ellers ville forvente negativ opsparing. Hertil kommer, at finanskrisen har sat en skrk i livet p mange, og det har ogs frt til mere opsparing og mere moderat vkst i forbruget. Strrelsen p den naturlige realrente, ogs kaldet r* i den konomiske litteratur, har betydning for den pengepolitiske transmission. Den pengepolitiske rente m ses i forhold til r* ved en vurdering af, om pengepolitikken stimulerer eller er kontraktiv. Det betyder, at pengepolitikken trods de lave pengepolitiske renter er mindre ekspansiv, end man umiddelbart skulle tro. Side 2 af 8 Om det er hj opsparing eller lave investeringer, der frer til den lave rente, er svrt at sige. Hertil kommer et paradoks: Spares der op til et forml, fx at sikre en bestemt indkomst som pensionist, betyder lav rente, at der skal spares endnu mere op. Renteniveauet udlignes p tvrs af lande som flge af frie internationale kapitalbevgelser. Herhjemme knytter fastkurspolitikken den danske rente til renten i euroomrdet. Der er ikke forventninger om, at situationen med lave nominelle og reale renter ndrer sig lige forelbigt. Et eksempel p det er, at strig i slutningen af juni i r med held har udstedt en nsten 100-rig obligation til en rente p 1,17 pct. p.a. Men siden udstedelsen er der sket en del. Renten er efterflgende faldet med 50 basispoint svarende til en kursgevinst p mere end 30 pct. Planche 6: Hvem bidrager til den hje globale opsparing? Den globale private finansielle formue er koncentreret hos de rigeste mennesker i USA, Kina og Japan. Planchen viser, hvem der bidrager mest til globalt savings glut, som det ogs kaldes. Savings glut er udtryk for en situation, hvor opsparingen overstiger, hvad der er af rentable investeringer at investere i. Det er bl.a. bemrkelsesvrdigt, at en vkstkonomi som Kina bidrager s stort til den globale opsparing. Verdens husholdninger gede isr deres opsparing i klvandet p finanskrisen og har haft en hj opsparing siden (ca. 5 pct. af global BNP). Aktiverne for de ovenstende grupper svarer nogenlunde til den samlede offentlige gld i verden. Herhjemme har der de senere r vret opsparingsoverskud i bde virksomheder, husholdninger og den offentlige sektor  det er ikke set tidligere p samme tid. Modstykket til den hje opsparing i husholdningerne er en historisk lav forbrugskvote. Tidligere tiders kroniske betalingsbalanceunderskud er de seneste rtier vendt til store overskud p i jeblikket ca. 6 pct. af BNP. Det er dog et niveau, der m forventes at falde p sigt. Planche 7: Bankernes indtjening kan ikke forventes at komme tilbage p historisk hje niveauer Hvis vi vender os mod bankerne, kan jeg konstatere, at de strste bankkoncerner fortsat har hj indtjening. Indtjeningen var lavere i 2018 end de historisk hje niveauer i 2016 og 2017, men alts stadig anseelig. Indtjeningen har vret bret oppe af meget lave nedskrivninger p udln som flge af lave renter og favorable konjunkturer. Det lave nedskriv- Side 3 af 8 ningsniveau kan ikke ventes at fortstte, og afkastet kan ikke forventes at komme tilbage p niveauet fra 2016-17 igen. De faldende renter har frt til ndringer i sammenstningen af bankernes indtjening, hvor nettorenteindtgter fylder en relativt mindre andel og nettogebyr og bidragsindtgter en relativt strre andel. Udsigterne for 2019 ser indtil videre pne ud, da indtjeningen pvirkes positivt af det store konverteringsomfang. Planche 8: Indtjening og pengepolitiske renter Der har vret en del snak om bankernes omkostninger ved negativ indskudsbevisrente. Det vil jeg gerne knytte et par kommentarer til. Frst og fremmest vil jeg gerne sl fast med syvtommersm, at indskudsbeviser og foliokonti er pengepolitiske instrumenter, ikke instrumenter til at understtte bankernes indtjening. Foliokonti skal sikre, at den daglige likviditetsudveksling kan ske p en sikker og smidig mde. I den nuvrende situation vil en forhjelse af foliorammen reducere gennemslaget fra indskudsbevisrenten til pengemarkedsrenterne. En betydelig forgelse af foliorammen vil derfor krve en nedsttelse af indskudsbevisrenten for at sikre samme gennemslag til pengemarkedsrenterne og dermed holde kronekursen fast. Det er der samlet set ikke vundet noget ved. I dag str vi i en situation med strukturelt lave renter p europisk plan, der ser ud til at fortstte en rum tid endnu. Det er en situation, der pvirker hele den finansielle sektor, herunder banker og centralbanker. Nationalbanken har et system, hvor danske banker op til et vist belb friholdes for negative renter. Men lad mig understrege, at det ikke er Nationalbankens opgave at friholde danske banker for strukturelt lave renter. I vrigt vil jeg minde om, at Nationalbankens overskud tilfalder staten. Hvis bankerne skal kompenseres yderligere, vil det betyde en overfrsel af midler fra staten til bankerne. Det er svrt at forsvare i den nuvrende situation, hvor bankernes indtjening fortsat er pn. Lad mig desuden stte lidt tal p effekten af den negative indskudsbevisrente p bankernes indtjening. I 2018 gav bankernes beholdning af indskudsbeviser et negativt afkast p ca. 1 mia. kr. Til sammenligning var den samlede indtjening i den danske banksektor p ca. 40 mia. kr. i samme periode. Hvis man kigger p hele perioden fra 2012-18, hvor indskudsbevisrenten har vret negativ det meste af tiden, har det negative Side 4 af 8 afkast p indskudsbeviser vret ca. 4 mia. kr., mens bankernes indtjening udgjorde ca. 218 mia. kr. Et andet meget debatteret emne har vret indfrelsen af negative indlnsrenter for formuende privatkunder. Lad mig i den forbindelse gre det helt klart, at indlnsrenten for private ikke har betydning for fastkurspolitikken. Det er en beslutning for den enkelte bank, om den vlger at stte negative indlnsrenter for dens kunder. Planche 9: Antallet af banker falder fortsat Som bank m man vre klar til lbende at tilpasse forretningsmodellen til ndrede vilkr. Antallet af danske banker har vret faldende igennem flere r. Hvor der i 1980 var nsten 300 danske banker i Danmark, var antallet i 2018 reduceret til 65. Der er en rkke forhold, der spiller ind p denne udvikling. Et forhold er den igangvrende digitaliseringsblge, der stiller betydelige krav til de enkelte banker om investeringer og tilpasninger for at flge med udviklingen. Digitalisering kan fre til strre spredning mellem sm og store spillere, da store banker kan udnytte stordriftsfordele. Digitalisering bner ogs op for en rkke nye spillere, som kan pvirke de fremtidige forretningsomrder for de traditionelle bankkoncerner. Konkurrence fra nye spillere er velkommen. Men det er vigtigt at holde fast i, at aktrer, der agerer som bank, ogs skal reguleres som bank. get regulering siden finanskrisen stiller ogs krav til bankernes tekniske kunnen, herunder ikke mindst hvidvaskomrdet. Det medvirker ogs til tendensen med frre banker. Som bank m man bde vre klar til lbende at tilpasse forretningsmodellen til de stigende krav til regulering og digitalisering, men ogs til at hndtere udfordringer som lavrentemiljet og geopolitiske risici som handelskrig og brexit. Fremtiden vil vise, om bankerne gr nok for at flge med udviklingen. Planche 10: Kreditkvaliteten af bankernes erhvervsudln er betydeligt bedre i de store banker Det fortsat lave renteniveau frer helt naturligt til en sgen efter afkast. I bankerne ges konkurrencen om kunderne som flge af den beskedne lneeftersprgsel og rigelig likviditet. Bankerne melder fortsat, at get konkurrence pvirker kreditstandarder til erhverv negativt. Konkurrencepres er primrt kommet til udtryk i lavere krav til rentemarginaler og gebyrer. Side 5 af 8 Bankernes kreditstandarder er bestemmende for kreditkvaliteten af lneportefljen. Hvis vi sammenligner kreditkvaliteten af erhvervsudlnet i de store og mellemstore banker, er der en tydelig forskel. Boniteten af lneportefljen er betydeligt bedre i de store banker end i de mellemstore banker. Lavere bonitet kan vre med til at forklare de hjere rentemarginaler p erhvervsudln i de mellemstore banker. Om bankernes udlnsrente er sat hjt nok til at dkke risici vides dog frst med sikkerhed, nr konjunktursituationen ndrer sig, og nedskrivninger og tab begynder at stige. Da renterne allerede er p et historisk lavt niveau, skal bankerne forberede sig p en lavkonjunktur uden betydelige rentefald. Det er derfor vigtigt, at bankerne er robuste, inden udviklingen vender. Planche 11: Opbygning af den kontracykliske kapitalbuffer Det er derfor nu, mens tiderne er gode, og risikoopbygningen er i gang, at den kontracykliske kapitalbuffer skal opbygges. Nr risici p et tidspunkt materialiserer sig, og der opstr stress i det finansielle system, kan bufferen frigives. Det reducerer risikoen for, at utilstrkkelig kapitaldkning fr institutterne til at stramme kreditgivningen i en sdan grad, at der opstr en kreditklemme. Den kontracykliske kapitalbuffer er et vigtigt makroprudentielt vrktj. Formlet er at modvirke en negativ effekt p realkonomien af en fremtidig finansiel krise. Bufferen skal ikke  og kan ikke  bremse kraftigt stigende boligpriser eller overdreven udlnsvkst i opgangstider. Den skal derimod opbygge modstandskraft i institutterne. Det Systemiske Risikord forventer at henstille om en yderligere forhjelse af den kontracykliske kapitalbuffersats p mdet i september (fra 1,5 til 2 pct.). Mlet er at n op p 2,5 pct., inden udviklingen vender. Det ml er sat for at sikre, at bufferen har en tilstrkkelig strrelse til at kunne gre en forskel. Planche 12: Afdmpning af vksten i boligpriserne  tegn p bld landing i Kbenhavn Boligmarkedet har vret med til at understtte hjkonjunkturen med stigende priser og hj omstning. Prisudviklingen i hovedstadsomrdet gav en overgang anledning til bekymring med vkstrater p isr ejerlejligheder p over 10 pct. pr. r. Det seneste r er det opadrettede prispres blevet mindre, og priserne er fladet ud og endog faldet lidt. Det tegner med andre ord til en bld landing for det kbenhavnske bolig- Side 6 af 8 marked. Samme udvikling ser vi i andre af de store byer. Priserne p huse p landsplan stiger fortsat i roligt tempo. Mange faktorer er i spil, nr det glder boligpriser. Udvikling i de disponible indkomster, renteniveau, nybyggeri, migrationsmnstre og ejendomsbeskatning. En markant stigning i renten vil kunne udlse en nedadrettet korrektion p boligmarkedet, og tilbagegangen kan potentielt set blive hidsig. Det glder ikke mindst, hvis rentestigningen kommer efter en lang periode med meget lave renter, som er blevet indlejret i prisniveauet. Det skal man have sig for je, selv om der  som jeg har argumenteret for  ikke umiddelbart er udsigt til et markant hjere renteniveau. Der har vret en del snak om, at Vkstvejledningen  eller "Vejledning om forsigtighed i kreditvurderingen ved belning af boliger i vkstomrder mv.", som er den mere prcise betegnelse, forhindrer unge, kreditvrdige familier i at kbe en bolig i Kbenhavn. Lad mig her sl et par ting fast om den verserende debat. For det frste; hvis man ikke havde indfrt begrnsninger p adgangen til variabelt forrentede ln for forgldede husholdninger, ville boligpriserne formentlig have fortsat deres stigning. Det ville ikke gre det nemmere for unge familier at komme ind p boligmarkedet. For det andet; Vkstvejledningen sikrer, at boligkbere i vkstomrderne, der nsker et variabelt ln, kan modst et boligprisfald. Det er i min optik en god ting. Til nste r kommer der (forhbentlig) nye ejendomsvurderinger, og fra 2021 trder et nyt boligskatteregime i kraft. Herefter vil boligskatterne blive get ved stigning i boligpriserne og blive lempet ved fald i boligpriserne, dvs. en automatisk stabilisator. Det vil hjlpe med at udjvne konjunkturudsving. De nye vurderinger kan give en korrektion p markedet for ejerlejligheder i de strre byer med meget hje kvadratmeterpriser. Nationalbanken har sknnet, at de nye ejendomsvurderinger og det nye skatteregime isoleret set kan medfre et fald i prisen p dyre ejerlejligheder p knap 10 pct. Det er en korrektion, som markedet vil kunne bre efter en lang periode med store stigninger. ndringen af boligbeskatningen har vret kendt et stykke tid, og den forudseende ejerlejlighedskber m forventes at have taget det i betragtning ved de handler, der er blevet indget de seneste par r. Planche 13: Boligmassen tilpasser sig nedad i dele af landet Trods generel fremgang er boligmarkedet udfordret i dele af landet. Nybyggeri efter dagens standard kan nppe ske til priser p 10-15.000 kr. pr. kvadratmeter. Det er over prisen p eksisterende ejendomme i mange Side 7 af 8 dele af landet (angivet med blt i planchen). Det er samtidig de omrder med en meget svag eller direkte faldende befolkningsvkst, hovedsagelig fordi de unge flytter til byen. I dele af landet er der behov for fald i boligmassen for at f markedet til at cleare. De ringeste ejendomme m rives ned. De lave priser er sledes i et vist omfang af strukturel karakter snarere end konjunkturmssigt betinget. Det m der naturligvis tages hensyn til i lngivningen. Planche 14: Er din bank forberedt? For at opsummere str den finansielle sektor over for en rkke problemstillinger i den kommende tid i form af makrofinansiel usikkerhed, lave renter, digitalisering, regulering og compliance. Der er i min optik 3 omrder, der er srligt vigtige at have fokus p. Kreditpolitikken m ikke lempes i jagten p get forretningsomfang eller for at fastholde kunderne. Selv om det kan friste i gode tider at ge indtjeningen, vil konsekvenserne af for lempelig kreditpolitik vise sig, nr nedskrivninger og tab begynder at stige i en konjunkturnedgang. Opbygning af kapital i gode tider. Kravene til bankernes kapitalstruktur bliver skrpet mrkbart de kommende r. Det er vigtigt at opbygge tilstrkkelig kapital i gode tider, s bankerne ikke af den grund bliver ndt til at stramme kreditpolitikken, nr konjunkturerne vender. Udsigt til lavere indtjening: Nedskrivninger vil stige, nr konjunktursituationen forvrres og presse indtjeningen nedad. Udover det konjunkturelle skal man som bank form at indrette sin forretningsmodel p lavrentemiljet og de stigende krav til regulering og digitalisering. Hvis det ikke forms, bliver det svrt. En lsning kan vre konsolidering. Title: Speech, Politiken's conference 'What we learned from the financial crisis'
text: DANMARKS NATIONALBANK Governor Nils Bernstein's speech at Politiken's conference "What we learned from the financial crisis" Friday, November 12, 2010 THE SPOKEN WORD APPLIES From mid-2003, Denmark had a boom that lasted until the end of 2007. Growth in Denmark was not higher than in the euro area and the US, but took place closer to the capacity limit. When the financial crisis hit Denmark, growth was already on the way down. During the boom, private and public consumption in Denmark increased faster than in most countries we normally compare ourselves to. Fiscal policy in the years 2004-2007 was cyclical, i.e. it contributed to the high level of activity. Unemployment fell from 2004 to mid-2008, when the financial crisis turned into an economic crisis, abruptly sending unemployment soaring from a record low of 1.7 percent. During the boom, real house prices rose by more than 50 per cent  far more in the capital. And real estate investments followed up. The Danish policy rate, as measured by Danmarks Nationalbank's lending rate, was just over 2% in the first half of the boom and then just over 3% on average in the second half. As you know, Danmarks Nationalbank's lending rate is set in accordance with the fixed exchange rate policy and therefore could not be used to counter the overheating of the economy. The Danish banks' total lending increased sharply during the recovery. The growth in lending for real estate purposes was particularly marked  especially from small and medium-sized banks. The banks' deposit deficit, i.e. the difference between their total loans and their deposits from customers, grew during the boom to approximately DKK 600 billion, the majority of which was collected abroad. The financial crisis started in the United States in August 2007. After that, it gradually and with different strengths spread to the rest of the world until September 2008, when, after the collapse of Lehman Bro, it escalated and culminated the following month. Money markets froze and banks' access to unsecured loans disappeared. Governments and central banks had to step in with loans and guarantees. The events of the autumn of 2008 hit the real economy with great strength, and 2 world trade fell by 20 per cent. In Denmark, where total production had peaked in 2007, GDP fell by around 7.5% from the fourth quarter of 2007 to the second quarter of 2009. That's little more than the decline in the countries we usually compare ourselves to. The financial crisis of subprime loans and the collapse or near collapse of many financial institutions that had invested in opaque securities came first to us from the outside. The same applies to the real economic shock in the form of the decline in world trade, which in a short time caused Danish exports to fall by 15 per cent. However, there can be no doubt that during the boom we ourselves would have made ourselves vulnerable to external shocks, and would also have had a downturn without the financial crisis and the resulting international recession. Let's take a closer look at the main areas  and let's start with the positive: We can start by rejoicing that the balance of payments throughout the process  both during the boom and during the current recession  has been robust and shown a solid surplus. As some will recall, it was once our economic Achilles heel. Public debt at the beginning of the crisis was low  at least compared to many other countries, and although during the crisis it has increased by 15 percent in relation to total production, the next year it will not exceed 50% of GDP. When we have warned against just letting the debt grow, it is due to the fact that our debt room is limited in the sense that Danish taxes are near a maximum and that public savings are difficult to gather political support for. It is therefore not easy to find room in the state budget to pay interest and pay off a higher debt. Our crisis response in the form of automatic stabilizers has worked: taxes and duties have been automatically reduced, while the cost of unemployment benefits and cash benefits has increased. Politically, they have chosen to stimulate further by, among other things, increasing public investment, and several parties have spoken in favor of easing even more. It is noteworthy that during the boom, when the automatic stabilisers in isolation dampened the business cycle, there was no corresponding willingness to stabilise the economy against overheating by political decisions. On the contrary, decisions were made that reinforced the boom. This asymmetry is dangerous and without economic foundation. If we then go to the financial area, I think many would agree that the currency crisis of autumn 2008 clearly demonstrated one of the advantages of being within the euro area. We only made it through by intervening massively in the foreign exchange market in support of the crown and by raising interest rates significantly while other countries cut interest rates. We received benevolent assistance in the form of 3 swap agreements with the European Central Bank (ECB) and the US Central Bank (Fed) so that we could lend euros and dollars to Danish banks. At Danmarks Nationalbank, we had underestimated the need for a larger foreign exchange reserve. We had expected that the state would be able to borrow additional currency in the international markets if the need arose. It proved impossible to raise currency that way at acceptable prices. We had to recognize the truth of the banal doctrine, namely that money is most difficult to get to when you need it most. We've learned from that. Many banks had gradually changed their business model during the boom, financed, inter alia, the strong lending growth with borrowing in the money and capital markets, a not insignificant part of which was through short-term loans. When the markets froze in the fall of 2008, the state had to issue a guarantee covering all deposits and loans to banks two years ahead. A guarantee that amounted to 21/2 times the Danish gross domestic product. It was, to put it mildly, no trivial guarantee, and we should all here in the Kingdom rejoice that it has now expired on October 1 and been replaced by far less guarantees. In my view, we must never again find ourself in a situation where a guarantee of that scope and content becomes necessary. In the future, in addition to usual deposits from ordinary customers, the banks' financing must to a much greater extent consist of loans with a long maturity, even though it is more expensive, and solid liquidity reserves must be established. Danmarks Nationalbank supports the tightening of the regulation of financial institutions that is underway. But no matter how we adjust, we will continue to experience business cycles that include ups and downs. The better we are at dampening these fluctuations at as high a level of activity as possible, the more prosperity we will experience. It is not only a Danish experience  it is almost universal  that housing and the property market, including new construction, tend to increase cyclical fluctuations. In the past, Denmark has had quantitative regulations aimed both directly at the housing and real estate markets, but also at lending by banks and mortgage banks. These are schemes that have all been abolished due to inecoability. But if fiscal policy cannot do the job, other means will have to be provided. Internationally, it is being considered to implement rules that generally increase capital requirements for banks and require additional capital in a cyclical recovery, which is then released when it goes the other way. This can help to dampen the cyclical fluctuations. In addition, flexible loan limits for property financing are being considered in several countries, so that the requirements for self-financing increase during a boom. If these changes occur in recognition of the difficulties of pursuing an adequate fiscal policy when needed, it will be natural to 4 conlegate decision-making power over these instruments to an independent body, such as the Central Bank. * * * Couldn't Danmarks Nationalbank have done better? Warned that there was a risk of a financial crisis  gone harder on the government and the banks? Taken a showdown, as it has been formulated in Politiken's columns? I would say without false modesty that Danmarks Nationalbank has played an active and constructive role in the design of the measures implemented in Denmark with a view to reducing the effects of the financial crisis following Lehmann Bro's bankruptcy. But what about the development before the crisis culminated? Couldn't we have done better? Let's take a closer look at it. Danmarks Nationalbank had not foreseen the financial crisis in the form it took with the culmination of Lehmann Brothers' bankruptcy on 15 September 2008. It's a fate we share with most financial players around the world. We have witnessed the biggest financial and economic crisis in 60 years. We have been demonstrated that the unlikely can happen. That we were not alone in the lack of foresight is shown by the fact that worldwide work has been undertaken to prepare the financial sector for similar future events. Today, we have a greater focus on risks that are given little probability  but large consequences if they occur. This is, for example, the reason why Danmarks Nationalbank has expressed concern about the refinancing risk of the very extensive flex loans, which in 2009 amounted to around DKK 550 billion. Danish banks had not invested dangerously in subprime loans. On the other hand, they had made themselves vulnerable to the situation created by the financial crisis  namely the freezing of the money markets and the shutdown of the capital markets. With large deposit deficits, financial institutions had to continuously raise new loans to finance already given loans. This model got into severe difficulties in the fall of 2008. It was a situation Danmarks Nationalbank had warned against several times in previous years. It is debatable whether we warned strongly enough  I'll get back to that  but the warning stayed there. As things developed after Lehmann's bankruptcy, it was estimated that it could become impossible for banks to renew the loans that financed much of their activities. That could trigger an uncontrollable crisis. 5 As mentioned, Bank Package I took care of this risk with a government guarantee for all deposits in and loans to banks. With the state guarantee in the back  in return for payment to the state  the banks' borrowing got going again. What about loan growth and the housing bubble  shouldn't we have taken action across these danger signals? We have been able to read that these were indeed danger signals that were understood at Danmarks Nationalbank in earlier times. I don't know what you imagine. Today, Danmarks Nationalbank has no instruments to take action against unwanted loan growth. Those opportunities disappeared with the liberalization of the money, capital and foreign exchange markets many years ago. The forms of regulation used at the time had become increasingly meaningless, as described in works published with a rigid volume by danmarks Nationalbank. The legal basis for Danmarks Nationalbank's agreements on credit intermediation was abolished in 1996 with express reference to the fact that monetary policy had been given new content. The banks that have had to turn the key, or have been close to it, are all banks that had engaged too heavily in selected parts of the real estate sector. It's a supervisory matter. And the Danish Financial Supervisory Authority has only now been given a broader legal basis to intervene. Let me add that the total losses of the Danish banking sector on loans and guarantees so far have been less than during the Nordic banking crisis in the early 90s. You could say that the lower losses this time are due to the state bailouts, but the state has actually taken good care of the risk it has run with the bank packages. Bank Package II from the winter of 2009 was implemented when the financial crisis had triggered an economic crisis. With the prospect of growing losses on lending and expectations of future greater demands on banks' capital, the concern was that the banks would become so reluctant to lend that we in Denmark could face a real credit squeeze, which would amplify the economic downturn. Against this background, a scheme was introduced according to which solvent financial institutions could receive a state capital injection against market returns. The central economic policy instrument to quell a boom in Denmark is fiscal policy. When tax cuts were granted in 2004, Danmarks Nationalbank stated that the tax cuts were only justifiable if there was a willingness to make corresponding tightening later on, when the cyclical situation called for it. In 2006, Danmarks Nationalbank proposed that fiscal policy be tightened. And repeated it later. It was not advice the government followed. There was also no support from the opposition. And when I proposed in 2006 a tightening of mortgage lenders' loan limits: Limited policy response! In the spring of 2008, before the culminating financial crisis, when I advocated allowing the economic downturn to take hold of unemployment, this idea was loudly rejected by both. 6 despite the fact that the unemployment rate at this time was below 2 per cent, and there was an acute shortage of labour, with the result that Danish wages rose much faster than foreign ones. I myself have previously expressed that Danmarks Nationalbank probably should have warned more loudly about the financial and economic development during the boom. Unfortunately, I don't think it would have made much difference. This is not how Danish politics works. This would have put Danmarks Nationalbank in a better position to face criticism. But it can't be decisive. It's an assessment case whether sharper-worded calls would have had an effect. But experience doesn't speak for it. If you want to give Danmarks Nationalbank greater responsibility for the business cycle, you must also give us some relevant instruments to intervene. Otherwise, it makes no sense.
text_original: DANMARKS NATIONALBANK Nationalbankdirektr Nils Bernsteins indlg ved Politikens konference "Det lrte vi af finanskrisen" Fredag den 12. november 2010 DET TALTE ORD GLDER Danmark havde fra midten af 2003 en hjkonjunktur, der varede til slutningen af 2007. Vksten i Danmark var ikke hjere end i euroomrdet og USA, men fandt sted tttere p kapacitetsgrnsen. Da finanskrisen ramte Danmark var vksten allerede p vej nedad. Under hjkonjunkturen steg det private og det offentlige forbrug i Danmark hurtigere end i de fleste lande, vi normalt sammenligner os med. Finanspolitikken var i rene 2004-2007 konjunkturmedlbende, dvs. den bidrog til det hje aktivitetsniveau. Arbejdslsheden faldt fra 2004 til midt 2008, hvor den finansielle krise udviklede sig til en konomisk krise og brat sendte arbejdslsheden i vejret fra et rekordlavt niveau p 1,7 pct. Under hjkonjunkturen steg de reale boligpriser med mere end 50 pct.  langt mere i hovedstaden. Og ejendomsinvesteringerne fulgte med op. Den danske pengepolitiske rente, mlt ved Nationalbankens udlnsrente var godt 2 pct. i frste halvdel af hjkonjunkturen og derefter godt 3 pct. i gennemsnit i anden halvdel. Nationalbankens udlnsrente faststtes som bekendt i overensstemmelse med fastkurspolitikken og kunne derfor ikke bruges til at imdeg overophedningen af konomien. De danske bankers samlede udln steg kraftigt under opsvinget. Vksten i udln til ejendomsforml var srlig markant  isr fra sm og mellemstore banker. Bankernes indlnsunderskud, dvs. forskellen mellem deres samlede udln og deres indln fra kunder voksede under hjkonjunkturen til ca. 600 mia. kr., hvoraf hovedparten hentedes i udlandet. Finanskrisen startede i USA i august 2007. Herefter spredtes den gradvist og med forskellig styrke til resten af verden indtil september 2008, hvor den efter Lehman Bros kollaps eskalerede og kulminerede den flgende mned. Pengemarkederne frs til og bankernes adgang til ln uden sikkerhed forsvandt. Regeringer og centralbanker mtte trde til med ln og garantier. Begivenhederne i efterret 2008 ramte realkonomien med stor styrke, og 2 verdenshandelen faldt med 20 pct. I Danmark, hvor den samlede produktion var toppet i 2007, faldt BNP med omkring 7,5 pct. fra 4. kvartal 2007 til 2. kvartal 2009. Det er lidt mere end faldet i de lande vi normalt sammenligner os med. Finanskrisen med subprimeln og kollaps eller nr kollaps for mange pengeinstitutter, som havde investeret i uigennemskuelige vrdipapirer, kom i frste rkke til os udefra. Det samme glder det realkonomiske std i form af faldet i verdenshandelen, som p kort tid fik dansk eksport til at falde med 15 pct. Der kan imidlertid ikke vre tvivl om, at vi under hjkonjunkturen selv havde gjort os srbare overfor udefra kommende std, og ogs ville have fet en nedgangskonjunktur uden finanskrisen og den deraf flgende internationale lavkonjunktur. Lad os se nrmere p de vsentligste omrder  og lad os begynde med det positive: Vi kan starte med at glde os over, at betalingsbalancen under hele forlbet  bde under hjkonjunkturen og under den nuvrende lavkonjunktur - har vret robust og vist et solidt overskud. Som nogle vil huske var det engang vores konomiske akilleshl. Den offentlige gld var ved krisens begyndelse lav  i hvert fald sammenlignet med mange andre lande, og selv om den under krisen er steget med 15 procent i forhold til den samlede produktion, vil den nste r ikke overstige 50 % af BNP. Nr vi alligevel fra Nationalbankens side har advaret mod bare at lade glden vokse, hnger det sammen med, at vores gldsrderum er begrnset i den forstand, at de danske skatter er nr et maksimum, og at offentlige besparelser er vanskelige at samle politisk tilslutning til. Det er derfor ikke nemt at finde plads p statsbudgettet til at forrente og afdrage en hjere gld. Vores kriseberedskab i form af automatiske stabilisatorer har virket: Skatter og afgifter er automatisk reduceret, mens udgifter til arbejdslshedsdagpenge og kontanthjlp er get. Politisk har man valgt at stimulere yderligere ved bl.a. at ge de offentlige investeringer, og flere partier har talt for at lempe endnu mere. Det er bemrkelsesvrdigt, at der under hjkonjunkturen, hvor de automatiske stabilisatorer isoleret set dmpede konjunkturudviklingen ikke var en tilsvarende vilje til at stabilisere konomien mod overophedning ved politiske beslutninger. Der blev tvrtimod truffet beslutninger, der forstrkede hjkonjunkturen. Denne asymmetri er farlig og uden konomisk fundament. Hvis vi derefter gr til det finansielle omrde, tror jeg mange er enige i, at valutakrisen i efterret 2008 klart demonstrerede en af fordelene ved at vre inden for euroomrdet. Vi klarede os kun igennem ved at intervenere massivt i valutamarkedet til sttte for kronen og ved at forhje renten markant, mens andre lande satte renten ned. Vi fik velvillig bistand i form af 3 swap-aftaler med Den europiske Centralbank (ECB) og Den amerikanske Centralbank (FED), s vi kunne udlne euro og dollars til danske pengeinstitutter. Vi havde i Nationalbanken undervurderet behovet for en strre valutareserve. Vi havde regnet med, at staten ville kunne lne yderligere valuta p de internationale markeder, hvis behovet opstod. Det viste sig umuligt at rejse valuta p den mde til acceptable priser. Vi mtte erkende sandheden i den banale lrestning, nemlig at penge er vanskeligst at komme til, nr man har mest brug for dem. Det har vi lrt af. Mange banker havde gradvist ndret deres forretningsmodel under hjkonjunkturen og finansierede bl.a. den kraftige udlnsvkst med lntagning p penge- og kapitalmarkederne, heraf en ikke uvsentlig del ved hjlp af korte ln. Da markederne frs til i efterret 2008, mtte staten udstede en garanti, der dkkede alle indskud og ln til banker to r frem. En garanti, der belbsmssigt svarede til 2 gange det danske bruttonationalprodukt. Det var mildt sagt ingen triviel garanti, og vi br alle her i Kongeriget glde os over, at den nu er udlbet 1. oktober og erstattet af langt mindre garantier. Vi m efter min opfattelse aldrig mere komme i en situation, hvor en garanti af det omfang og indhold bliver ndvendig. Bankernes finansiering m fremover ud over sdvanlige indskud fra almindelige kunder i langt hjere grad best af ln med lang lbetid, selv om det er dyrere, ligesom der m etableres solide likviditetsreserver. Danmarks Nationalbank sttter den skrpelse af reguleringen af pengeinstitutter, som er p vej. Men uanset hvordan vi indretter os, vil vi fortsat opleve konjunkturforlb, der indeholder opture og nedture. Jo bedre vi er til at dmpe disse udsving p et s hjt aktivitetsniveau som muligt, desto strre velstand vil vi opleve. Det er ikke blot en dansk erfaring  den er vel nrmest universel  at bolig og ejendomsmarkedet, herunder nybyggeriet, har det med at ge konjunkturudsvingene. Danmark har tidligere haft kvantitative reguleringer bde rettet direkte mod bolig- og ejendomsmarkedet, men ogs rettet mod penge- og realkreditinstitutternes udln. Det er ordninger, der alle er afskaffet p grund af manglende effektivitet. Men hvis finanspolitikken ikke kan lfte opgaven m der andre midler til. Det overvejes internationalt at gennemfre regler, der generelt ger kapitalkravene til bankerne og stiller krav om ekstra kapital i et konjunkturopsving, som s frigives, nr det gr den anden vej. Det kan vre med til at dmpe konjunktursvingningerne. Derudover overvejes det i flere lande at gennemfre fleksible lnegrnser for ejendomsfinansieringen, sledes at kravene til egenfinansieringen stiger under en hjkonjunktur. Hvis disse ndringer sker i erkendelse af vanskelighederne ved at fre en tilstrkkelig finanspolitik, nr der er behov for det, vil det vre naturligt at 4 henlgge beslutningskompetencen over disse instrumenter til et uafhngigt organ, fx centralbanken. * * * Kunne Nationalbanken ikke have gjort det bedre? Advaret om, at der var risiko for en finanskrise  get hrdere til regeringen og bankerne? Taget et opgr, som det har vret formuleret i Politikens spalter? Jeg vil uden falsk beskedenhed sige, at Nationalbanken har spillet en aktiv og konstruktiv rolle ved udformningen af de foranstaltninger, der i Danmark er gennemfrt med henblik p at mindske virkningerne af den finansielle krise efter Lehmann Bros konkurs. Men hvad s med udviklingen fr krisen kulminerede? Kunne vi ikke have gjort det bedre? Lad os se nrmere p det. Danmarks Nationalbank havde ikke forudset finanskrisen i den form, den fik med kulminationen ved Lehmann Brothers konkurs den 15. september 2008. Det er en skbne, vi deler med de fleste finansielle aktrer verden over. Vi har vret vidne til den strste finansielle og konomisk krise i 60 r. Vi har fet demonstreret, at det usandsynlige kan ske. At vi ikke var alene om den manglende forudseenhed ses af den kendsgerning, at der er ivrksat et verdensomspndende arbejde, der skal ruste den finansielle sektor mod lignende fremtidige hndelser. Vi har i dag strre fokus p risici, som tillgges lille sandsynlighed  men store konsekvenser, hvis de indtrffer. Det er fx rsagen til at Nationalbanken har udtrykt betnkelighed ved refinansieringsrisikoen ved de meget omfattende fleksln, som i 2009 belb sig til omkring 550 mia. kr. Danske pengeinstitutter havde ikke i faretruende omfang investeret i subprime ln. Derimod havde de gjort sig srbare over for den situation den finansielle krise skabte  nemlig fastfrysningen af pengemarkederne og nedlukningen af kapitalmarkederne. Med store indlnsunderskud var pengeinstitutterne ndt til lbende at rejse nye ln til finansiering af allerede givne udln. Denne model kom i svre vanskeligheder i efterret 2008. Det var en situation Nationalbanken flere gange de foregende r havde advaret imod. Man kan diskutere om vi advarede kraftigt nok  det skal jeg nok vende tilbage til  men advaret blev der. Som tingene udviklede sig efter Lehmann konkurs, var det vurderingen, at det kunne blive umuligt for bankerne at forny de ln, som finansierede store dele af deres aktiviteter. Det kunne udlse en ustyrbar krise. 5 Den risiko tog Bankpakke I som nvnt hnd om med en statsgaranti for alle indskud i og ln til banker. Med statsgarantien i ryggen  mod betaling til staten  kom der igen gang i bankernes lntagning. Hvad s med udlnsvksten og boligboblen  skulle vi ikke have grebet ind over for disse faresignaler? Vi har kunnet lse, at det sandelig var faresignaler, man forstod i Nationalbanken i tidligere tider. Jeg ved ikke, hvad man forestiller sig. Nationalbanken har i dag ingen instrumenter til at gribe ind over for en unsket udlnsvkst. De muligheder forsvandt med liberaliseringen af penge-, kapital- og valutamarkederne for mange r siden. De reguleringsformer, som blev anvendt dengang, var blevet mere og mere meningslse, som det er beskrevet i vrker udgivet med stift bind af Nationalbanken. Det lovmssige grundlag for Nationalbankens aftaler om kreditformidling blev ophvet i 1996 med udtrykkelig henvisning til, at pengepolitikken havde fet nyt indhold. De banker, som har mttet dreje nglen om, eller har vret tt ved det, er alle banker, som havde engageret sig for strkt i udvalgte dele af ejendomssektoren. Det er et tilsynsanliggende. Og Finanstilsynet har frst nu fet en bredere hjemmel til at gribe ind. Lad mig s tilfje, at den danske banksektors samlede tab p udln og garantier indtil nu har vret mindre end under den nordiske bankkrise i begyndelsen af 90'erne. Man kan sige, at de lavere tab denne gang skyldes de statslige redningspakker, men staten har faktisk taget sig godt betalt for den risiko, den har lbet med bankpakkerne. Bankpakke II fra vinteren 2009 blev gennemfrt da den finansielle krise havde udlst en konomisk krise. Med udsigt til voksende tab p udln og forventninger om fremtidige strre krav til bankernes kapital, var bekymringen at bankerne ville blive s tilbageholdende med udln, at vi i Danmark ville kunne komme til at st over for en egentlig kreditklemme, som ville forstrke den konomiske nedtur. P den baggrund blev der indfrt en ordning, hvorefter solvente pengeinstitutter kunne f et statsligt kapitalindskud mod markedsmssigt afkast. Det centrale konomisk-politiske instrument til at dmpe en hjkonjunktur i Danmark er finanspolitikken. Da der i 2004 blev givet skattelettelser udtalte Nationalbanken, at skattelettelserne kun var forsvarlige, hvis der var vilje til at foretage modsvarende stramninger senere hen, nr konjunktursituationen krvede det. I 2006 foreslog Nationalbanken, at finanspolitikken blev strammet. Og gentog det senere. Det var ikke et rd, regeringen fulgte. Der var heller ingen sttte fra oppositionen. Og da jeg i 2006 foreslog en stramning af realkreditinstitutternes lnegrnser: Begrnset politisk respons! Da jeg i forret 2008 inden finanskrisen kulminerede talte for, at man lod konjunkturafmatningen sl igennem p arbejdslsheden, blev der hjlydt taget afstand fra denne tanke fra begge 6 sider af det politiske spektrum p trods af, at arbejdslsheden p dette tidspunkt var under 2 pct., og der var akut mangel p arbejdskraft med det resultat, at de danske lnninger steg langt hurtigere end de udenlandske. Jeg har selv tidligere givet udtryk for, at Nationalbanken nok burde have advaret mere hjlydt over for den finansielle og konomiske udvikling under hjkonjunkturen. Desvrre tror jeg ikke, det ville have gjort den store forskel. Sdan fungerer dansk politik ikke. Det ville have stillet Nationalbanken bedre over for kritik. Men det kan ikke vre afgrende. Det er en vurderingssag om skarpere formulerede opfordringer ville have haft en effekt. Men erfaringen taler ikke for det. nsker man at give Nationalbanken et strre ansvar for konjunkturudviklingen, m man ogs give os nogle relevante instrumenter til at gribe ind. Ellers giver det ingen mening.

Title: Speech to the Danish Construction Conference on Productivity
text: Construction productivity  why is the focus on it? Nils Bernstein's speech at the Danish Construction Conference on Productivity on 12 May 2011 DANMARKS NATIONALBANK THE SPOKEN WORD APPLIES Thank you for the invitation to speak here today In my post, I will focus on the role of construction in the Danish economy, including looking at the development in productivity in the sector. The Danish economy has been through a turbulent period. From 2004 to 2007, we experienced a strong boom with labour shortages, strong wage increases and an erosion of wage competitiveness. The slowdown set in towards the end of 2007 and was compounded by the international financial crisis. Since the spring of 2009, the economy has been growing again, with a break in the fourth quarter of last year, which we expect to be a lone swallow (Figure 2  GDP). As the poster illustrates, there is still a long way to go before production is back to the level immediately prior to the crisis. In our latest forecast, we expect the economy to grow in the order of 2% this year and the next few years. One of the areas where cyclical swings are most strongly expressed is the housing market. This was also the case this time (planche 3  housing investment). When house prices rise in relation to construction costs, as was the case during the boom, it draws with it increased housing investment  it becomes cheaper to build new instead of buying an existing home. In fact, housing investment rose to a level not seen since the early '70s. This represented an overheating of the sector and was not a sustainable level of activity. The rise in house prices during the boom is largely due to new forms of borrowing, tax breaks and a low interest rate. In addition to the fact that higher house prices draw larger investments with them, the higher property prices also imply that homeowners get more home value, and thus experience that they get a greater wealth. This often draws more private consumption with it, thus contributing to increasing demand in the economy. Also contributing to the overheating was a so-called cyclical fiscal policy (planche 4  fiscal policy). Normally, fiscal policy is countercyclical in the sense that it dampens activity when society's output is above the sustainable ka- 2 pacity level. And on the other hand, it stimulates the production of society when there is untapped capacity in the economy. That is, the task of fiscal policy is, among other things, to dampen the cyclical swings. However, this did not happen during the boom of 2005 to 2007, when public finances reinforced the cyclical recovery. It wasn't appropriate. Most people can see that today. At the time of this, there was little support for the view. Cyclical fluctuations are particularly the housing market because the supply side, i.e. the housing stock, cannot be quickly adapted to changes in demand. This is true both in an upward and downward direction. Danmarks Nationalbank has recently proposed some measures that could dampen the construction cycle. We have made two proposals. On the one hand, a gradual phasing out of the interest-only loans and, on the other hand, a reintroduction of the principle that the property value tax must follow the development of cash prices. These two measures can help prevent us from overheating again or, conversely, the collapse of the housing market altogether. The latter is also important. The purpose of the proposals is not to weaken the housing market, on the contrary. The property value tax is initially proposed to be maintained at the current level, but made dependent on cash prices. This means that if house prices fall, the property value tax is eased compared to today, thus helping to stabilize the market. Conversely, if prices rise. Abolishing the interest-only loans for new borrowers provides a corresponding stabilizing mechanism. If you count on it, these two proposals turn out to have a significant counter-cyclical effect (Planche 5  cyclical dampening). The blue bars on the plank show actual GDP growth, while the yellow bars show the growth that would have been had the two proposals been implemented. Perhaps the difference between the two pillars doesn't look great. However, if the same moderation were to be achieved through fiscal policy, even very large interventions would have to be made. *** Then let's look at how things stand with the development in productivity at home, including in construction. The growth in hourly productivity, i.e. how much value creation per hour worked grows per year, has decreased significantly in Denmark since the 1960s. Every decade there has been a decrease compared to the previous one (Planche 6  productivity long series). In particular, it is the growth of the so-called "Total Factor Productivity" that has decreased, i.e. the productivity increase that typically occurs in an economy in addition to the growth resulting from increased efforts of capital resources, investment and increased quality of labor, i.e. better education. Total factor productivity depends, among other things, on technical progress, improved workflows and logistics, etc. Declining productivity growth over the past decades is a general phenomenon in almost all developed industrial countries, but the decline at home has been 3 particularly large (Planche 7  productivity international comparison). In fact, the development since the mid-1990s is very significant. And that's true no matter what parts of the economy we look at, at least in industry. The crisis meant a cyclical dip in productivity, but industry in particular quickly got back on track (Planche 8  prod. industry). If we measure the overall economy, the dip was larger, but here too we have seen a significant recovery, although without the economy being completely back on its trend (Planche 9  prod. the entire economy). If, however, we look at the construction sector, it looks miserable  to speak in plain language. In fact, over the past twenty years, the productivity trend has been negative (Planche 10  prod. construction). This result is partially dependent on the choice of starting point, since the series is very unstable. This is hourly productivity, i.e. the evolution of value added in real terms per hour worked. Criticism of productivity developments as measured by national accounts figures can always be directed. There are measurement problems, composition effects, etc. However, the development is so significant and persistent over time that it cannot simply be dismissed with data problems. That there is a problem, there is no doubt (Planche 11  prod. in selected professions). I guess that's also the reason why a conference like this is being held. *** Why is weak productivity development in construction a societal problem? A number of conditions can be mentioned here. Basically, it's about the prosperity of society. It can be increased through three channels (Planche 12  Prosperity Channels). 1) through growth in hourly productivity, i.e. getting more out of the labor resources that are put in. 2) through an increased work effort 3) through an improved exchange relationship with foreign countries. It is less relevant for construction, as exports from the sector are limited. Looking at the period from the mid-1990s until the crisis set in, a large part of the increase in wealth in society has been due to productivity growth (Planche 13  GDP per capita). Here we look at the economy as a start, and not particularly at the construction. In the future, productivity growth will be even more important if we are to continue to experience increasing prosperity, as population trends mean that the growth in the labour force will be less than we have been used to, perhaps even negatively  fewer people have to support more people. We therefore have an additional obligation to use societal resources as best as possible. Construction is also important in understanding why the economy is subject to business cycles. 4 The construction acts a bit like a valve for the economy. During a boom, activity and employment in construction typically react more strongly than in the economy in general, and the lower the productivity growth, the faster capacity problems become. It increases inflationary pressures in the economy. During boom periods, labour flows into the construction sector from other sectors, so labour shortages are spreading. During the recent boom, there was a very strong increase in construction employment in a very short period of time (Planche 14  construction employment in the long run). This happened at the same time as other sectors also lacked manpower. This is reflected in the development of unemployment. The recorded unemployment rate, now called net unemployment, bottomed out at 46,000 in 2008, or less than 2 percent of the labor force. Unemployment in construction had already been at that level for several years (Planche 15  unemployment). Such a low unemployment rate is significantly below the level compatible with the balance of the economy  the structural level. We estimate this level to be not below 100,000 when measured on net unemployment. During the crisis, unemployment in construction has increased massively. It largely reflects the additional labor that entered the profession during the boom. It is not realistic that all the laid-off employees will again get work in construction. There is simply a need to get some people out of the profession. It may sound harsh, but there's no way around it. It's no use going and waiting for the situation as it looked during the boom to return again. During the boom, the low unemployment rate and the pressure on the labour market translated into the rates of wage growth, which came up around 5% p.a., when things were going strongest (Planche 16  wage increase rates). This was high both in relation to the underlying productivity development and in relation to our foreign competitors. As the plank shows, fluctuations in wage growth rates are particularly strong in the construction sector. This reflects the fact that cyclical fluctuations are showing themselves strongest in the construction sector. Flexible wage formation is in itself positive. But construction during the boom is pushing up wages in other more competitive sectors where there is a higher degree of wage stiffness downwards. In doing so, it takes longer and requires a higher unemployment rate, before high wage increases during an overheating are again squeezed out of the economy. Danish wage competitiveness has weakened significantly over the past fifteen years (Planche 17  competitiveness). The weakening in the so-called unit labour costs for industry was mainly in the period preceding the boom. This reflects the fact that, unlike the construction sector, productivity in the industry has been good in recent years. When we use industry figures in our competitiveness targets, it is because this sector is the most competitive. Construction is more of a domestic industry, but the development of the sector has a knock-on effect on other professions, especially through wage formation. 5 Over the past twenty years, construction employment has moved around a level of about 160,000 (Plance 18  construction employment short course). The sector accounts for about 5 per cent of the value creation in the economy. As in industry, there has not been a trend decline in construction employment. It has stayed around a fixed level, but with large fluctuations. Employment in construction at the moment is not particularly low from a historical perspective. The decisive factor in economic policy should be the creation of wealth in general in society, and not to ensure high employment in specific sectors. The challenge is therefore to make use of the surplus of resources, including the unemployed, that are currently in construction, in other sectors of the economy. This transformation is made more difficult by the fact that the Danish wage increases for a long period have been higher than those of our competitors, whereby the Danish wage level has risen very high (Planche 19  salary levels). Here are shown wage levels in the industry, as this is most relevant in a competitive context, but also because we have the best statistics here. But I don't think I'm making any big mistake in assuming that the situation is the same in the construction sector. When is a salary too high? To answer that question, wages must be compared with productivity. If productivity increases, there is also a basis for higher wages. However, if there is not enough productivity behind a wage, it will result in higher prices, to the detriment of construction customers and competitiveness in general via wage contagion. Thus, there is no argument that the construction sector is only to a lesser extent exposed to foreign competition on the sales side. A salary that does not have a background in productivity is a problem also in professions that predominantly produce for the domestic market. At the same time, a mismatch between productivity and wage levels makes it easier for foreign workers to enter the Danish market. If Danish labour were more productive, the risk of being undercut by labour from outside would be less. *** Finally, let me sum up. Why is low growth in productivity in construction a societal problem? (Planche 20  Conclusions): First, low productivity growth inhibits the development of society's prosperity. Societal resources should be used in the sectors that create wealth the most. That's where productivity is highest. Second: The capacity limit is reached faster by increasing demand. It gives wage pressure. Low productivity growth and high wage growth produce inflation. Third, during booms, construction typically attracts labor from other sectors. That causes the pressure in the economy to spread. It's 6 Subsequently, it is difficult to get the excessive labour resources out of the construction again when a more normal situation needs to be restored. Fourth, one result of all this is that construction amplifies fluctuations in the economy. Fluctuations are in themselves inappropriate in relation to a more calm development, as there are stiffnesses in the economy and thus adjustment costs when cornering  cf. that we first bring labour into a sector, which then subsequently has to go out again. It's welfare-degrading. Fifth, low growth in productivity in construction makes it less appropriate to increase demand for the sector's production, for example through public investment. Growth in wealth rests, as I said, on the fact that resources go into those sectors that have high value creation per hour worked. Finally, sixth: Low productivity and high wages make construction workers more vulnerable to being outcompeted by foreign labour. I have deliberately bypassed the question of how we increase productivity in construction. I'm not the right person to answer that. I hope that some of those present with greater sector knowledge have some suggestions for that. Thank you very much for the attention.
