Nils Bernsteins tale til Dansk Byggeris konference om produktivitet 12. maj 2011 DANMARKS NATIONALBANK DET TALTE ORD GLDER Tak for indbydelsen til at tale her i dag Jeg vil i mit indlg fokusere p byggeriets rolle i dansk konomi, og herunder se p udviklingen i produktiviteten i sektoren. Dansk konomi har vret igennem en turbulent periode. Fra 2004 til 2007 gennemlb vi en strk hjkonjunktur med arbejdskraftmangel, strke lnstigninger og udhuling af lnkonkurrenceevnen. Afmatningen satte ind mod slutningen af 2007 og blev forstrket af den internationale finanskrise. Siden forret 2009 har der atter vret vkst i konomien, med et afbrk i 4. kvartal sidste r, som vi dog regner med var en enlig svale (Figur 2  BNP). Som planchen illustrerer, er der endnu et godt stykke vej fr produktionen er tilbage p niveauet umiddelbart forud for krisen. Vi forventer i vor seneste prognose, at konomien vil vokse i strrelsesordenen 2 pct. i r og de nste par r. Et af de omrder, hvor konjunktursving kommer strkest til udtryk, er boligmarkedet. Det var ogs tilfldet denne gang (planche 3  boliginvesteringer). Nr boligpriserne stiger i forhold til byggeomkostningerne, som det var tilfldet under hjkonjunkturen, trkker det gede boliginvesteringer med sig  det bliver billigere at bygge nyt i stedet for at kbe en eksisterende bolig. Faktisk steg boliginvesteringerne til et niveau, der ikke er set siden begyndelsen af 70'erne. Det var udtryk for en overophedning af sektoren og var ikke et holdbart aktivitetsniveau. Stigningen i boligpriserne under hjkonjunkturen skyldes i hj grad nye lneformer, skattestop og en lav rente. Udover at hjere boligpriser trkker strre investeringer med sig, indebrer de hjere ejendomspriser ogs, at boligejerne fr mere frivrdi, og dermed oplever, at de fr en strre formue. Det trkker ofte mere privatforbrug med sig og bidrager dermed til at ge eftersprgslen i konomien. Medvirkende til overophedningen var ogs en skaldt konjunkturmedlbende finanspolitik (planche 4  finanspolitik). Normalt er finanspolitikken konjunkturudjvnende i den forstand, at den dmper aktiviteten, nr samfundets produktion ligger over det holdbare ka- 2 pacitetsniveau. Og p den anden side stimulerer samfundets produktion, nr der er uudnyttet kapacitet i konomien. Dvs. finanspolitikkens opgave er bl.a. at dmpe konjunktursvingene. Det skete imidlertid ikke under hjkonjunkturen i 2005 til 2007, hvor de offentlige finanser forstrkede konjunkturopsvinget. Det var ikke hensigtsmssigt. Det kan de fleste godt se i dag. Dengang det foregik, var der ikke megen tilslutning til synspunktet. Konjunkturudsving slr srlig hrdt ud p boligmarkedet, fordi udbudssiden, dvs. boligmassen, ikke hurtigt kan tilpasses ndringer i eftersprgslen. Det glder bde i opadgende og nedadgende retning. Nationalbanken har for nylig foreslet nogle tiltag, som vil kunne dmpe byggekonjunkturen. Vi har stillet to forslag. Dels en gradvis udfasning af de afdragsfrie ln og dels en genindfrelse af princippet om, at ejendomsvrdiskatten skal flge udviklingen i kontantpriserne. Disse to tiltag kan bidrage til at forebygge, at vi igen fr overophedning eller omvendt, at boligmarkedet falder helt sammen. Det sidste er ogs vigtigt. Formlet med forslagene er ikke at svkke boligmarkedet, tvrtimod. Ejendomsvrdiskatten foresls i udgangspunktet fastholdt p det nuvrende niveau, men gres afhngig af kontantpriserne. Det betyder, at falder huspriserne, s lettes ejendomsvrdiskatten i forhold til i dag og hjlper dermed til at stabilisere markedet. Omvendt hvis priserne stiger. Afskaffelse af de afdragsfrie ln for nye lntagere giver en tilsvarende stabiliserende mekanisme. Regner man p det, viser disse to forslag sig at have en vsentlig konjunkturdmpende effekt (Planche 5  konjunkturdmpning). De bl sjler p planchen viser den faktiske BNP-vkst, mens de gule sjler viser den vkst, der ville have vret, hvis de to forslag havde vret gennemfrt. Mske ser forskellen p de to sjler ikke stor ud. Skulle den samme afdmpning imidlertid ns gennem finanspolitikken, ville der skulle endog meget store indgreb til. *** Lad os s se p, hvordan det str til med udviklingen i produktiviteten herhjemme, herunder i byggeriet. Vksten i timeproduktiviteten, dvs. hvor meget vrdiskabelsen pr. prsteret arbejdstime vokser om ret, er faldet markant herhjemme siden 1960'erne. Hvert rti har der vret et fald i forhold til det forudgende (Planche 6  produktivitet lang serie). Det er isr vksten i den skaldte "Totalfaktorproduktivitet", der er faldet, dvs. den produktivitetsstigning, der typisk er i en konomi udover den vkst, der flger af get indsats af kapitalresurser, investeringer og get kvalitet af arbejdskraften, dvs. bedre uddannelse. Totalfaktorproduktiviteten afhnger bl.a. af tekniske fremskridt, forbedrede arbejdsgange og logistik m.m. Faldende produktivitetsvkst gennem de seneste rtier er et generelt fnomen i nsten alle udviklede industrilande, men faldet har herhjemme vret 3 srligt stort (Planche 7  produktivitet international sammenligning). Faktisk er udviklingen siden midten af 1990'erne meget markant. Og det glder uanset hvilke dele af konomien, vi ser p, dog mindst inden for industrien. Krisen betd et konjunkturbetinget dyk i produktiviteten, men isr industrien kom hurtigt tilbage p sporet (Planche 8  prod. industri). Mler vi p den samlede konomi, var dykket strre, men ogs her har vi set en markant genopretning, dog uden at konomien helt er tilbage p sin trend (Planche 9  prod. hele konomien). Ser vi imidlertid p bygge- og anlgssektoren, ser det jammerligt ud  for nu at tale i klart sprog. Faktisk har produktivitetstrenden over de seneste tyve r vret negativ (Planche 10  prod. byggeri). Dette resultat er delvist afhngigt af valg af udgangspunkt, da serien er meget ustabil. Der er tale om timeproduktivitet, dvs. udviklingen i vrditilvkst i faste priser pr. prsteret arbejdstime. Der kan altid rettes kritik af produktivitetsudviklinger mlt ud fra nationalregnskabstal. Der er mleproblemer, sammenstningseffekter osv. Udviklingen er imidlertid s markant og vedvarende over tid, at den ikke blot kan affrdiges med dataproblemer. At der er et problem, er der ingen tvivl om (Planche 11  prod. i udvalgte erhverv). Det er vel ogs baggrunden for, at der holdes en konference som denne. *** Hvorfor er en svag produktivitetsudvikling i byggeriet et samfundsmssigt problem? Her kan der nvnes en rkke forhold. Helt grundlggende handler det jo om samfundets velstand. Den kan ges gennem tre kanaler (Planche 12  velstandskanaler). 1) gennem vkst i timeproduktivitet, dvs. at f mere ud af de arbejdskraftresurser, der sttes ind. 2) gennem en get arbejdsindsats 3) gennem et forbedret bytteforhold over for udlandet. Det er mindre relevant for byggeriet, da eksporten fra sektoren er begrnset. Ser vi p perioden fra midten af 1990'erne til krisen satte ind, har en stor del af velstandsstigningen i samfundet haft baggrund i vkst i produktivitet (Planche 13  BNP pr. capita). Her ses p konomien under et og ikke specielt p byggeriet. Fremover bliver vkst i produktivitet endnu vigtigere, hvis vi fortsat skal opleve stigende velstand, da befolkningsudviklingen gr, at vksten i arbejdsstyrken bliver mindre end vi har vret vant til, mske endda negativ  frre skal forsrge flere. Vi har derfor en ekstra forpligtelse til at anvende de samfundsmssige resurser s godt som muligt. Byggeriet er endvidere vigtigt i forstelsen af, hvorfor konomien er underkastet konjunkturer. 4 Byggeriet fungerer lidt som en ventil for konomien. Under en hjkonjunktur reagerer aktiviteten og beskftigelsen i byggeriet typisk kraftigere end i konomien i vrigt og des lavere vksten i produktiviteten er, des hurtigere bliver der kapacitetsproblemer. Det ger inflationspresset i konomien. I opgangsperioder strmmer der arbejdskraft over i byggesektoren fra andre sektorer, s mangel p arbejdskraft spreder sig. Under den seneste hjkonjunktur skete der en meget strk stigning i byggebeskftigelsen i lbet af meget kort tid (Planche 14  byggebeskftigelsen i langt forlb). Det skete samtidig med, at andre sektorer ogs manglende arbejdskraft. Det afspejler sig i ledighedsudviklingen. Den registrerede ledighed, nu kaldet nettoledighed, bundede i 2008 p 46.000, svarende til under 2 pct. af arbejdsstyrken. Ledigheden i byggeriet havde allerede da ligget p det niveau i flere r (Planche 15  ledighed). En s lav ledighed er markant under det niveau, der er foreneligt med balance i konomien  det strukturelle niveau. Vi anslr dette niveau til at vre ikke under 100.000, nr der mles p nettoledigheden. Under krisen er ledigheden i byggeriet steget massivt. Det afspejler i hj grad den ekstra arbejdskraft, der kom ind i erhvervet under hjkonjunkturen. Det er ikke realistisk, at alle de afskedigede medarbejdere igen fr arbejde inden for byggeriet. Der er simpelthen behov for at f nogle folk ud af erhvervet. Det kan lyde hrdt, men der er ikke nogen vej uden om. Det nytter ikke at g og vente p, at situationen, som den s ud under hjkonjunkturen, vender tilbage igen. Den lave ledighed og presset p arbejdsmarkedet gav sig under opsvinget udslag i lnstigningstakterne, der kom op omkring 5 pct. p.a., da det gik strkest (Planche 16  lnstigningstakter). Det var hjt bde i forhold til den underliggende produktivitetsudvikling og i forhold til vore udenlandske konkurrenter. Som planchen viser, er udsvingene i lnstigningstakter srligt strke i bygge- og anlgssektoren. Det afspejler, at konjunkturudsvingene viser sig strkest i bygge- og anlgssektoren. En fleksibel lndannelse er i sig selv positivt. Men byggeriet under hjkonjunkturen er med til at presse lnningerne op i andre mere konkurrenceudsatte sektorer, hvor der er en hjere grad af lnstivhed nedad til. Derved tager det lngere tid og krver en hjere ledighed, inden for hje lnstigninger under en overophedning igen er presset ud af konomien. Den danske lnkonkurrenceevne er svkket markant over de seneste femten r (Planche 17  konkurrenceevne). Svkkelsen i de skaldte enhedslnomkostninger for industrien l hovedsagelig i perioden forud for hjkonjunkturen. Det afspejler, at produktiviteten i industrien i modstning til bygge- og anlgssektoren de seneste r har vret god. Nr vi anvender tal for industrien i vore konkurrenceevneml, er det fordi, denne sektor er den mest konkurrenceudsatte. Byggeriet er i hjere grad et hjemmemarkedserhverv, men udviklingen i sektoren har en afsmittende effekt p andre erhverv, isr via lndannelsen. 5 Set over de seneste tyve r har byggebeskftigelsen bevget sig omkring et niveau p ca. 160.000 (Plance 18  byggebeskftigelsen kort forlb). Sektoren str for ca. 5 pct. af vrdiskabelsen i konomien. Der har ikke som i industrien vret tale om et trendmssigt fald i byggebeskftigelsen. Den har holdt sig omkring et fast niveau, men med store udsving. Beskftigelsen i byggeriet for jeblikket er ikke specielt lav i historisk perspektiv. Det afgrende i den konomiske politik br vre velstandsskabelsen generelt i samfundet, og ikke at sikre en hj beskftigelse i bestemte sektorer. Udfordringen er derfor at f nyttiggjort det overskud af resurser, herunder arbejdslse, der i dag befinder sig inden for byggeriet, i andre sektorer af konomien. Denne transformation vanskeliggres af, at de danske lnstigninger i en lang periode har ligget hjere end hos vore konkurrenter, hvorved det danske lnniveau er komme meget hjt op (Planche 19  lnniveauer). Her er vist lnniveauer i industrien, da dette er mest relevant i en konkurrencesammenhng, men ogs fordi vi her har den bedste statistik. Men jeg tror ikke jeg begr nogen stor fejl ved at antage, at situationen er den samme inden for bygge- og anlgssektoren. Hvornr er en ln for hj? For at besvare det sprgsml m lnnen sammenholdes med produktiviteten. ges produktiviteten, er der ogs basis for hjere lnninger. Er der imidlertid ikke tilstrkkelig produktivitet bag en ln, slr det ud i hjere priser, til skade for byggeriets kunder og konkurrenceevnen generelt via lnafsmitning. Det er sledes ikke noget argument, at bygge- og anlgssektoren kun i mindre grad er udsat for udenlandsk konkurrence p afstningssiden. En ln, der ikke har baggrund i produktivitet, er et problem ogs i erhverv, der overvejende producerer til hjemmemarkedet. Et misforhold mellem produktivitet og lnniveau gr det samtidigt lettere for udenlandsk arbejdskraft at komme ind p det danske marked. Hvis dansk arbejdskraft var mere produktiv, ville risikoen for at blive underbudt af arbejdskraft ude fra vre mindre. *** Lad mig til sidst summe op. Hvorfor er lav vkst i produktiviteten i byggeriet et samfundsmssigt problem? (Planche 20  konklusioner): For det frste: Lav produktivitetsvkst hmmer udviklingen i samfundets velstand. De samfundsmssige resurser br anvendes i de sektorer, som er mest velstandsskabende. Det er der, hvor produktiviteten er hjest. For det andet: Kapacitetsgrnsen ns hurtigere ved stigende eftersprgsel. Det giver lnpres. Lav vkst i produktivitet og hj vkst i lnninger giver inflation. For det tredje: Under hjkonjunkturer tiltrkker byggeriet typisk arbejdskraft fra andre sektorer. Det fr presset i konomien til at sprede sig. Det er 6 efterflgende svrt at f de for store arbejdskraftresurser ud af byggeriet igen, nr en mere normal situation skal genetableres. For det fjerde: Et resultat af alt dette er, at byggeriet forstrker udsvingene i konomien. Udsving er i sig selv uhensigtsmssige set i forhold til en mere rolig udvikling, da der er stivheder i konomien og dermed tilpasningsomkostninger ved sving  jf. at vi frst henter arbejdskraft ind i en sektor, som s efterflgende skal ud igen. Det er velfrdsforringende. For det femte: Lav vkst i produktiviteten i byggeriet gr det mindre hensigtsmssigt at ge eftersprgslen efter sektorens produktion fx via offentlige investeringer. Vkst i velstand hviler som sagt p, at resurserne gr over i de sektorer, som har hj vrdiskabelse pr. arbejdstime. Endelig for det sjette: Lav produktivitet og hj ln gr alt andet lige arbejdskraften i byggeriet mere srbar over for at blive udkonkurreret af udenlandsk arbejdskraft. *** Jeg er bevidst get uden om sprgsmlet om, hvordan vi ger produktiviteten i byggeriet. Det er jeg ikke den rette til at svare p. Det hber jeg, at nogle af de tilstedevrende med strre sektorkendskab har nogle bud p. Mange tak for opmrksomheden.

Title: Speech at Brsen Executive Club
text: Governor Nils Bernstein's speech at Borsen Executive Club The spoken word applies. Thank you for the invitation to speak here today. I will begin by addressing the question of whether, in the light of the sovereign debt problems in some euro area countries, we should welcome the fact that we are not in the euro. Next, I will give Danmarks Nationalbank's view on the current economic situation. Let me start by stating that the fixed exchange rate policy, which has now for almost 30 years been one of the cornerstones of economic policy at home, has served Denmark well. Inflation and interest rates are in line with the best countries in the euro area, and the recovery in our prosperity has been, when adjusted appropriately, on a par with the countries we normally compare ourselves to. The problems the Danish economy has with deteriorating competitiveness and an excessive budget deficit are largely a result of our own actions and cannot be blamed solely on the grounds of future conditions. The prerequisite for the fixed exchange rate policy is, of course, that there is a credible anchor to attach the krone exchange rate to. It is therefore very much in Denmark's interest that the euro remains such an anchor. And I think it will continue to be. A little squarely put, it is not the euro that is currently in crisis. Some euro area countries are having problems. Assessed on the point of view of relevant parameters such as exchange rate against other main currencies and inflation, it can be determined that the euro is a success. The stabilising function of the euro was evident, among other things, during the recent global recession. In earlier times, such situations typically gave rise to competing devaluations, with countries seeking to pass the buck on to their neighbours. The high level of public indebtedness we see in a number of euro area countries is not the result of the introduction of the euro and only to a lesser extent of the financial crisis. It has been created over the last few decades, with some countries failing to consolidate in good times, thereby allowing debt to grow. Such a policy would create problems, both inside and outside the single currency. But market reactions may come faster for countries outside the coin. The fixed exchange rate policy has given Denmark many of the benefits that a full membership would provide, but not all. The problem with standing outside is partly Page 1 of 8 economic, partly political. Especially the last aspect becomes ever greater as time goes on. I have argued on previous occasions that membership of the euro will result in a slightly lower interest rate in Denmark in calm times, increase foreign trade and lower the transaction costs of foreign trade. If we do the thought experiment of the euro disappearing, which I consider unlikely, there would, in my opinion, be pressure on the single market. Wouldn't we end up in a situation where each country would seek to nurture its own narrow interests? And if there is anything that we, as a small open country that is completely dependent on trade with the outside world, must protect, it is the free movement of goods across borders. Over the longer term, if Denmark joined the euro, growth will be positively affected - the GDP level can be expected to increase by 1/2-1 per cent. The most tangible benefit of a euro membership will be seen during periods of currency turmoil, as we last saw in 2008 in the wake of the Lehman Brothers bankruptcy. Crown crises will be a thing of the past in euro membership. Politically, the problem is that in practice we are getting further and further away from the discussions in the for a where EU policy, rules and positions in a wide range of areas of interest are also defined for us. Of course, this applies first and foremost to the setting of the policy rate and access to the ECB's facilities. But to this is added the lack of information flows. Examples of this were the process of covered bonds and, most recently, the issue of the use of mortgage bonds in banks' liquidity preparedness. These are areas of vital importance to Denmark, and where the Danish rules and institutions also differ from the conditions in other EU countries. There is therefore a great need to explain and defend the Danish rules in the relevant areas. The lack of presence in the central for a greatly complicates the Danish negotiating position. All in all, therefore, there is absolutely no reason why we should be happy to be outside the euro. On the contrary, we have the utmost interest in the euro remaining a stable and credible factor in European economic policy. I think it will continue to be, too. Don't get me wrong! I am not proposing that a referendum be called now on Danish participation in the euro. By all accounts, such a vote would elicit a resounding no. A new vote, in my view, should not take place until the day we are confident that there will be a majority in favour of support. A new no vote will postpone any connection for more than 10 years. Page 2 of 8 *** I will now turn to the current economic situation and the outlook for the near future. The recovery of the world economy has slowed down in the past part of the year, after a period of decent growth in the first half of the year. However, the growth picture is very different when we compare the rich and middle-income countries. The slowdown has occurred especially in advanced economies. Financial market turmoil over the summer and the continued uncertainty surrounding the debt situation in a number of euro area countries have led to a noticeable downward revision of growth expectations. Recent developments are a reminder that the road back from a recession combined with a banking crisis takes time and can be expected to be bumpy. Most advanced economies, but probably especially parts of the euro area, therefore have a protracted trajectory ahead of them before the closing of the output gap and a normalisation of the labour market situation can be expected. Growth prospects must also be assessed in the light of slight progress in growth potential, including as a result of slowing inflows or direct declines in the population of the age groups from which the workforce is primarily recruited. If nothing else happens, the number of hours worked will decrease. In addition, growth and capacity utilisation in a number of countries, including Denmark, were unsustainably high in the years leading up to the crisis. And it is neither to be expected nor desirable to return to such a situation. It is therefore important that we do not use the level of unemployment and employment during the boom as measuring our level of ambition for labour market developments. Over the summer, risk aversion has increased among investors, who have largely gone out of stocks and into bonds. This has led to significant declines in stock prices in many places and resulted in lower bond yields in countries not affected by debt problems. The continued uncertainty surrounding the debt situation in southern Europe has also been shown in deteriorating conditions in euro area money markets. There is an widening gap between unsecured and secured money market rates, and the ECB has large deposits as well as lending. Banks are making increased use of marginal facilities. These are signs that the inter-bank market is operating sluggishly. Sluggishly functioning inter-bank markets bring to mind the situation in the wake of the Lehman Brothers bankruptcy in the fall of 2008, when markets froze completely. The challenge today is to prevent the debt crisis in a number of euro area countries from dragging on a European banking crisis. This is being worked hard to avoid both nationally in euro area countries and at EU level. Page 3 of 8 By virtue of our euro opt-out, Denmark can only watch from the sidelines. We must develop our own instruments. The direct exposure of Danish banks to the debt-ridden euro area countries is limited and manageable. The sector is therefore primarily affected indirectly when financing opportunities in international capital markets generally deteriorate. Danmarks Nationalbank's new loan scheme can also be seen in this context. The setback in the context of the 2008-09 financial crisis was countered in many countries with extensive demand stimulus programmes. To this was added the effect of the so-called automatic stabilizers. The result is large deficits in the public finances in a situation where debt levels in relation to the size of the economies are already high in many places. Possibilities to respond to the recent moderation with further fiscal stimulus to economies is thus severely limited. This is happening in a situation where the recovery in the wake of the financial crisis has not quite succeeded in making itself-bearing, i.e. driven by private consumption and investment. The situation is aggravated by the fact that both the United States and Europe call into question the willingness and ability of political systems to make the necessary adjustments. The process surrounding the raising of the US debt ceiling was not constructive. In the euro area, we still lack a convincing long-term plan on how to deal with the debt problems of southern European countries and Ireland. The latest addition is that the German Chancellor and the French President have put forward a plan in a month, i.e. before the plan adopted this summer has been implemented. It says something about the dynamics of the crisis. In Greece, debt problems are particularly high and both the political and administrative capacity to deal with the challenges has been weak, while in Portugal and ireland in particular it sees better. These three countries are all small economies that should be manageable in cooperation between Europe and the IMF. Only if the turmoil really hits countries like Italy and Spain will it get really serious. It is in the potential spread of the crisis the biggest uncertainty factor lies. In that light, the sharp downgrade of Italy's sovereign debt is worrisome. On the positive side, both Spain and Italy are far stronger economies than Greece, Ireland and Portugal. Where does this leave the prospects for the near future? Overall, the key figures point to a weakened recovery in the coming period, but there are factors that are pulling the other way. Short-term interest rates are extremely low and long-term interest rates have fallen over the summer, excluding the problem countries. In addition, there are high growth rates in increasingly important middle-income countries, as well as lower energy prices. Finally, both investment and consumption quotas are in Page 4 of 8 many countries below the historical average. Here is a significant growth potential. The planned fiscal consolidations seem cyclical in the very short term, but convincing plans for how to deal with the debt problem can, on the other hand, help to strengthen consumer and business confidence and thus boost the private sector of the economy. Much therefore depends on the political and implementing of a credible plan for how to contain the debt crisis in a number of euro area countries. *** I will now turn to the domestic economic situation. Since mid-2009 and up to and including the second quarter of 2011, the Danish economy has grown at an annual rate of around 1.5 per cent. However, the growth track has been very uneven. This underlines the importance of not interpreting too harshly on the national accounts figures for a single quarter, but seeing the development over a period of time. The international development has meant that we have had to downgrade our expectations for exports in the coming period. It cannot help but have an impact on growth and employment at home in the second half of the year and into 2012. We must therefore be prepared for a poor second half of the year, where we do not expect any progress. Further into the forecast period, growth is expected to pick up again. This should be seen in the light of the extremely low level of interest rates, a possible downward correction of the very high level of savings in both households and firms, and renewed recovery in export markets. In 2012 and 2013, we estimate growth of 1.6% in each of the years. This is slightly above the IMF's expectation for the euro area, which has been dragged down by countries hit by the debt crisis, and leads to a continued narrowing of the negative output gap at home. Obviously, if the world economy goes into a crisis like the one we saw in the wake of the Lehman Brothers bankruptcy in the fall of 2008, we too will be hit and our forecast will be too optimistic. If the debt crisis escalates out of control, we are in a different situation and heading into uncharted territory. But you are hardly much mistaken if you expect countries with strong state finances in this situation to do best. When the output gap can narrow despite the expectation of historically restrained economic growth, it is because the economy's potential is growing even smaller. The trend of potential production is determined by the development of hourly productivity and population. We have problems in both areas that I need to come back to. As in other advanced economies, we probably have to get used to a new "normal" when it comes to the rate at which the economy, and thus prosperity, is growing. I don't think we've quite adjusted to that. Page 5 of 8 Mentally. At the same time, it is important to emphasize that this is not something that can be changed with expansionary fiscal policy in the form of growth packages. The fundamental challenges are best ensured by a sustainable fiscal policy underpinned by structural reforms. In this connection, let me make a few comments on the status of the labour market. The Danish labour market is doing relatively well. Employment has remained largely unchanged since the beginning of 2010. Employment may have fallen by almost 160,000 since 2008, but as mentioned, this is a misleading starting point for the level of ambition. The employment peak in 2008 was the result of a sharp overheating of the economy and not a sustainable level. It is not appropriate to make the return to this peak an objective of economic policy. We estimate that there is room for an employment increase of almost 50,000 people from the current level. In addition, employment increases will require reforms to increase structural employment levels. I would also like to make a few comments on fiscal policy. At home, the expansionary effect emanating from the public finances in 2009-10 was among the largest in the EU when we see it in relation to the size of the economy. The effect was also largely from a historical perspective, and e.g. significantly greater than the kick-start in the early 1990s. This was possible due to the fact that we had a good starting point in the form of a relatively low public debt. However, it is crucial that such a policy is precisely temporary. The more measures, for example in the form of advancing public investment, that are made today, the greater the slowdown that must take place at a later stage. A tightening that may well have to be made in a situation where economic growth is still moderate. The key word is fiscal credibility. It hinges on the credibility of a credible plan to ensure the long-term sustainability of public finances. To gain credibility with investors, there must be delivered, not just when it comes to stimulating the economy, but also when it comes to tightening up. During the debt crisis, Denmark has benefited immensely from the fact that our policy has been seen as credible and Danish government securities as safe. It rubs off on the level of interest rates throughout the economy, including on mortgage bonds. It is a situation that we must do everything possible to safeguard and ensure continues in the future. If the credibility of economic policy is lost and interest rates start to rise, Denmark will be seriously affected. *** A country can become wealthy in several ways and in several ways. The safest, but perhaps also most cumbersome, is by working more. I.e., diligence. The more hours we perform, the greater the prosperity will be for a given Page 6 of 8 population size. An increased number of working hours can be done both by the fact that each individual works more or by a larger share of the population contributing to the labor market. In terms of hourly effort per head per year, we are low at home internationally, while we have a very high employment rate. If the surveys published by the press periodically can be trusted, the desire to work more hours is limited. Now, material prosperity is not just a matter of hourly effort, but also of how smartly and efficiently we work when we work. It's the hourly productivity. Here we are seriously lagging behind, as I have already mentioned. Growth in Danish productivity has been low for a number of years. In addition, the number of people in the age classes from which the workforce is predominantly recruited will decrease in the coming years. A greater use of foreign labour could change this, but first and foremost there is a need for reforms that increase the domestic labour supply by bringing people on public support into the labour market to a greater extent. The withdrawal and unemployment benefit reforms are examples of such measures. The Ministry of Finance estimates that these two reforms will transitionally increase the growth of the economy's potential by 1/2 percentage point from 2015. We may also be lucky. And we have been. In particular, Danish companies produce goods that can be sold at high prices on export markets, so-called "up-market" products. This has meant that Denmark has had an increasing exchange ratio since the mid-1990s. This contributes to the Danish consumption opportunities beyond what a simple growth in GDP in volumes shows. The calculation of GDP in volumes seeks precisely to clean out such price effects, but the price effects are relevant if we want to compare the development in danish consumption opportunities with those of other countries. Finally, the Danes as a nation have for a period been frugal in that part of the year's production has not been consumed, but has been invested abroad. This means that today we are entitled to a part of foreign production result in the form of wealth income from abroad. This contributes to the current account surplus and further increases Danish consumption opportunities beyond what GDP growth shows. If we look at the Danish GDP growth from 1995 to 2010, we are at the absolute low end in an OECD comparison. The Danish economy has only grown by an average of 1.4% per year over the past 15 years. This is significantly less than, for example, our Nordic neighbours. However, there has been a big difference in how much the population has changed. Denmark has had a relatively low population growth, and increased production, which is simply an expression of a larger population, does not increase consumption opportunities per head. There will just be more to spread this year's production result out on. Page 7 of 8 If this is taken into account and further corrected for terms of exchange and foreign property income, gross national income per head emerges. It is a more accurate measure of wealth development if comparisons are to be done internationally. In such a statement, Denmark does not do so badly. The development of prosperity in Denmark over the past 15 years has been stronger than in Germany and the United States and in line with Sweden and the Netherlands. That we have problems with hourly productivity, there is no doubt, and that efforts must be made to increase the supply of labour is also a given. But on the other hand, we shouldn't paint with an overly black brush either. Over the past 15 years, the Danish economy has performed well in an international comparison of the development of material wealth. Thanks for the attention. Page 8 of 8

Det tror jeg ikke, vi helt har indstillet os p rent Side 5 af 8 mentalt. Det er samtidig vigtig at understege, at det ikke er noget, der kan ndres med ekspansiv finanspolitik i form af vkstpakker. De grundlggende udfordringer sikres bedst gennem en holdbar finanspolitik understttet af strukturreformer. Lad mig i den forbindelse knytte et par kommentarer til status p arbejdsmarkedet. Beskftigelsesstigninger herudover vil krve reformer, der kan ge det strukturelle beskftigelsesniveau. Jeg vil ogs gerne knytte er par kommentarer til finanspolitikken. Herhjemme var den ekspansive effekt der udgik fra de offentlige finanser i 2009-10 blandt de strste i EU nr vi ser det i forhold til konomiens strrelse. Vel at mrke en opstramning som meget vel vil skulle foretages i en situation, hvor den konomiske vkst stadig er moderat. Ngleordet er finanspolitisk trovrdighed. For at opn trovrdighed hos investorerne skal der leveres, ikke bare nr det glder om at stimulere konomien, men nok s meget, nr der skal strammes op. Danmark har under gldskrisen haft en kolossal fordel af, at vores politik er blevet anset som trovrdig og danske statspapirer som sikre. Det smitter af p renteniveauet i hele konomien, inklusive p realkreditobligationerne. Det er en situation, som vi skal gre alt for at vrne om og sikre fortstter fremover. Hvis trovrdigheden om den konomiske politik mistes og renterne begynder at stige, vil Danmark for alvor blive ramt. *** Et land kan blive velhavende p flere mder og ad flere veje. Den sikreste, men mske ogs mest besvrlige, er ved at arbejde mere. Dvs. flid. Des flere timer vi prsterer, des strre vil velstanden alt andet blive for en given Side 6 af 8 befolkningsstrrelse. Et get antal arbejdstimer kan bde ske ved, at hver enkelt arbejder mere eller ved, at en strre andel af befolkningen bidrager p arbejdsmarkedet. Med hensyn til timeindsats pr. hoved pr. r ligger vi lavt herhjemme internationalt set, mens vi til gengld har en meget hj erhvervsfrekvens. Hvis man kan stole p de sprgeundersgelser, som pressen med mellemrum offentliggr, er nsket om at arbejde flere timer begrnset. Nu er den materielle velstand ikke bare et sprgsml om timeindsats, men ogs om hvor smart og effektivt vi arbejder, nr vi arbejder. Det er timeproduktiviteten. Her halter vi alvorligt bagefter, som jeg allerede har vret inde p. Vksten i den danske produktivitet har vret lav i en lngere rrkke. Hertil kommer, at antallet af personer i de aldersklasser, hvorfra arbejdsstyrken overvejende rekrutteres, vil falde de kommende r. Det vil en strre anvendelse af udenlandsk arbejdskraft et stykke hen ad vejen kunne ndre p, men frst og fremmest er der behov for reformer, der ger det indenlandske arbejdsudbud ved i hjere grad at f personer p offentlig forsrgelse ud p arbejdsmarkedet. Tilbagetrknings- og dagpengereformerne er eksempler p sdanne tiltag. Finansministeriet sknner, at disse to reformer overgangsvist vil ge vksten i konomiens potentiale med  procentpoint fra 2015. Vi kan ogs vre heldige. Og det har vi vret. Danske virksomheder producerer i srlig grad varer, som kan slges til hje priser p eksportmarkederne, skaldte "up-market" produkter. Det har betydet, at Danmark har haft et stigende bytteforhold siden midten af 1990'erne. Det bidrager til de danske forbrugsmuligheder ud over hvad en simpel vkst i BNP i mngder viser. Beregningen af BNP i mngder sger netop at rense sdanne priseffekter ud, men priseffekterne er relevante, hvis vi vil sammenligne udviklingen i de danske forbrugsmuligheder med udlandets. Endelig har danskerne som nation i en periode vret sparsommelige derved, at en del af rets produktion ikke er blevet forbrugt, men derimod er blevet investeret i udlandet. Det betyder, at vi i dag har krav p en del af udlandets produktionsresultat i form af formueindkomst fra udlandet. Det bidrager til overskuddet p betalingsbalancen og ger yderligere de danske forbrugsmuligheder ud over hvad vksten i BNP viser. Ser vi p den danske vkst i BNP fra 1995 til 2010 ligger vi i den absolut lave ende i en OECD-sammenligning. Dansk konomi er kun vokset med i gennemsnit 1,4 pct. pr. r over de seneste 15 r. Det er markant mindre end fx vore nordiske naboer. Der har imidlertid vret stor forskel p, hvor meget befolkningen er ndret sig. Danmark har haft en forholdsvis lav befolkningsvkst, og get produktion, der blot er udtryk for en strre befolkning ger ikke forbrugsmulighederne pr. hoved. Der bliver blot flere at sprede rets produktionsresultat ud p. Det er et mere retvisende ml for velstandsudviklingen, hvis der skal sammenlignes internationalt. I en sdan opgrelse klarer Danmark sig ikke s drligt. Title: Speech at the Danish Bankers Association's Directors' Conference 2011
text: Speech by Governor Nils Bernstein at the Danish Bankers Association's Directors' Conference 2011 The spoken word applies. Thank you for the invitation to speak here today. First, I want to say a little about the growth prospects internationally. Then something about how the development is shaping up in Denmark. And finally, I want to tell you about our preliminary considerations on the expansion of the loan options at Danmarks Nationalbank. The global business cycle has deteriorated in recent months. Weaker ratios and heightened financial uncertainty have meant a downward revision of the growth outlook for the near future. But the growth picture is very different when we compare the rich countries with the middle-income countries. China, India and a number of other middle-income countries continue to have impressive growth rates. Even Africa is prospering when we disregard the drought-stricken areas  and enormous growth potential. That's one of the good news of these times. On the other hand, progress is only slow in the rich part of the world - with a few exceptions. After a period of worldwide rapid progress, we must adjust to a period of more modest growth. After all, when things are moving forward, it is not least due to the market economy's built-in self-regulation after the downturn. Stocks need to be replenished, investments that have been postponed are intruding as a result of attrition and obsolescence, and consumer postponement of major purchases does not last. The development is supported by the fact that when this increased demand takes hold, employment rises again. Incomes are growing. This underlying healing of the economy remains effective. But there are holes in the road. The current cyclical recovery is hampered by the problems arising from the rapidly growing public debt. The handling of the European debt crisis, and fears of proliferation, create uncertainty about the sustainability of the nascent recoveries. The political negotiations over the U.S. debt ceiling and the downgrade of U.S. Treasury securities have raised doubts about the long-term sustainability of U.S. treasury. It limits the current freedom of action to give the world's largest economy a further boost. Page 1 of 8 The willingness and ability of political systems to make the necessary adjustments has been questioned in both the United States and Europe. All in all, this means that we are probably facing a period of lower growth than we have been used to. The financial and economic crisis was mitigated by extensive demand stimulus programs and the effect of the so-called automatic stabilizers. In many countries, this has left public finances with significantly higher debt and larger deficits. The possibilities for further fiscal stimulus to the economy are, if not exhausted then at least, considerably limited. By comparing the effects of previous financial crises over a number of years in a large number of countries, growth has been shown to have been negatively impacted for up to 10 years after a financial crisis compared to the previous 10 years. Balance sheet adjustment among consumers, businesses and the public sector is taking its toll on growth for a long time after a financial crisis. In addition, there is lower risk appetite and tougher financial regulation. In a way, you could say that there is good debt and there is bad debt. It makes sense to have a financial sector that channels savings to where the return on investments is highest. Companies need to be able to make investments when technology and market opportunities make it profitable. Investments, as a rule, require debt to increase. It is in most cases "good debt". For citizens, income and expenses throughout life are not equally distributed. There may therefore be good sense in indebted for a period of time. It also makes sense for governments to debt finance large infrastructure projects and to mitigate the consequences of sharp cyclical downturns. But debt must be approached with caution to avoid the negative effects. It must not continue to grow, so it becomes a millstone around its neck, and the ability to pay back can be called into question. It's bad debt. This is clearly shown by developments in a number of European countries. What is worrying is that despite the many bailouts or initiatives, there are no conspicuous signs of improvement  quite the opposite. The critical level of debt is not a point or a precise limit that is reached, but a development in which things get progressively worse. In a recent study, a researcher has shown that when gross debt rises to around 80-90% of GDP  be it public debt, corporate debt and, to some extent, household debt  it negatively affects the growth of society. This challenge is exacerbated by the fact that Western countries will all have the demographics against them for many years to come. The share of the elderly is growing and there will be Page 2 of 8 relatively fewer to support more. Healthcare costs will grow in particular due to the increasing number of elderly people. We are entering a period that will necessarily be marked by consolidation. We need to get used to a new "normal" where there must be a tougher prioritisation of public spending. *** And then to Denmark. After a few quarters of growth close to zero, GDP grew nicely again in Q2. Taken together, the first half of the year looks reasonable. But we should expect to have at least a couple of somewhat weak quarters ahead of us. For 2011 as a whole, we expect growth to end at 11/4% and at just over 11/2% in the next few years until 2013. This is a downward revision of almost 1/2 percentage point compared to our latest forecast. The downward revision is based on weaker growth in our export markets and weaker private demand. Both consumers and businesses remain reluctant to spend money. The weaker growth in export markets comes after a series of negative shocks to the world economy: commodity prices that had come up very high, the calamities in Japan, which not only affected the country itself, but through the international division of labor also affected other parts of the world. Add to this the debt problems in Europe and the United States, which I have already mentioned. The growth outlook at home is broadly in line with the euro area, but lower than in the US, where potential growth is higher due to population growth. Since the turn of the millennium, the growth trajectory in the Danish economy has been uneven. We started with a recession after the dot-com bubble, followed by a strong boom that went into an actual recession. We are now on our way out of it. The boom from 2005 to 2007 ended in a regular overheating of the economy. That is, unemployment was pushed down to a level that was clearly unsustainable, and employment to an equally unsustainably high level. It is an important message that employment and unemployment levels from the last boom, i.e. from 2005 to 2007, are not being targeted in the future economic policy. These levels can be achieved only by a new overheating. So what can we realistically set ourselves as a goal until 2020? It depends on the development of productivity and population development. And these are not sizes that you easily change. For a long period of time, Denmark has had a disappointingly low growth in productivity at the same time as a population development that implies a decreasing approach in the working age group. Page 3 of 8 Look. This has slowed the growth of the economy's potential output, that is, the growth that can be sustained over a longer period of time without unsustainable price and wage increases. On top of these growth-determining factors has come a recession, which further depresses potential output, at least for a period of time, as the recession, with its unemployment, impairs the skills of the workforce and the continuous renewal of the capital apparatus weakens. For the next few years, the growth in potential production is estimated at around 1% per year. Since we are currently below the potential production  there is a so-called negative production gap  there is room for production to grow faster than the growth in potential production for a few years, corresponding to the fact that the negative production gap is closed. In Danmarks Nationalbank's view, the closure of the negative output gap does not require what are currently referred to as growth packages. We expect the gap to close over the next few years as a result of the general business cycle. To promote this process would be an attempt to fine-tune the cyclical trend, which is in any case very difficult to time and which, in combination with the increased consumption and investment opportunities, may result in us hitting again over potential production. There is experience that the political reaction function in this case is not symmetrical. In plain language: the political will to intervene if things go too fast is not quite equivalent to the desire to push if you think it is too slow. In a longer perspective  that is, on the other side of 2013  potential growth is likely to be only slightly higher than 1% per year. The Ministry of Finance estimates 1.3% by 2020. Transitionally a little more when, and if, the withdrawal reform is implemented. Lastingly higher growth rates can only be achieved if, over time, we manage to increase the growth of hourly productivity. And that doesn't happen overnight. We probably even have the development of the business structure against us. We must therefore for a longer period of time adjust to a lower growth in the Danish economy than we have been used to, and than we have mentally adjusted to. We are heading for "a new normal". Economic policy must adapt to this. This does not necessarily mean more unemployed, but it dampens the rate at which wealth is increasing in this country. Denmark is one of the countries that, by virtue of a good starting point, has been able to ease the most during the crisis and at the same time one of the countries where the planned tightening is the least. The focus of economic stabilisation policy should be rigidly focused on the sustainability of public finances so that we do not lose the confidence of markets. If we lose it first, a negative interest rate effect could far overshadow any further expansionary measures. The current very Page 4 of 8 Low interest rates help keep the economy in check for many  both households and businesses. *** In terms of employment, the Danish economy has lost over 150,000 jobs since its peak in the autumn of 2008. These jobs have been lost in a very short period of time. Conversely, a large proportion of these jobs were also won in a relatively short period of time from 2005 onwards. The employment peak in 2008 represents a historic high. It was a peak reached during a clear overheating of the economy, illustrated by an unemployment rate of less than 50,000 people, while at the same time heavy imports of foreign labor. An unemployment rate of 50,000 is far below any structural level estimate, and similarly, employment and the labor force must be estimated to have been above their "structural levels." Let me repeat: it is both unrealistic and inappropriate to make the peak of employment in 2008 an objective of economic policy. Despite some increase in recent months, unemployment remains moderate. We expect a slight increase towards the beginning of 2012, but after that the unemployment rate falls down towards its structural level. * * * Much of the employment growth during the recovery was driven by an increase in construction activity. Construction employment increased by nearly 40,000, and in early 2008 reached its highest level since the early 1970s. As you know, the construction sector is very cyclical and the extraordinarily high level of activity in the construction sector was a long way down the road an overheating phenomenon, which also drained other sectors of vacant hands. It was clearly untenable. Employment in construction, which is largely a domestic industry with only modest exports, is now, according to national accounts, back to pre-boom levels, and employment has even been increasing in the first months of the current year. As of June 1, a housing deduction scheme was initiated, which has not yet had the opportunity to work fully. All in all, there is no evidence that there should be a need to do more to stimulate employment in construction, which is also struggling with significant productivity problems. Channelling resources into sectors with low productivity growth does not strengthen lasting growth and prosperity. The labour resources that have been freed up from the sector must most appropriately find new employment elsewhere. Of course, this requires that we here in Denmark are competitive in relation to foreign countries. And here we have something to catch up on. Page 5 of 8 *** I will now turn to one of the challenges facing the financial sector in the time to come. Prior to the financial crisis, liquidity was plentiful and cheap. Even small financial institutions could finance themselves in the international financial markets at advantageous prices and allowed themselves to be tempted by this. This meant that a number of institutions - and not just small ones - built up significant deposit deficits. The crisis has clearly shown that high loan growth financed by loans in international financial markets is risky. For small and medium-sized banks, on the other hand, the old-fashioned business model - where you do not lend more money than you are entrusted with from your own customers - has shown its strength. The financial crisis is still taking its toll and there is still some way to go before the sector can stand on its own two feet. So you can't just sit back and await calmer conditions. On the other hand, it is about to be the last call, and for some institutions there will be a need to make absolutely necessary adjustments to the business model so that they become viable. The debt issues with an individual State guarantee will expire in the course of 2012 and 2013. The challenge of refinancing this debt is compounded by the fact that several institutions will need to take on new debt simultaneously. For individual institutions, issuances represent a significant part of their overall balance sheet. A situation in which a larger number of financial institutions simultaneously get into liquidity problems can give rise to financial instability. This is a great challenge that you are facing. And, of course, as the country's central bank, it has given us cause for reflection. Danmarks Nationalbank has therefore, as you know, decided to extend the security basis for the monetary policy loans with the banks' lending of good quality. It raises a wide range of questions that we are currently considering. I will touch here on the main ones. Can it even be done without coming into conflict with "negative pledge" clauses in existing loans? We believe that after consulting legal expertise, as this is the usual central banking activity. On the other hand, we do not know all the forms of such clauses and do not have the practical opportunity to fully uncover this issue. It will therefore be your own business to secure yourself against such clauses. There will be talk that loans can be included in the collateral basis on an equal footing with other collateral and thus can be used as collateral for both intraday and interday credit. Page 6 of 8 In addition, we are considering introducing a longer current lending facility in Danmarks Nationalbank on the basis of the overall collateral basis at a variable interest rate. The extension will come into force from 1 October, and there is talk of a general arrangement that will run until further notice. Similar arrangements are known from central banks of other countries, including the European Central Bank. Lending as collateral for loans in Danmarks Nationalbank is made possible by an amendment to the Danish Securities Trading Act, which allows lending to be provided as collateral without the individual borrower having to be informed about it. Danmarks Nationalbank can only receive a list of the loans that are pledged. It constitutes the security act. Before the change in the law, pledging loans in practice was very difficult. The details of the scheme are being determined and will be announced together before we open the window on 1 October. On the one hand, the challenge is to design the scheme so that it can actually help facilitate the transition to a situation without state guarantees. On the other hand, Danmarks Nationalbank will not compromise on the fact that there must be full security behind our lending. Thus, it will be an indispensable principle that only lending with good quality can be mortgaged. But at the same time, there is no need to build up a large bureaucracy in Danmarks Nationalbank, where we have to credit the individual loans ourselves. We would prefer to use the credit rating that is already going on in the institutions. In this connection, we look at the Financial Supervisory Authority's quality categories, including the category "normal quality", which among other things requires that the loans are taken care of annotation-free from the customer's side. We are aware that there needs to be a translation of the IRB institutions' rating models into "normal quality". In order for us to accept that the assessment of the lending' bona fides is carried out by the individual financial institution, the external auditor must confirm that the institution has the necessary procedures and procedures for doing so. We also consider the extent to which the external auditor must declare himself on the list of loans provided as a mortgage. The loan-to-value of the loans will be determined after a haircut. This haircut is intended to ensure that Danmarks Nationalbank assumes only negligible credit risk. We have not yet decided on the exact haircut, but in setting the haircut, it is natural to look at the ECB's rules. At the same time, it is our legal assessment that if a financial institution gets into solvency problems  and a buyer cannot be found  the institution will end up in Finansiel Stabilitet A/S  regardless of whether a decision has already been made on Bank Package 3 or not. This also speaks to looking at valuation principles and haircuts in Finansiel Stabilitet A/S. Page 7 of 8 As I said, we have not yet decided on the exact haircut. Then there is the question of the delimitation of lending. In Denmark, for example, a large part of the loans are granted as overdraft facilities, which have a variable feature. The question is whether overdraft facilities are usable as collateral and under what conditions? For example, it could be an additional haircut that takes into account the inherent variation in overdraft facilities. We're looking at that. Interest rates are an extremely important parameter. An interest rate supplement to the policy rate can be an effective management tool that can help provide the right incentives for banks' use of different types of collateral. On the other hand, the consideration of the fixed exchange rate policy, which is unparalleled is Danmarks Nationalbank's most important task. If there is great depth in the use of the new loan-to-value basis, an interest rate premium could create uncertainty about the policy rate. In this context, it plays a role that the ECB does not apply an interest rate surcharge. An alternative governance mechanism could be a maximum over the use of the collateral base by each institution. On the other hand, quantitative restrictions narrow the flexibility of the scheme. Finally, briefly about your liquidity preparedness. We are in close dialogue with the Danish Financial Supervisory Authority about the conditions under which the new loan-to-value basis can be included in section 152. I expect that will be fully clarified ahead of October 1. * * * Finally, generally inspired by the sector, we will charge a fee to cover our administrative costs. Let it be said right away: It is not the intention that banks in the future should base their business model on the possibility of borrowing loans from Danmarks Nationalbank. Nor should you put your hands on the refinancing of individual state guarantees. Danmarks Nationalbank has previously called for you to prepare for the expiry of the individual state guarantees. The call continues to apply and has not become less topical. The extension of Danmarks Nationalbank's loan-to-value basis should not be a sleeping pillow, but is intended as a bridge builder to a future without government guarantees. Thanks for the attention.
