Det talte ord glder Nationalbankdirektr Nils Bernstein Tale ved Realkreditrdets rsmde 24. april 2008 Tak for indbydelsen. *** P Realkreditrdets rsmde sidste r sagde jeg om den konomiske situation i USA: Det ser heller ikke ud til, at de problemer, der er i selskaber, der har specialiseret sig i boligln til mindre kreditvrdige husholdninger, vil brede sig til andre dele af kapitalmarkederne. Det var ikke en vurdering jeg var alene om. Jeg tager det som en pmindelse om, at konomiske forudsigelser skal tages med et gran salt. Man kan uden at overdrive sige, at det er get noget anderledes end forudsagt. De konomiske udsigter for USA og Europa er gradvis blevet nedjusteret gennem det sidste rs tid. Og det der startede som problemer for selskaber specialiseret i skaldte subprimeln har spredt sig til andre dele af den finansielle sektor  ogs uden for USA  og lgger nu en dmper p produktion og beskftigelse. Som igen virker negativt tilbage p de finansielle virksomheder. Vurderingen er i dag, at USA er p vej ind i en recession, som i hvert fald varer til 2. halvr af 2008, hvorefter det i bedste fald vil g langsomt frem. Europa undgr efter alt at dmme recessionen, men m belave sig p beskedne vkstrater mellem 1 og 2 pct. i de kommende r. Udviklingen er kommet bag p de fleste, selvom hjkonjunkturen i USA havde toppet fr subprimeproblemerne. Et positivt trk er, at udviklingslandene og de nye vkstkonomier indtil videre stort set er get fri af den konomiske nedtur. Det har afbdet faldet i den globale konomi. Samtidig har prisstigningstakten taget et hop opad overalt i verden, drevet af stigende energi- og fdevarepriser. Prisstigningerne stter snvre grnser for fortsatte lempelser af den konomiske politik. Der er risiko for at f skubbet inflationsforventningerne i vejret og igangstte en pris- og lnspiral. De stigende priser p fdevarer mrkes selvsagt isr i de fattige lande og rykker hastigt opad p den internationale dagsorden. *** 2 Der tales i dag om tab i den finansielle sektor, der kan lbe op i 1000 mia. dollar. Et belb der er 3 gange s stort som det danske nationalprodukt, uden sammenligning i vrigt. Tabene har ramt bde finansielle virksomheder og andre, frst og fremmest i USA, men ogs i Europa. De strste tab er konstateret i nogle af verdens strste banker, og en enkelt har vret p fallittens rand. Der er tale om virksomheder, der har haft tusindvis af hjtuddannede og hjt betalte medarbejdere og chefer til rdighed for netop at undg sdanne tab. Forlbet har givet anledning til selvransagelse i bde finansielle virksomheder og hos myndigheder, der for sent s problemerne og greb ind. Hvordan kunne det g s galt, og hvordan kan man forebygge, at det sker igen? Der er allerede skrevet meget om rsagerne. Og forlbet vil helt sikkert blive genstand for mange lrde afhandlinger i de kommende r, som vil kunne drage fordel af bagklogskabens klare lys. Grundlggende kan finansiel virksomhed koges ned til at bygge bro mellem dem som p et givent tidspunkt har brug for at anvende mere end de tjener og rder over, og dem som er i den modsatte situation. Denne formidling betyder, at virksomheder kan investere i forventning om fremtidig indkomst. Og at vi som husholdninger kan kbe hus eller lejlighed med 20 pct. i udbetaling. Og at regeringer fra tid til anden kan have underskud p statsbudgettet. Den finansielle formidling  nr den er bedst - sikrer, at opsparerne fr det bedst mulige afkast til den valgte risiko, og at det er de mest givtige investeringer, der fremmes. Formidlingen foregr p tvrs af grnserne, og den finansielle sektor er blandt de fremmeste i globaliseringen. Vigtigheden af en effektiv finansiel sektor kan ikke overvurderes i et moderne samfund. Omfanget af den finansielle formidling har imidlertid i de seneste r vret s kraftigt voksende i kombination med sofistikeret produktudvikling, at risikovurderingssystemer og incitamentsstrukturer ikke alle steder har kunnet flge med i kampen om markedsandele. Hvor udviklingen har skabt en atmosfre af eufori, har grdighed og slseri kunnet trives. En vigtig mekanisme til at rette op herp er naturligvis, at nogen har brndt fingrene og har mrket konsekvenserne. Men det rkker nok ikke. Et sikkert gt er i dag, at der kommer skrpede regler. Nu hvor det gr den anden vej, glder det om at finde den rigtige balance mellem skrpede regler og hensynet til, at den finansielle formidling fortsat kan tjene samfundsnyttige forml. G7 landene anmodede sidste efterr det skaldte Financial Stability Forum (FSF), som bl.a. bestr af finansministerierne, centralbankerne og finanstil- 3 synene i de store lande, om at foretage en analyse af de rsager og svagheder, der har frt til krisen og komme med forslag, der kan forbedre de finansielle markeders og institutioners modstandsdygtighed. Det er interessant lsning og burde vre pensum for alle, der er beskftiget i den finansielle sektor. FSF fremstter 67 forslag under 5 hovedoverskrifter: Den frste gruppe af forslag handler om at skrpe kravene til de finansielle institutioners kapital, likviditet og risikostyring. Der skal vre mere at st imod med. Den umiddelbare vanskelighed er naturligvis implementeringen i en situation, hvor kravene kunne gre ondt vrre. Den anden gruppe af forslag har til forml at ge gennemsigtigheden i markederne ved at offentliggre alle relevante risici og skabe strre sikkerhed i vrdiansttelserne. Det har get usikkerheden, at de finansielle institutioner kun drypvis har deklareret deres tab, og at det har vret vanskeligt at vrdianstte aktiver, der ikke mere omsttes. En tredje gruppe af forslag retter sig mod kreditvurderings- bureauernes rolle i den finansielle formidling. Det er ndvendigt, at forbedre kvaliteten af vurderingsprocessen s interessekonflikter undgs og at ge forstelsen af resultaterne. Myndighederne skal revurdere deres brug af bureauernes arbejde. Som det fjerde foresls, at der for hver af de strste grnseoverskridende banker i verdenen oprettes en gruppe af reprsentanter for de relevante landes tilsynsmyndigheder. Det sker i en erkendelse af, at myndighederne i dag er for drligt forberedte til at hndtere eventuelle kriser i banker, der med datterselskaber og filialer arbejder p tvrs af landegrnserne. Endelig opfordres centralbankerne til strre fleksibilitet, herunder at udvide deres lnefaciliteter. En af erfaringerne i den nuvrende krise har vret, at centralbankerne ikke har haft de tilstrkkelige lnefaciliteter til rdighed overfor banker i likviditetsklemme. Som det fremgr, er der hilsener til os alle: De private virksomheder, regeringer, tilsynsmyndigheder og centralbanker. De fleste af forslagene anbefales at vre frt ud i livet inden udgangen af indevrende r. Resten i 2009. *** Hvordan pvirker s al det her os her i Danmark? Hvor paradoksalt det end lyder, kommer afmatningen i den internationale konomi, som den tegner sig nu, ganske bekvemt for Danmark. Konjunkturen har vret strk i en rrkke, hjulpet p vej af en lav rente og en ekspansiv finanspolitik. Beskftigelsen er rekordhj, og arbejdslsheden den laveste i en generation. Overskuddet p betalingsbalancen er faldet markant, 4 men der er heldigvis ikke opbygget finansielle ubalancer under opsvinget. Husholdningerne er under t velkonsoliderede og har meget at st imod med, selvom boligmarkedet har vret svagt i halvandet r. Den vsentligste ubalance er, at dansk konomi i nogen tid har befundet sig tt p sin kapacitetsgrnse. Manglen p arbejdskraft har get kravet om lnstigninger, og gabet mellem vksten i danske og udenlandske lnninger er vokset i de senere r. Forbrugerpriserne nede i marts op p 3,1 pct. rlig stigning; som i udlandet hovedsagelig drevet af stigende energi- og fdevarepriser. Forbrugernes forventninger til at priserne vil stige er voksende. Manglen p arbejdskraft stter grnser for vksten i dansk konomi. I Nationalbankens seneste prognose fra marts er det centrale skn, at dansk konomi bremser op i de kommende r. Men at vi frst i 2010 nr op p en arbejdslshed, der er forenelig med en bredygtig lnudvikling p lngere sigt. Tidligere var finansiel uro normalt ledsaget af valutauro i Europa. Det har der indtil nu kun vret mindre spor af. Det er nrliggende at give det mindre antal europiske valutaer som flge af euroen er stor del af ren herfor. Det er en fordel for Danmark, at euroen eksisterer, og nu er valuta i 15 lande. Det har sammen med Den Europiske Centralbanks likviditetstilfrsel som reaktion p finansuroen mindsket risikoen for strre realkonomiske skadevirkninger. Det finansielle system i Danmark er ikke uberrt af finansuroen. Men heldigvis mindre end i flere andre lande. Det skyldes, at danske investorer kun i mindre grad har investeret i - og dermed tabt p  subprime-relaterede aktiver. Vi har vores egne gode realkreditprodukter. Vi har dog ogs i Danmark set, hvorledes pengeinstitutterne p grund af usikkerheden er blevet mere tilbageholdende med at yde usikrede ln til hinanden i pengemarkedet, isr p de lngere lbetider. Finansieringen er sledes blevet kortere og dyrere. Og det pvirker isr de pengeinstitutter, der i de senere r har oparbejdet et stort indlnsunderskud i tillid til, at de kunne skaffe billig likviditet i pengemarkedet eller ved at udstede obligationer. I den nuvrende situation og i overensstemmelse med internationale anbefalinger overvejer vi i Danmarks Nationalbank ligesom andre centralbanker vores lnefaciliteter. Disse overvejelser er ikke tilendebragt. Men det er vores opfattelse, at veldrevne danske pengeinstitutter ikke undigt skal komme i en likviditetsklemme p grund af den internationale finansuro. Med disse ord siger jeg tak for opmrksomheden og nsker et fortsat godt rsmde.

Title: Speech at the 100th anniversary of DA wage statistics
text: Basis of speech: The spoken word applies Coffee: Speech at the 100th Anniversary of DA Wage Statistics Inflation and Welfare Today we mark that in October 1907 the main board of the Confederation of Danish Employers decided to establish a wage statistic. It is clear from the anniversary paper that the main reason for creating the wage statistics was to create a common frame of reference for employers and employees. Many labor disputes of that time were due to different perceptions of wage conditions within individual subjects. Other important things happened in the labor market in 1907. This year we celebrate the 100th anniversary of unemployment insurance. It was then Minister of the Interior Sigurd Berg who was the godfather of the Act on Unemployment Funds from 9 April 1907. One of the main elements of the scheme was that the members of the coffers were to provide one half of the dues and the state and municipality the other. Unemployment as a concept was thus recognized as a public matter. Denmark was the first country where a country-wide unemployment insurance took hold. And, as you know, the DA's wage statistics are also used to determine the amount of unemployment benefits. The DA's wage statistics have become a focal point for the wage negotiations in Denmark. Of course, the statistics have changed over the years, but what is called today's focus has always been on reliability, so that when negotiating wages, the parties had confidence in the numerical basis. Today, Danmarks Nationalbank is allowed to host this event is due to the practical circumstances, but there are now also some clear links between the wage statistics and Danmarks Nationalbank's activities. Wages, as you know, are the most important cost factor in society. A good illumination of wage conditions is therefore necessary if Danmarks Nationalbank is to be able to solve one of its main tasks, namely to "maintain a secure money system". The wording is from 1936. But the message was d0 and is d0 that Danmarks Nationalbank must seek to stabilise the crown's purchasing power, that is, the value of the money. The value of money is inversely proportional to the price level. When prices go up, you get fewer goods for your money d0 inflation erodes the value of money. Maintaining the purchasing power of the Crown therefore assumes that inflation is low. 2 In all countries and at all times, prices play a key role in the distribution of the economy's resources. The price of a commodity d0 and this also applies to labour d0 should reflect supply and demand conditions, and price changes should reflect shifts therein. In a situation of low and stable inflation, a rise in prices will usually be an expression of either a change in competitive conditions or a shift in the balance between supply and demand. It may be because demand has increased or because the cost of production has increased. Inflation is making it harder for consumers and businesses to interpret the signals from prices. The poorer basis for decision-making will generally lead to socially inappropriate decisions about buying, selling and production, so that the overall welfare of society is impaired. About 40 years ago, there was a tendency for politicians, economists and other participants in the social debate to give up on inflation. It was here to stay. So it was a matter of limiting the adverse effects beyond the unavoidable noise of market economy signals. Some even went so far as to consider inflation as a potential cyclical stimulus element. With appropriate indexation, one could reduce the cost of inflation, especially if it did not fluctuate too much. Regarding the latter, however, it quickly became an experience that high inflation is also fluctuating inflation. In practice, it was especially expensive time regulation of wages that became widespread, while in this country it was not really able to index the loan agreements. One of the big problems, otherwise, was that a real redistribution took place from society's savers to its patrons. Denmark suffered from a lack of savings, which was reflected in a chronic deficit in the balance of payments for a quarter of a century until the end of the 1980s. Sure, interest rates rose, but too little to compensate savers for rising inflation, so the real value of savings fell. The tax system played a key role in this regard. Interest rates were at the same time too high and too low. It was too high for businesses. In the early 1980s, interest rates were around 20% and inflation around 10. The real interest rate was thus around 10 per cent and thus at a level where very few investments in real capital were profitable. Too little was therefore invested in the production apparatus. At the same time, interest rates were too low for households, which were encouraged to borrow. People who paid the highest marginal tax were, in effect, paid nearly 75 percent of their interest expenses by the IRS. The real interest rate after tax, which is what counts for households, was negative, about -5 per cent, so via 3 in the tax system, households were rewarded for incurring debt, whether for house purchases or for direct consumption. Thus, it was largely the interaction between high inflation and the tax system that drove Denmark close to the abyss in the early 1980s. Eventually, politicians intervened, gradually dampening inflation to the current low level of below 2 per cent. Today, inflation is not something you think about on a day-to-day basis. The fixed exchange rate policy and the abolition of the animal time regulation of wages are important in this regard. Importantly, it was also that the tax value of the interest deduction was reduced so that households with negative capital income in 2007 can no longer deduct 3/4 of the interest expenses. The last 25 years of development in the Danish economy unconditionally support the gains from fairly stable prices and moderate wage increases. From the mid-1970s to the mid-1980s, inflation was high d0 averaging around 9% a year. But wage increases could not keep up with price developments, and real wages for a worker were lower in 1985 than in 1975. Since 1990, inflation has been close to 2% a year, and real wages have risen every year. In the last hundred years, there has only once been a longer period of constant real wage growth than the ongoing one. It was from the mid-1950s to the mid-1970s when real wages for workers rose significantly year on year. But then, unlike now, large imbalances were built up in the economy. Inflation was rising and clearly stronger than in the other European OECD countries, and competitiveness was greatly weakened. Thus, the seeds were laid for the following ten years of real wage stagnation. From the beginning of the 1980s, in virtually all developed countries, a shift took place towards a more stability-oriented policy. The previous widespread perception that there was a persistent contradiction between low inflation and high employment had proven to be wrong. There were therefore gains in the form of a better functioning economy to be gained by bringing inflation down. Of course, this also required lower wage increases if the development was to be sustainable. In Denmark, the change of direction in 1982 involved a number of fiscal and income policy tightenings. Moreover, the incoming government wrote off exchange rate adjustments d1 in practice devaluations d1 as an economic policy instrument. In the twenty-fifth years since then, the fixed exchange rate policy has been a central element of Danish economic policy, and the central rate of the crown vis-below first Dmarken and now the euro has been stuck for twenty years. Confidence in economic policy increased in the years after 1982, while inflation fell noticeably to the level around 2% that has been in force from 1990 to the present. 4 Confidence in the fixed exchange rate policy is essential to its success. It is also true for monetary policy more generally that good performance requires a credible central bank. It is usually a year-long process to gain the outside world's confidence that you will follow the announced policies. At the same time, trust is fragile in the sense that it can be lost again very quickly. A prerequisite for confidence in monetary policy and its ability to ensure stable prices is the existence of reliable price statistics that are perceived as credible. It allows businesses and consumers to better make informed choices. Similarly, a reliable wage statistic is important. Today, we can rejoice that 100 years ago, far-sighted people made the decision to make a reliable wage statistic. A statistic that both negotiators and those on whose behalf negotiations consider to describe reality. For the public servants, you haven't gotten that far. It is therefore possible in the public sphere to have discussions about the actual wage conditions of public employees. A statistic that both public employees and public employers agreed described the reality could thus have prevented the debate in recent months about what public employees actually earn. Finally, let me summarise: Danmarks Nationalbank must ensure low inflation, low inflation benefits the whole of society, not least the weakest groups, and the favourable developments in unemployment and employment in recent years are partly a result of the fact that we have come close to price stability. This development also assumes moderate wage increases, but has not hindered and continues to prevent an increase in real wages and corporate earnings. The challenge is to avoid real wages rising so much that the socio-economic balance is jeopardised. Therefore, the wage statistics are also scrutinized with great care. A reliable wage statistic is a good thing that is an important part of the Danish model.
text_original: Grundlag for talen: Det talte ord glder Kopi: Tale ved 100-rs jubilum for DA-lnstatistik Inflation og velfrd I dag markerer vi, at Dansk Arbejdsgiverforenings hovedbestyrelse i oktober 1907 besluttede at etablere en lnstatistik. Det fremgr af jubilumsskriftet, at hovedbegrundelsen for at oprette lnstatistikken var at skabe en flles referenceramme for arbejdsgivere og lnmodtagere. Mange arbejdskonflikter p den tid skyldtes forskellige opfattelser af lnforholdene inden for de enkelte fag. Der skete andre vigtige ting p arbejdsmarkedet i 1907. Vi kan i r fejre 100 rs-jubilet for Arbejdslshedsforsikringen. Det var davrende indenrigsminister Sigurd Berg, der stod fadder til Lov om Arbejdslshedskasser fra 9. april 1907. Et af hovedelementerne i ordningen var, at kassernes medlemmer skulle yde den ene halvdel af kontingentet og stat og kommune den anden. Arbejdslshed som begreb var dermed anerkendt som et offentligt anliggende. Danmark var det frste land, hvor en landsomspndende arbejdslshedsforsikring slog igennem. Og som bekendt bliver DA's lnstatistik ogs brugt til faststtelse af strrelsen af arbejdslshedsdagpenge. DA's lnstatistik er blevet et fikspunkt for lnforhandlingerne i Danmark. Statistikken har selvflgeligt ndret sig i lbet af rene, men det, der i dag hedder fokus, har hele tiden vret p plidelighed, s parterne, nr der blev forhandlet ln, havde tillid til det talmssige grundlag. Nr Nationalbanken i dag fr lov til at lgge hus til dette arrangement skyldes det praktiske forhold, men der er nu ogs nogle klare forbindelser mellem lnstatistikken og Nationalbankens virke. Lnnen er som bekendt den vigtigste omkostningsfaktor i samfundet. En god belysning af lnforholdene er derfor ndvendig, hvis Nationalbanken skal kunne lse den ene af sine hovedopgaver, nemlig at "at opretholde et sikkert pengevsen". Formuleringen er fra 1936. Men budskabet var  og er  at Nationalbanken skal sge at stabilisere kronens kbekraft, det vil sige pengenes vrdi. Penges vrdi er omvendt proportional med prisniveauet. Nr priserne stiger, fr man frre varer for sine penge  inflation udhuler pengenes vrdi. Fastholdelse af kronens kbekraft forudstter derfor, at inflationen er lav. 2 I alle lande og til alle tider spiller priserne en central rolle i forbindelse med fordelingen af konomiens resurser. Prisen p en vare - og det glder ogs arbejdskraft - br afspejle udbuds- og eftersprgselsforholdene, og prisndringer br afspejle skift heri. I en situation med lav og stabil inflation vil en prisstigning da ogs som regel vre udtryk for enten ndrede konkurrenceforhold eller for et skift i balancen mellem udbud og eftersprgsel. Det kan vre fordi eftersprgslen er steget, eller fordi omkostningerne i produktionen er get. Inflation gr det svrere for forbrugere og virksomheder at tolke signalerne fra priserne. Det drligere beslutningsgrundlag vil generelt fre til samfundsmssigt set uhensigtsmssige beslutninger om kb, salg og produktion, s den samlede velfrd i samfundet forringes. For rundt regnet 40 r siden var der en tendens til, at politikere, konomer og andre deltagere i samfundsdebatten gav op over for inflationen. Den var kommet for at blive. S det gjaldt om at begrnse skadevirkningerne ud over den uundgelige stj i de markedskonomiske signaler. Nogle gik endda s langt, s man betragtede inflation som et potentielt konjunkturstimulerende element. Med en passende indeksering kunne man mindske omkostningerne ved inflationen, isr hvis den ikke svingede for meget. Angende det sidste blev det dog hurtigt en erfaring, at hj inflation ogs er svingende inflation. I praksis var det isr dyrtidsregulering af lnninger, der blev udbredt, mens man her i landet ikke for alvor nede at f indekseret lneaftalerne. Et af de store problemer var ellers, at der fandt en real omfordeling sted fra samfundets sparere til dets lnere. Danmark led under mangel p opsparing, som kom til udtryk i et kronisk underskud p betalingsbalancen i et kvart rhundrede frem til slutningen af 1980erne. Nok steg renten, men for lidt til at kompensere sparerne for den stigende inflation, s realvrdien af opsparingen faldt. Skattesystemet spillede en central rolle i den forbindelse. Renten var p samme tid for hj og for lav. Den var for hj for virksomhederne. I begyndelsen af 1980erne var renten omkring 20 pct. og inflationen omkring 10. Realrenten var sledes omkring 10 pct. og dermed p et niveau, hvor det var meget f investeringer i realkapital, der var rentable. Der blev derfor investeret for lidt i produktionsapparatet. Renten var samtidig for lav for husholdningerne, som blev tilskyndet til at lne. Personer, der betalte den hjeste marginalskat, fik i realiteten nsten 75 pct. af deres renteudgifter betalt af skattevsenet. Realrenten efter skat, som er det, der tller for husholdningerne, var negativ, ca. -5 pct., s via 3 skattesystemet blev husholdningerne belnnet for at stifte gld, hvad enten det var til huskb eller til direkte forbrug. Det var sledes i hj grad samspillet mellem hj inflation og skattesystemet, der krte Danmark tt p afgrunden i begyndelsen af 1980erne. Til sidst greb politikerne ind og fik gradvist dmpet inflationen til det nuvrende lave niveau i underkanten af 2 pct. I dag er inflation ikke noget, man tnker p i det daglige. Fastkurspolitikken og ophvelsen af dyrtidsreguleringen af lnninger er vigtige i den forbindelse. Vigtigt var det ogs, at skattevrdien af rentefradraget blev sat ned, s husstande med negativ kapitalindkomst i 2007 ikke mere kan fradrage 3/4 af renteudgifterne. De sidste 25 rs udvikling i dansk konomi sttter ubetinget gevinsterne ved nogenlunde stabile priser og moderate lnstigninger. Fra midten af 1970'erne til midten af 1980'erne var inflationen hj  i gennemsnit omkring 9 pct. om ret. Men lnstigningerne kunne ikke flge med prisudviklingen, og reallnnen for en arbejder var lavere i 1985 end i 1975. Siden 1990 har inflationen som nvnt ligget tt p 2 pct. om ret, og reallnningerne er steget hvert r. I de sidste hundrede r har der kun n gang vret en lngere periode med konstant reallnsfremgang end den igangvrende. Det var fra midten af 1950'erne til midten af 1970'erne, hvor reallnnen for arbejdere steg markant r for r. Men dengang blev der i modstning til nu opbygget store ubalancer i konomien. Inflationen var stigende og klart strkere end i de vrige europiske OECD-lande, og konkurrenceevnen blev kraftigt svkket. Dermed blev kimen lagt til de flgende ti rs reallnsstagnation. Fra begyndelsen af 1980'erne fandt der i stort set alle udviklede lande et skifte sted mod en mere stabilitetsorienteret politik. Den tidligere udbredte opfattelse af, at der var en vedvarende modstning mellem lav inflation og hj beskftigelse havde vist sig at vre forkert. Der var derfor gevinster i form af en bedre fungerende samfundskonomi at hente ved at f inflationen ned. Det forudsatte selvflgelig ogs lavere lnstigninger, hvis udviklingen skulle vre holdbar. I Danmark involverede retningsskiftet i 1982 en rkke finans- og indkomstpolitiske stramninger. Desuden afskrev den tiltrdende regering valutakursjusteringer  i praksis devalueringer  som konomisk-politisk instrument. Fastkurspolitikken har i de femogtyve r siden da vret et centralt element i den danske konomiske politik, og kronens centralkurs over for frst Dmarken og nu euroen har ligget fast i tyve r. Tilliden til den konomiske politik steg i rene efter 1982, samtidig med at inflationen faldt mrkbart til det niveau omkring 2 pct., der har vret gldende fra 1990 og til nu. 4 Tilliden til fastkurspolitikken er afgrende for dens succes. Det glder ogs for pengepolitik mere generelt, at gode resultater fordrer en trovrdig centralbank. Det er normalt en relang proces at opn omverdenens tiltro til, at man vil flge den annoncerede politik. Samtidig er tilliden skrbelig i den forstand, at den meget hurtigt kan mistes igen. En forudstning for tilliden til pengepolitikken og dens evne til at sikre stabile priser er, at der findes en plidelig prisstatistik, der opfattes som trovrdig. Det giver virksomheder og forbrugere bedre mulighed for at trffe deres valg p et informeret grundlag. P samme mde er en plidelig lnstatistik vigtig. Vi kan i dag glde os over, at fremsynede personer for 100 r siden traf beslutning om at lave en plidelig lnstatistik. En statistik som bde forhandlere og dem p hvis vegne der forhandles anser for at beskrive virkeligheden. For de offentligt ansatte er man ikke net s langt. Det er derfor muligt i det offentlige rum at fre diskussioner om de offentligt ansattes faktiske lnforhold. En statistik, som bde de offentligt ansatte og de offentlige arbejdsgivere var enige om beskrev virkeligheden, kunne sledes have forebygget de seneste mneders debat om, hvad de offentligt ansatte egentligt tjener. Lad mig til sidst opsummere: Nationalbanken skal sikre en lav inflation, en lav inflation er til fordel for hele samfundet, ikke mindst de svageste grupper, og de seneste rs gunstige udvikling i arbejdslshed og beskftigelse er bl.a. et resultat af, at vi er kommet tt p prisstabilitet. Den udvikling forudstter ogs moderate lnstigninger, men har ikke hindret og hindrer fortsat ikke en fremgang i reallnnen og virksomhedernes indtjening. Udfordringen er at undg, at reallnnen stiger s meget, at den samfundskonomiske balance sttes over styr. Derfor granskes lnstatistikken ogs med stor omhu. En plidelig lnstatistik er et gode, som er en vigtig del af den danske model.

Title: Speech at Think Tank Europe's webinar on digital euro
text: SPEECH BY GOVERNOR PER CALLESEN AT THINK TANK EUROPE WEBINAR ON 23 APRIL 2021 ON THE QUESTION: "SHOULD THE EU HAVE A DIGITAL EURO" THE SPOKEN WORD APPLIES 23. april 2021 Thank you for the invitation to speak at Think Tank Europe's webinar1. I'm not going to use the term "digital euro" as it doesn't give a good picture of what the issue is about. Individuals and companies have digital deposit accounts in private banks. Private banks in the euro area all have digital deposit accounts with the European Central Bank, the ECB. In other words, deposits and the payment system are already highly digitized. Thus, the ECB issues large amounts of digital currency if this is how it prefers to refer to deposit accounts. What is new is not digital, but whether individuals and not financial companies should have a deposit account d0 or something that works in the same way d0 with a direct claim against the central bank. The most correct term will be "retail CBDC2", which translates to central bank currency for retail customers. Neither the ECB nor other central banks have decided whether this is something they will do. It can get very big or it can get very small. The conclusion seems to be that it will be small, but not very small. In autumn 2020, the ECB wrote a very good report on the subject3, which can be recommended to be read in its entirety. Chapter 3 provides a thorough review of the problems of such a product, and the ECB and others have subsequently spoken publicly about how they envisage how these problems can be dealt with, if any45. Although it has not been decided, this possible handling provides an opportunity to interpret what we are talking about: a) A cap, probably in the order of 3,000 euros equivalent to just over 20,000 DKK, will be introduced as a limit on what can be on such an account. It will require a mechanism that automatically transfers an excess amount to a private deposit account if deposits into the account would otherwise bring it over the limit. The ceiling is due to the consideration of avoiding a comprehensive 1 2 3 4 Dele af webinaret kan genses p8c Tbenketanken Europas hjemmeside Central Bank Digital Currency ECB d0 report on a digital euro: Disruption or transformation: the impact of a digital euro on the financial system - 5 cost-of-a-digital-euro-for-the-financial-system/ Evolution or revolution? The impact of a digital euro on the financial system, speech by Fabio Panetta, Member of the Executive Board of t he ECB, at a Bruegel online seminar Page 1 of 4 the transfer of deposits in private banks to the ECB d0 which does not have to be a major problem in normal times, but in turn would amplify a financial crisis in times of pressure. It is a good question whether, precisely in a crisis where it is particularly important to avoid it, political or popular pressure will not arise to raise the limit. b) The administration of such an account will be zoned to the private banks. Thus, the ECB does not want to manage hundreds of millions of deposit accounts with the associated obligation to manage account transfers and customer inquiries, to know customers and to comply with anti-money laundering rules, etc. Central banks have neither the expertise nor the capacity to operate retail banking. You have to imagine that when you go into your regular online banking and look at the accounts you have, there will be an extra one that looks like the others, where the ceiling is 3,000 euros, but where you have a direct claim against the ECB (instead of being covered by deposit guarantee and the soundness of the private bank). We have a certain parallel in the shareholder account, which has a cap, and where people with shares move a part of them to that account if they see benefits from it. c) There will be corresponding restrictions on the use of such accounts by foreigners. It can also be difficult in practice for foreigners to open an account without access to a regular account with a euro area bank. This will be done to avoid extra currency pressure, speculation and volatility in the foreign exchange market. It should be noted that restrictions in the form of account caps and restrictions on foreigners mean that in practice there will be no effect of significance in relation to a desire for greater dissemination of the international role of the euro. But there could probably be a role for tourists. The claim against the ECB does not have to take the form of a deposit account directly. There will also be experiments with the development of so-called "token", which are marketable unique digital certificates that may even be exchanged directly from person to person, e.g. with mobile phones and without being on the web, i.e. offline. One has to imagine that two people can exchange a certificate offline, while the posting only happens later when you are online. It's a potentially interesting innovation. So far, it doesn't look like there's an effective system for handling that type of transaction. Sweden has tested it a bit6. A token-based product does not change the need for all persons' receivables to be registered centrally7. There will be quite a few security- questions that need to be dealt with, e.g. in relation to if you lose your mobile phone or the computer breaks down. It is not obvious why such a product needs to be run by a central bank rather than private banks, but it is likely to foster innovation in the field. It can be argued that retail CBDC is legally a parallel to cash, as the central bank is the direct counterparty, but on a practical level it is unlikely to be perceived by customers as a substitute for cash. It is a new digital product, which in its nature is very close to what you can do with existing digital banking products. There will therefore be close substitution between the digital products. There will be a fear among some as to whether retail CBDC will be 6 7 E-krona pilot phase 1 On the possibility of a / cash-like CBDC - like-cbdc.pdf Page 2 of 4 used as an opportunity to remove the cash d0 the ECB and other central banks therefore much to explain that this will not be the case. There will be a discussion about anonymity. The use of cash is quite anonymous, but digital products cannot be. In principle, you can set a limit below which you promise not to investigate payments, but then you also have to monitor that criminals do not circumvent the border by dividing payments into smaller chunks, and in practice it is difficult to refuse criminal investigations with reference to such an administratively set limit. There will be a question of return on the deposit. In principle, the interest rate can be set at such an unattractive level that for deposits over an amount of, for example, the 3,000 euros can replace the effect of a ceiling. However, it is unrealistic that a low rate of return will be able to stop a bank run. A limit of db3,000 is unlikely to have a noticeable impact, but otherwise the ECB's remuneration on the account would undoubtedly form a sub-limit for what private banks can set of deposit rates. In relation to the motivation for retail CBDC, the following is inspired by an interview with Agustin Carstens, General Manager of BIS8. In practice, customers are unlikely to experience much new with retail CBDC, as the product is so similar to existing private bank accounts. (It might be expressed in the way that retail CBDC will be a small step for consumers and businesses, but a big step for central banks.) Carstens mentions three types of motivation for the ongoing projects. First, there are many countries and regions with less developed payment systems, for example, without instant payments. There, an account for everyone in the same bank will make it easier to get instant payments. Secondly, it will initiate some additional competition that can foster innovation in the private sector as well. Thirdly, there are some who perceive it as a special advantage to be able to directly "pay in central bank money", which is what you can do with cash, although more and more people choose not to. Note that it is neither controlled by central banks nor politically that consumers and businesses are increasingly choosing to move money between their accounts digitally rather than with cash. Further, it is argued that if the individual countries and currency areas design retail CBDC according to the same standards, it would be possible to develop further on a system for cross-border payments between currency areas. Currently, the majority of the discussions are about the possible technological solution, cf. also that many people pay attention to the word "digital". At Danmarks Nationalbank, we have spent a lot of resources on the issue, written a report9 and follow thoroughly what other central banks are doing. However, we have started elsewhere, namely with the consideration of what the gains will be for the users and, not least, the economic, financial, legal, operational and competitive issues. 8 Agustin Carsten's interview with Adam Posen (PIIE): 9 Central Bank Digital Money in Denmark? Page 3 of 4 How will it affect Denmark if other central banks provide access to retail CBDC, i.e. accounts for citizens and companies at central banks? The answer is that it depends on the construction. There will be virtually no effect if we are talking about a product with an account ceiling of 3,000 euros and with restrictions on what foreigners can do. Conversely, it can be significant if, which seems unrealistic, access to unlimited accounts at the ECB becomes available to both Danes and euro area residents, including large companies and pension funds. That would hardly be a problem in the current situation, but one has to imagine some potentially larger capital movements, including during periods of pressure on the crown. In conclusion, some remarks in headline form about what Danmarks Nationalbank sees as the biggest challenges in the payments area, which at the same time are areas we devote a lot of resources to: a5 The biggest thing is undoubtedly security and stability, including both the risk of cybercrime and breakdowns in the IT systems for more technical reasons. We have extensive cooperation with the sector, public authorities and other central banks in the field. We chair and secretariat FSOR10, carry out TIBERtest11 and head the Payments Council We are working to integrate the technical preparedness and robustness of our role as banks' online banking into the common European system. a5 We were out relatively early with instant payments in Denmark, and this is an advantage we must preserve. a5 The handling of anti-money laundering rules and the requirements for knowing customers is a major challenge for both banks and public authorities. A lot of resources are spent on it, and it is not obvious that the results are commensurate with it. We have tried to contribute with the development of an advanced digital system that, with the help of detailed payment information, can better target a joint effort in this area. a5 Payments across countries still leave much to be desired, especially (which we will hear more about from the initiators of Diem) transfers to less developed countries, but also between countries in Europe and even the Nordic countries. The ECB is developing the TIPS instant payment system to handle different currencies, and the largest Nordic banks have joined forces on the P27 project, which will also be able to contribute in this field. Thanks for the word. 10 11 Financial Sector Forum for Operational Resilience Threat Inlelligence Based Ethical Redteaming Page 4 of 4

APRIL 2021 OM SPRGSMLET: "SKAL EU HAVE EN DIGITAL EURO" DET TALTE ORD GLDER 23. april 2021 Tak for invitationen til tale p Tnketanken Europas webinar1. Jeg kommer ikke til at bruge udtrykket "digital euro", da det ikke giver et godt billede af, hvad sprgsmlet handler om. Privatpersoner og virksomheder har digitale indlnskonti i private banker. Private banker i euroomrdet har alle digitale indlnskonti i Den Europiske Centralbank, ECB. Med andre ord er indln og betalingssystemet allerede meget digitaliseret. ECB udsteder sledes store mngder digital valuta, hvis det er sdan man foretrkker at benvne indlnskonti. Det nye er ikke det digitale, men om privatpersoner og ikke finansielle virksomheder skal have en indlnskonto  eller noget der virker p samme mde - med et direkte krav mod centralbanken. Den mest korrekte betegnelse vil vre "retail CBDC2", som kan oversttes til centralbankvaluta for detailkunder. Hverken ECB eller andre centralbanker har besluttet, om det er noget, de vil gre. Det kan blive meget stort eller det kan blive meget smt. Konklusionen synes at blive, at det bliver smt, men ikke meget smt. ECB skrev i efterret 2020 en rigtig god rapport om emnet3, som kan anbefales lst i sin helhed. Kapitel 3 giver en grundig gennemgang af problemerne ved et sdant produkt, og ECB og andre har efterflgende udtalt sig offentligt om, hvordan de forestiller sig hvordan disse problemer i givet fald kan hndteres45. Selv om det jo s heller ikke er besluttet, giver denne mulige hndtering en mulighed for at fortolke, hvad vi taler om: a) Der vil blive indfrt et loft, sandsynligvis i strrelsesordenen 3.000 euro svarende til godt 20.000 kr., som en grnse for hvad der kan st p en sdan konto. Det vil krve en mekanisme, der automatisk overfrer et overskydende belb til en privat indlnskonto, hvis indbetalinger til kontoen ellers ville bringe den over grnsen. Loftet skyldes hensynet til at undg en omfattende 1 2 3 4 Dele af webinaret kan genses p Tnketanken Europas hjemmeside http://thinkeuropa.dk/oekonomi/skal-eu-have-en-digital-euro Central Bank Digital Currency ECB  report on a digital euro: https://www.ecb.europa.eu/euro/html/digitaleuro-report.en.html Disruption or transformation: the impact of a digital euro on the financial system https://www.bruegel.org/events/disruption-or-transformation-the- 5 cost-of-a-digital-euro-for-the-financial-system/ Evolution or revolution? The impact of a digital euro on the financial system, speech by Fabio Panetta, Member of the Executive Board of t he ECB, at a Bruegel online seminar https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/key/date/2021/html/ecb.sp210210~a1665d3188.en.html Page 1 of 4 overflytning af indln i private banker til ECB  hvilket ikke behver at vre et strre problem i normale tider, men til gengld ville forstrke en finansiel krise i tider med pres. Det er et godt sprgsml, om der ikke netop i en krise, hvor det er srlig vigtigt at undg det, vil opst et politisk eller folkeligt pres for at hve grnsen. b) Administrationen af en sdan konto vil blive udlagt til de private banker. ECB nsker sledes ikke at administrere mange hundrede millioner indlnskonti med tilhrende pligt til at administrere kontooverfrsler og kundehenvendelser samt kende kunderne og overholde hvidvaskregler mv. Centralbanker har hverken ekspertise i eller kapacitet til at drive detailbank. Man skal forestille sig, at nr man gr ind i sin almindelige netbank og ser p de konti man har, s vil der komme en ekstra, der ligner de andre til forveksling, hvor loftet er 3.000 euro, men hvor man har et direkte krav mod ECB (i stedet for at vre dkket af indskydergaranti og den private banks soliditet). Vi har herhjemme en vis parallel i aktionrkontoen, som har et loft, og hvor folk med aktier flytter en del af dem over p den konto, hvis de ser fordele ved det. c) Der vil vre tilsvarende restriktioner p udlndinges anvendelse af sdanne konti. Det kan ogs i praksis vre vanskeligt for udlndinge at oprette en konto uden adgang til en almindelig konto i en bank i euroomrdet. Det vil man gre for at undg ekstra valutapres, spekulation og volatilitet p valutamarkedet. Man skal bemrke, at begrnsninger i form af kontoloft og restriktioner p udlndinge betyder, at der i praksis ikke vil vre nogen effekt af betydning i forhold til et nske om strre udbredelse af euroens internationale rolle. Men der kan formentlig blive en rolle for turister. Kravet mod ECB behver ikke at tage form direkte som en indlnskonto. Der bliver ogs eksperimenteret med udvikling af skaldte "token", som er omsttelige unikke digitale certifikater, som mske endda vil kunne udveksles direkte fra person til person, fx med mobiltelefoner og uden at vre p nettet, dvs. offline. Man skal forestille sig, at to personer kan udveksle et certifikat offline, mens konteringen frst sker senere, nr man er online. Det er en potentielt interessant innovation. Indtil videre ser det ikke ud til, at der er et effektivt system til hndtering af den type transaktioner. Sverige har testet det lidt6. Et token-baseret produkt ndrer ikke ved behovet for, at alle personers tilgodehavende skal registreres centralt7. Der vil vre ganske mange sikkerheds- sprgsml, der skal hndteres, fx i forhold til hvis man mister sin mobiltelefon eller computeren gr itu. Det er ikke oplagt hvorfor et sdant produkt behver at vre drevet af en centralbank frem for private banker, men det kan sandsynligvis fremme innovation p omrdet. Der kan argumenteres for, at retail CBDC rent juridisk er en parallel til kontanter, da centralbanken er den direkte modpart, men p det praktiske plan vil det af kunderne nppe blive opfattet som en substitut for kontanter. Det er et nyt digitalt produkt, som i sin karakter ligger meget tt op af hvad man kan med eksisterende digitale bankprodukter. Der vil derfor vre tt substitution mellem de digitale produkter. Der vil vre en frygt blandt nogen for om retail CBDC vil blive 6 7 E-krona pilot phase 1 On the possibility of a https://www.riksbank.se/en-gb/payments--cash/e-krona/e-krona-reports/e-krona-pilot-phase-1-report-3/ cash-like CBDC https://www.riksbank.se/globalassets/media/rapporter/staff-memo/engelska/2021/on-the-possibility-of-a-cash- like-cbdc.pdf Page 2 of 4 brugt som anledning til at fjerne kontanterne  ECB og andre centralbanker derfor meget for at forklare, at det ikke vil vre tilfldet. Der vil vre en diskussion om anonymitet. Anvendelse af kontanter er ganske anonym, men det kan digitale produkter ikke vre. Man kan i princippet stte en grnse, under hvilken man lover ikke at efterforske betalinger, men s er man ogs ndt til at overvge, at kriminelle ikke omgr grnsen ved at dele betalinger op i mindre bidder, og i praksis er det svrt at afvise efterforskning af kriminalitet med henvisning til en sdan administrativt fastsat grnse. Der vil vre et sprgsml om forrentning af indestendet. Renten kan principielt sttes p et s uattraktivt niveau, at det for indestende over et belb p fx de 3.000 euro kan erstatte virkningen af et loft. Det er dog urealistisk, at en lav forrentning vil kunne stoppe et bankrun. Det vil nppe have mrkbar betydning med en grnse p 3.000 euro, men ellers ville ECB's forrentning af kontoen uden tvivl danne en undergrnse for hvad private banker kan stte af indlnsrente. I forhold til motivationen for retail CBDC er det flgende inspireret af et interview med Agustin Carstens, General Manager af BIS8. I praksis vil kunderne nppe opleve ret meget nyt med retail CBDC, da produktet i s hj grad minder om eksisterende private bankkonti. (Det kan mske udtrykkes p den mde at retail CBDC vil vre et lille skridt for forbrugere og virksomheder, men et stort skridt for centralbanker). Carstens nvner tre typer af motivation for de igangvrende projekter. For de frste er der mange lande og regioner med mindre udviklede betalingssystemer, fx uden straksbetalinger. Der vil en konto for alle i samme bank gre det nemmere at f straksbetalinger. For det andet vil det igangstte noget ekstra konkurrence, som kan fremme innovationen i ogs den private sektor. For det tredje er der nogen, der opfatter det som en srlig fordel at kunne direkte "betale i centralbankpenge", hvilket er det man kan med kontanter, om end stadig flere vlger det fra. Bemrk at det hverken er styret af centralbanker eller politisk at forbrugere og virksomheder i stort og stigende omfang vlger at flytte penge mellem deres konti digitalt frem for med kontanter. Supplerende argumenteres for at sfremt de enkelte lande og valutaomrder udformer retail CBDC efter samme standarder, ville det vre muligt at udvikle videre p et system til grnseoverskridende betalinger imellem valutaomrderne. Aktuelt handler hovedparten af diskussionerne om den mulige teknologiske lsning, jf. ogs at mange hfter sig ved ordet "digital". Vi har i Nationalbanken brugt en del ressourcer p sprgsmlet, skrevet en rapport9 og flger grundigt med i, hvad andre centralbanker gr. Vi har imidlertid startet et andet sted, nemlig med overvejelserne om, hvilke gevinster der vil vre for brugerne og ikke mindst de konomiske, finansielle, juridiske, operationelle og konkurrencemssige sprgsml. 8 Agustin Carstens interview med Adam Posen (PIIE): https://www.bis.org/speeches/sp210331.htm 9 Digitale centralbankpenge i Danmark? https://www.nationalbanken.dk/da/publikationer/Sider/2017/12/Digitale-centralbankpenge-i-Danmark.aspx Page 3 of 4 Hvordan vil det pvirke Danmark, sfremt andre centralbanker giver adgang til retail CBDC, dvs. konti for borgere og virksomheder i centralbanker? Svaret er, at det afhnger af konstruktionen. Der vil vre stort set ingen effekt, hvis vi taler om et produkt med kontoloft p 3.000 euro og med restriktioner p, hvad udlndinge kan gre. Omvendt kan det have vsentlig betydning hvis der, hvilket forekommer urealistisk, bliver tale om adgang til ubegrnsede konti i ECB for bde danskere og indbyggere i euroomrdet, herunder for store virksomheder og pensionskasser. Det ville nppe vre noget problem i den nuvrende situation, men man m i s fald forestille sig nogle potentielt strre kapitalbevgelser, herunder i perioder med pres p kronen. Afslutningsvis nogle bemrkninger i overskriftform om hvad Nationalbanken ser som de strste udfordringer p betalingsomrdet, hvilket samtidigt er omrder, vi stter mange ressourcer af til:  Det strste er uden tvivl sikkerhed og stabilitet, herunder bde risikoen for cyberkriminalitet og nedbrud i it-systemerne af mere tekniske rsager. Vi har et omfattende samarbejde med sektoren, offentlige myndigheder og andre centralbanker p feltet. Vi varetager formandskab og sekretariat for FSOR10, udfrer TIBERtest11 og leder Betalingsrdet Vi arbejder p at f integreret det tekniske beredskab og robustheden bag vores rolle som bankernes netbank i det flles europiske system.  Vi var relativt tidligt ude med straksbetalinger i Danmark, og det er en fordel, vi skal bevare.  Hndteringen af hvidvaskregler og kravene til at kende kunderne er en stor udfordring for bde bankerne og de offentlige myndigheder. Der bruges store ressourcer p det, og det er ikke oplagt at resultaterne str ml med det. Vi har forsgt et bidrage med udviklingen af et avanceret digitalt system, der ved hjlp af detaljerede betalingsoplysninger bedre kan mlrette en flles indsats p omrdet.  Betalinger p tvrs af lande lader fortsat meget tilbage at nske, isr (som vi kommer til hre mere om fra initiativtagerne til Diem) overfrsler til mindre udviklede lande, men ogs mellem lande i Europa og sgar Norden. Det arbejdes der p. ECB er ved at videreudvikle straksbetalingssystemet TIPS til at hndtere forskellige valuta, og de strste nordiske banker er get sammen om P27-projektet, der ogs vil kunne bidrage p det felt. Title: Speech at the Nordic Cyber Conference
text: SPEECH BY GOVERNOR LARS ROHDE AT THE NORDIC CYBER CONFERENCE CHECK AGAINST DELIVERY 21 November 2017 On behalf of the Nordic central banks I would like to welcome you all to the 1st Annual Nordic Cyber Conference here in Copenhagen. I am very pleased to see that so many have chosen to participate today. I want to give a special warm welcome to all the presenters who have agreed to share their knowledge on cybersecurity with us; it is highly appreciated. CYBERTHREATS AND FINANCIAL STABILITY The cyber threat is real. The World Economic Forum has consistently ranked cyberattacks and data theft among the top 10 global risks and cyber is discussed among the world's leaders alongside natural disasters and interstate conflict when they meet in Davos. In worst case cyberattacks could lead to financial instability. When it comes to securing the financial stability, cyberresilience is a factor alongside ensuring that the credit institutions are robust and that they have sufficient capital and liquidity reserves to draw on in difficult times. The cyberthreat is here to stay, and to me personally it means that terms like red-team testing, NotPetya and social engineering are becoming part of my everyday vocabulary. INTERCONNECTED AND BACK-UP We live in a digitalised world. And the Nordic countries are among the most digitalised countries in the world. Also, the Nordic countries are renowned for having some of the most modern and well-functioning financial infrastructures in the world. One example is the instant retail payments. Side 1 af 3 These solutions are based on a close collaboration within the financial sector in the Nordic countries. This is something to be proud of and a strength, but in some sense this high level of interconnection is also a liability. We are not stronger than the weakest link. It is therefore essential that we take measures to best protect us from cyberattacks, detect them when they occur, respond to them appropriately, and recover from them as fast as possible. Otherwise the very foundation of our digital financial sector could be compromised. And let us not forget that ultimately the cyberthreat could endanger the trust in the financial sector and also the digitalisation of the society as a whole. One question that comes to my mind though, is the following: Do we have a sufficient back up system if our infrastructure systems do not work for a longer period of time? We need to focus on this in the future. CYBERATTACKS IN A FINANCIAL CRISIS The cyberthreat is complex. Attacks are perpetrated by a diverse group of agents, from small-time offenders through hacktivists to nation states. Attacks may spread rapidly through networks, and their impact can reach far beyond their intended targets. One example is the NotPetya attack on Ukraine in June this year. The malware spread to a large number of global companies and seriously disrupted their operations for days. One victim was the Danish shipping giant Maersk, which has since reported losses between 250 and 300 million dollars due to the incident. Imagine that such an attack were to hit a bank that was already in financial trouble during the financial crisis in 2008? Imagine that a major attack hit the entire financial sector with the same consequences as NotPetya? The consequences for financial stability could be severe. Side 2 af 3 CORPORATION Central banks  in close cooperation with the financial sector, public authorities, and the governments  need to play an active role in enhancing the cyberresilience of the critical financial infrastructure. This cooperation should of course also be supplemented by initiatives in the financial sector. In that regard, I am very pleased that the Nordic banks have decided to establish the Nordic Financial Cert with the main purpose of sharing information and thereby increasing the cyberresilience in the Nordic financial sector. CONTENT OF THE CONFERENCE In my view, one of the best ways to ensure higher cyberresilience is through knowledge-sharing, and that is exactly what I hope we can all achieve at the conference today. We will begin with an overview of the cyberthreat seen from different perspectives. Next, we will learn how to deal with it, on a national strategic level, both from a governmental and a private sector point of view. We will continue the afternoon with a discussion of cyberregulation as well as cybertesting individual institutions. Finally, our keynote speaker, Lucas Kello, will give us his view on how the digital future may appear in the light of evolving cyberthreats. The cyberthreats are here to stay and we must continually adapt to the changing landscape of technology, threats, and actors. Your participation at this conference today is a first step in this adaptive direction. Thank you. Now, it gives me great pleasure to introduce to you our moderator, Chris Skinner. Chris is known as an independent commentator on the financial markets and is the Chair of the European networking forum The Financial Services Club, and Chair of Nordic Finance Innovation. We are very pleased that Chris is with us today, so without further ado  Chris, the floor is yours! Side 3 af 3

Title: Speech at the Danish Bankers Association's annual meeting
text: Nils Bernstein Speech at the Danish Bankers Association's annual meeting on 30 November 2005 Thanks for the invitation. And by the way, thank you for the kind reception I have met from the financial institutions. Let me make it clear at once that I will continue my predecessor's line on monetary and monetary policy. It is a policy that has served Denmark well. I've been with it for so long that I remember the time we used exchange rate adjustments actively to solve our structural problems. As you know, this led to double-digit inflation rates and an interest rate level of over 20 per cent. In the end, everyone could see that this policy was untenable. Today, the focus is rarely on fixed exchange rate policy. It is considered unfashionable outside the country's borders. Nevertheless, it has been important for Denmark. It has had broad political support and contributed to very low inflation, probably in practice so low that it no longer occupies the population in everyday life. Over the past 15 years, price increases have been kept at around 2 per cent a year on average. And if we look at store prices, in recent years they have been completely at rest. This real wage protection is something that we all enjoy on a day-to-day basis. At the same time, companies can more easily plan with a fixed exchange rate of euros. The basis of their investments is not abruptly changed, because the exchange rate changes. Companies know that it is especially up to them to cope with the demands of the future through the development of products and employees. The lower inflation rate is not only a Danish phenomenon, but is also seen globally. The increasing participation of Asian countries in the world economy has a price- and wage-dampening effect on the rest of the world. It also rubs off on long-term interest rates. Since the global investment appetite is less than usual, and since both central banks and pension institutions are currently buying long-term bonds for large amounts, long-term interest rates are at the lowest level in the post-war period. These impacts will wear off sooner or later  when we don't know  but when that happens, the consequence will be higher interest rates. ---o0o--- 2 Economic policy in this country has for a number of years had broad political support. In fact, the Danish "model" is increasingly seen as a role model for other countries. It is especially the conditions in the labor market that are of interest. How flexibility and social security can go hand in hand. What we are seeing now is the result of many years of development of the Danish model. It's a process that will never be finished. Good reforms are well thought out, and they must take the time they take. Ideas need to mature to build support for the reforms. The process is important to reach a good result. The fixed exchange rate policy means that the level of the Danish interest rate is generally determined abroad. On the other hand, this also means that it does not always correspond to Danish needs. In practice, it hasn't been a problem. Fiscal policy has been adjusted to avoid both overheating and high unemployment. With a forward-looking and reform-oriented policy, one can usually settle for minor corrections to the course of the annual budget bill. On the other hand, it is important that long-term goals are constantly being targeted. In this context, the experience of other countries may be useful. The Netherlands is currently struggling to emerge from a self-created recession. Favourable economic development in the late 90s brought with it large surpluses in public finances. Part of the profits were spent, including on tax cuts, and the economy boiled over. But it wasn't until late in the process that the consequences showed. Wages soared, as did unemployment, and public finances suddenly showed a large deficit. You had to tighten up in the midst of a recession that you only now seem to be getting out of. The clear lesson is that one should not use the profits when things are going well, and especially not if there is a shadow of a risk that the competitiveness of companies will be harmed. The economic development in Denmark has been favourable in recent years. First and foremost, there is reason to rejoice. Unemployment has fallen and is now at a low level, private consumption is advancing by seven miles, yet we have a surplus in the balance of payments while the money flows into the treasury. It's almost too good to be true  and there's reason to be cautious. Demand remains strong  perhaps a little too strong. It's not something we know for sure. On the other hand, we are sure that the day we know it is going too fast, we have some unpleasant years ahead. Then it is too late to correct the course without significant costs. The challenge today is to ensure the balance that makes it possible to bring unemployment down even further than today. We should like to have some more of society's weakest in continuous work  and we will not reach that if we get overheating. 3 Therefore, it is not only in traffic, but also in economic policy, that one must respect the speed limits. Violations of the economic speed limits are punished more severely than with a clip in the driver's license. Currently, this means that there is no room for any kind of easing, either on the revenue or expenditure side, quite the opposite. The spending policy objectives of the state and municipalities must be respected, and the cyclical situation is not for unfunded tax cuts. As the Dutch experience so clearly states: During a boom, economic policy should not contribute to accelerating development further. ---o0o--- Many of the major European countries are struggling with a bad economy. The high unemployment rate creates uncertainty. The recognition of the need to create greater flexibility in the labour market is growing. But the reforms so far are small. A main problem in Italy, France and Germany is that companies invest too little on their home turf, and since households are not much in favour of opening up their wallets, all that remains is to wait for an export-driven recovery. We could wish for a consumption-driven recovery in Europe. But this assumes that households will and can spend more. But at the same time, it must be noted that the financial sector in many of the countries is not really geared to finance households' wishes for consumption or housing. Banks have been geared up for household savings to finance corporate investments, not to lend money to households. In Denmark, lending by banks and mortgage banks to households is about the size of production. In Italy, which is the other extreme in the EU, households have borrowed only a quarter through these market channels, but probably more if loans from the family are taken with them. However, the market channels are important if you do not want family relations to be the central point when young people have to buy their own home or car or simply distribute consumption rationally over life. The very high Danish figures for household borrowing reflect in particular that homeowners can borrow on the capital market via mortgage credit. It's a good thing, but not without reservations. New forms of borrowing, also on the books of financial institutions, have probably contributed to the very strong increases in house prices. Most of the increase, however, must be attributed to the low interest rate, the growth of real incomes and the frozen property value tax. Thus, there is no question of an inexplicable bubble in prices, but prices can fall when interest rates one day rise. 4 These are good times for the banks, and lending is growing. It is also in good times that losses are seen as something that was a thing of the past and that credit quality can go down. Not in its own bank, but with competitors. The banks are currently doing considerable work to incorporate the new international accounting rules and the future capital adequacy rules  Basel II. It requires a lot of resources. At the same time, it is an important task so that the individual financial institution can decide on the need for buffers to stand against bad times. Also in other parts of the financial field, a lot of effort has been spent on new legislation and its implementation. The Commission has now indicated that the legislation is essentially in place in the financial field. Now it is time to make the single market for financial services work. The Danish Monetary Fund is conducting a review of the entire financial system in Denmark, under the so-called Financial Sector Assessment Program  FSAP. Let's consider it a good opportunity to have a service. It is useful to look at whether we have adapted ourselves in the best possible way according to international standards. The IMF has just completed a 14-day visit to the country. I would like to thank you for the efforts of the members of the Danish Bankers Association and a large number of the other players in the financial system in connection with the visit. FSAP is a long process and there is still a lot to work on in the coming months. The Danish Monetary Fund's final assessment with recommendations for Denmark is expected to be available in mid-next year. Bodil (Nyboe Andersen) has asked me to thank you for good cooperation not only last year, but for a number of years. I would like to do this and at the same time wish that the good cooperation can continue in the years to come.

Title: Danish competitiveness in a globalized world. National Committee for Operating Economics
text: Nils Bernstein National Committee for Operating Economics, 30 November 2006 d0 Danish competitiveness in a globalised world Thank you for the invitation to speak today. I think the last time I spoke in this circle, it was about fertilizer plans. Today I want to say something about "Danish competitiveness in a globalized world". Globalization is one of the hot topics of the time. It fills in the media picture and on the political agenda. Companies think it into their strategic planning. And for many wage earners, it creates new challenges, but also brings increased prosperity. Globalization, understood as the fact that the earth has become smaller, is not a new phenomenon. The trend of ever-increasing movement of goods, services, people, capital and information across national borders and continents has been going on for centuries. Several conditions have played a major role in the process. (slide 2). Technological development is probably the most decisive driver. In recent centuries, there have been a number of technological advances that have made the world "smaller". Better means of transport and communication means that almost everything today can be transported from one end of the world to the other much faster and cheaper than before. Something has happened in leaps and bounds, others gradually. Institutions that help secure open borders are also important. If all countries were as closed as North Korea, it would not be possible to take advantage of the so-called comparative advantages, i.e. to do what we do best. Knowledge and technology would not be spread. This is one of the reasons why organisations such as the WTO, the EU and the UN are important. Finally, it is crucial that there are no obstacles to globalisation in the form of, for example, wars. Not least World War II beat back globalization. The fear of terror has the same elements in it. Commodity trade was the area that first gained great importance. The share of foreign trade in GDP here in Denmark is thus today no greater than it was 100 years ago. (slide 3). Agriculture's transition to animal production at the end of the 19th century, when cheap and better grain from the United States, among others, outcompeted- 2 The Danish was in fact a successful result of globalization. The use of the centrifug in dairy farming came at the right time. The development has gone in waves. Over the past decade, it's as if the process has been on an upward wave. This is due to a number of factors, and let me point out a few of the most significant. The fall of the Iron Curtain and China's market economy opening have provided access to new large markets and a large and cheap labor resource. In addition, the development of IT technology has made it possible to move information from one end of the world to the other in a matter of seconds at very low prices. With the liberalization of capital movements in the 80s, completely new conditions have been created for the financial markets. All in all, the changes have created an ocean of new opportunities for many companies, such as outsourcing production and trading services across national borders. But how is Denmark positioned in the increasingly global world economy? Can we even keep our welfare society together when competition from low-wage countries intensifies? With the entry of China and India into the global economy, the workforce has increased by 2 billion people working for very low wages. Initially, we can state that things are immediately going well. Denmark is today one of the world's most prosperous countries. Also when we correct that the price levels are different from country to country, i.e. that the purchasing power of DKK 1 is not the same, Denmark comes out as one of the countries with the highest income per capita. (slide 4). A few of the countries we normally compare ourselves to are higher than us, but most are lower. And countries like China and India, despite their rapid growth, are still far behind. We can even rejoice that the Danish economy is currently in a strong recovery d0 perhaps a little too strong for Danmarks Nationalbank's taste, but that is another story. (slide 5). Employment is growing, unemployment is at its lowest level in 30 years, and in many industries there is a pronounced shortage of available hands. At the same time, companies have good earnings, employees have a steady increase in real wages, and Denmark has a large surplus on the balance of payments. So there is little evidence that globalisation has put pressure on the Danish economy d0 quite the opposite. Of course, there are many companies that have had to restructure, curtail and perhaps even close under the increasing competitive pressure from outside, but at the same time new companies have emerged that take advantage of the opportunities in the global marketplace. Before the euphoria takes over, it must be remembered that the Danish economy in these years is favored by special conditions. The large increase in property and land prices in recent years has increased wealth and helped boost consumption and investment. In addition, oil and gas production in these years is large. (slide 6). This has meant that Denmark as a whole has earned the mean- 3 On the rising oil prices. (slide 7). It is unknown how much oil is hiding in our underground, but that the gains are temporary is indisputable, and it is likely that the contribution to the country's economy will soon begin to wane. That is why it is so important that the large extraordinary revenues from the North Sea that the state has in these years are used to pay off debts and are not used for ongoing operations. The benefits of our underground values are thus spread over several generations. Even when the special conditions from the property market and energy are taken into account, however, it is difficult to reach any other conclusion than that Denmark has a good competitiveness. We are doing well and benefiting from globalisation. For some, economic success is a paradox in the light of various characteristics of the Danish economy. First, the public sector is large. (slide 8). The public spending pressure is higher than in all other (Western) countries d0 and our tax burden is only surpassed by the Swedes d0 for as long as it lasts. Over the years, many have argued that the large public sector takes up a large part of the total resources, so it hampers the private sector's opportunities for the development. And the tax burden is highlighted as inhibiting initiative and enthusiasm. Secondly, the income distribution in Denmark is smoother than in other countries. (slide 9). And whereas from 1980 to 2000 there was an international trend of rising income inequality, inequality d0 albeit only slightly d0 declined at home. The increase in income that has been achieved over the past decades has not only benefited a few, but has been spread widely across the Danish population. One may come across the view that an even distribution of income helps to dampen initiative and enthusiasm. Third, our labor costs are among the highest in the world. (slide 10). International figures show that today only Norway has higher labour costs than us. And the difference between labor costs in Denmark and abroad has even grown in the last 10 years. Some might be inclined to compare the Danish economy to a bumblebee that, as you know, should not be able to fly? One fact that is sometimes highlighted in the debate is that the Danish growth in gross domestic product in the last 10-15 years has not been impressive by international standards. That's true d0 but it's not necessarily an indication that we've done worse than others. Our relatively low economic growth is linked to two factors: demographics and productivity. In Denmark, the working-age population has increased less than in other countries, such as the United States. A smaller approach to the labour market leads to lower growth without reflecting poorer economic development. After all, there are fewer to share the result. 4 With productivity, it is more complex. So what do we get out of a given effort. As economists, we are often inclined to argue that high productivity growth is an expression of strength and low productivity growth of weakness. However, this assumes that the difference in productivity is not matched by a decrease in the price of production with high productivity growth compared to production with low productivity growth. In the past decade, however, that is very much what has happened. Finland and Sweden have a large IT production and have been characterized by high productivity growth. But effective international competition has led to the fact that prices for IT production have simultaneously fallen. In Denmark, IT production is quite modest, and Danish companies have generally not experienced similar price drops. The difference is reflected in the ratio of exchange, that is, an index of the ratio of export and import prices. (slide 11). In Finland and Sweden, the exchange ratio has decreased, while it has increased in Denmark. So you don't necessarily get rich from high productivity growth, but it may be necessary to survive. I think that in agriculture you are the ones who know this phenomenon best. In order to get a more accurate picture, GDP growth rates should be corrected for differences in terms of trade. If this is done, you see that Denmark has done quite well compared to Sweden and Finland. (slide 12). Competitiveness has many dimensions. In the past, there was a tendency to focus especially on wage competitiveness. Salary is still an essential parameter, but developments have shown that it cannot stand alone. Various organizations draw up some broader inventories of competitiveness. They seek to include a wide range of the framework conditions that affect the competitiveness of companies. These are not perfect goals, but they deserve attention because they take a broader perspective on competitiveness. A common characteristic of these statements is that Denmark is positioned as a country with a very good competitiveness. An example is the Economist Intelligence Unit, which for the past two years has ranked the Danish economy as the most competitive in the world. Another is the World Economic Forum's Global Competitiveness Indicator. In the autumn, Denmark was ranked No. 4 in the global rankings. (slide 13). In front of us were only two Nordic countries, Sweden and Finland, as well as Switzerland. The three Nordic countries are thus giving back to not only the United States and our EU partners, but even more so to countries such as China and India. It invites to take a closer look at what gives the good location. (slide 14). The indicator is made up of over 100 sub-indicators, which are collected into 9 categories, which in turn are grouped into three main groups. 5 With the large number of indicators, it is not 100 that Denmark is ranked in the international top. Denmark belongs to the top 10 in all 9 categories, so the absence of decidedly weak areas is part of the explanation. (slide 15). If you study the many indicators, three positions of strength emerge: First, Denmark d0 compared to other countries d0 has effective institutions. Corruption and crime are low. Our legal system is well functioning. Private property rights are respected. Our politicians are considered reliable. And the public sector is efficient. It can be said that we have a well-developed social capital. I will make no secret of the fact that it pleases an old bureaucrat. It is often overlooked how much good institutions mean for the development of a market economy. Secondly, the Danish economy is strong. A number of oil countries are ranked better than Denmark in the report, but only a few countries among the 20 most competitive have better economic ratios. Inflation and interest rates are low, and there are surpluses in public finances. It creates a stable framework where companies and employees can concentrate on producing and developing without worrying about tomorrow bringing unexpected bills. And thirdly, Denmark is well placed in a number of areas where the public sector is a major producer. The health status of the Danish population is generally good d0 although our average lifespan continues to lag slightly behind the other Nordic countries, among others. Our education system, including continuing education, is assessed positively. One of the factors that draws up is that a relatively large proportion of the population gets a higher education. (slide 16). Finally, the infrastructure, which includes, inter alia, transport, electricity, water and waste, is considered to be well-functioning.
