So to put it simplistically, you could say that we may have a large public sector, but it also contributes positively to our competitiveness in a number of areas. The focus is often on Denmark's high tax burden, and this also drags down the competitiveness of the World Economic Forum's statement. There is little doubt that our tax burden in isolation negatively affects the economy, first and foremost the supply of labour through the high marginal taxes. A recent OECD analysis indicates that the higher the marginal tax, the lower the average working hours. (slide 17). On the other hand, there is no evidence that the tax burden significantly discourages people from being in the labour market. The Danish participation in the labour market is thus among the highest. (slide 18). The statement from the World Economic Forum shows that one must be careful to focus unilaterally on the tax burden. Significant parts of public activity support the country's competitiveness and contribute to making our institutions more efficient. It is also worth noting that both Finland and Sweden, which, as mentioned, are ahead of us in the rankings, also have large public sectors. 6 When Denmark is ranked as a highly competitive country, it does not mean that we are among the most competitive in all areas. Danish wages are high and must therefore be accompanied by a correspondingly high productivity. In line with rising real wages, as well as political and technological changes, a number of companies, especially in the manufacturing industry, have moved production to countries with a much lower wage level. This has been a contributing factor to the fact that the share of manufacturing companies in employment has declined over the past 10 years. (slide 19). This is a development that naturally entails costs for, among other things, the individual employee who has to find a new job. Most often, fortunately, it goes pretty quickly. Thus, in the past decade, the private service industries have absorbed all the labor that has been turned over from industry and agriculture. Socio-economically, it gives a gain because we move labour into professions where earnings are higher. Especially in the past, there were often political demands for support for professions in decline. When the support was given, it typically only led to the "torment being dragged on". The profession ended up having to curtail anyway. The state had wasted some money, and the competitiveness of the professions had been weakened, if anything, because a necessary transformation had been delayed. An example of transformation is seen in the manufacturing sector. In 1970, the garment industry was far larger than the pharmaceutical industry d0 both in terms of employment and value added. (slide 20). Today, it's just the opposite. A low-productive profession has constrained, while a highly productive profession has expanded. The development of the clothing industry, by the way, is interesting. The industry has by no means disappeared from the Danish map. (slide 21). Foreign trade in textiles was as large as ever last year, despite the fact that production has fallen. It reflects the fact that companies in the garment industry are trying to "skim the cream": they concentrate their efforts where the remuneration is greatest, and today this is primarily in the field of design and business management. A competitive market economy relies on having a flexible workforce, which, as the economic environment changes, finds from occupations in decline to occupations in upswing. We're pretty well off there. Turnover in the job market in Denmark is internationally high. (slide 22). This reflects, among other things, that job protection in Denmark is less than in many of the other EU countries. In turn, there is a widely accepted social safety net. The increasing importance of service industries for the Danish economy can be seen in service exports, which have grown rapidly over the past 10 years. (slide 23). The reason for the abrupt increase is not only organic growth. Favourable freight rates in maritime transport and acquisitions of foreign shipping companies have pulled in the same direction. 7 There are many indications that the very high freight rates have been a transient phenomenon. Cross-border business transactions, on the other hand, are not. Danish companies are acquired by foreign companies, and foreign companies are acquired by Danish ones. It's part of globalization. It is hardly a coincidence that companies such as Maersk and Danske Bank, but also Danish agriculture, have expanded abroad in recent years. In addition to good business acumen, it is about utilizing strong competencies, and this often includes logistics and the ability to manage complex processes. Danish companies are well placed in the global competition today. If we will also stand well tomorrow, we cannot rest on our laurels. In the spring, the government presented a major globalisation plan with a wide range of initiatives. They must ensure that Denmark also in the future has a strong competitive and cohesive cohesion, so that we can maintain our position as one of the world's most prosperous societies without major divisions between rich and poor. The plan identifies four focus areas: (slide 24) ? World-class ? education Strong and innovative research ? More growth entrepreneurs ? Transformation and renewal The education area must be strengthened from the start of primary school over secondary education and higher education to adult and continuing education. Research and innovation must be promoted through a combination of greater resources and increased competition. The challenges are vast and diverse. But if we maintain many years of good Danish tradition of facing the problems instead of sticking our heads in the bush, Denmark will continue to be able to benefit from the development of the global economy.
text_original: Nils Bernstein Landsudvalget for driftskonomi, 30. november 2006  Dansk konkurrenceevne i en globaliseret verden Tak for invitationen til at tale i dag. Jeg tror, sidst jeg talte i denne kreds, var det om gdningsplaner. Jeg vil i dag sige noget om "Dansk konkurrenceevne i en globaliseret verden". Globalisering er et af tidens varme emner. Det fylder i mediebilledet og p den politiske dagsorden. Virksomhederne tnker det ind i deres strategiske planlgning. Og for mange lnmodtagere skaber det nye udfordringer, men bringer ogs get velstand. Globalisering forstet som, at jorden er blevet mindre, er ikke et nyt fnomen. Tendensen til stadigt stigende bevgelse af varer, tjenester, mennesker, kapital og informationer p tvrs af landegrnser og kontinenter har stet p i rhundreder. Flere forhold har spillet en stor rolle for processen. (slide 2). Den teknologiske udvikling er vel nok den mest afgrende drivkraft. De seneste rhundreder er der sket en rkke teknologiske landvindinger, som har gjort verden "mindre". Bedre transport- og kommunikationsmidler gr, at nsten alt i dag kan transporteres fra den ene ende af verden til den anden langt hurtigere og billigere end tidligere. Noget er sket i spring  andet gradvist. Ogs institutioner, der medvirker til at sikre bne grnser, har stor betydning. Hvis alle lande var s lukkede som Nordkorea, ville det ikke vre muligt at udnytte de skaldte komparative fordele, dvs. at lave det, vi er bedst til. Viden og teknologi ville ikke blive spredt. Det er bl.a. derfor, at organisationer som WTO, EU og FN er vigtige. Endelig er det afgrende, at der ikke lgges forhindringer i vejen for globalisering i form af eksempelvis krige. Ikke mindst 2. verdenskrig slog globaliseringen tilbage. Frygten for terror har samme elementer i sig. Varehandel var det omrde, der frst fik stor betydning. Udenrigshandelens andel af BNP her i Danmark er sledes i dag ikke strre, end den var for 100 r siden. (slide 3). Landbrugets omstilling til animalsk produktion i slutningen af det 19. rhundrede, da billigt og bedre korn fra bl.a. USA udkonkur- 2 rerede det danske, var i virkeligheden et vellykket resultat af globalisering. Anvendelsen af centrifugen i mejeribruget kom p det rigtige tidspunkt. Udviklingen er get i blger. I det seneste rti er det som om, processen har vret p en opadgende blge. Det skyldes en rkke forhold, og lad mig pege p et par af de vsentligste. Jerntppets fald og Kinas markedskonomiske bning har givet adgang til nye store markeder og en stor og billig arbejdskraftresurse. Dertil kommer, at it-teknologiens udvikling har gjort det muligt at flytte information fra den ene ende af verden til den anden i lbet af sekunder til meget lave priser. Med liberaliseringen af kapitalbevgelserne i 80'erne er der skabt helt nye vilkr for de finansielle markeder. Alt i alt har ndringerne skabt et ocean af nye muligheder for mange virksomheder, fx outsourcing af produktion og handel med tjenester over landegrnser. Men hvordan er Danmark placeret i den stadigt mere globale verdenskonomi? Kan vi overhovedet holde sammen p vores velfrdssamfund, nr konkurrencen fra lavtlnslande skrpes? Med Kinas og Indiens indtrden i den globale konomi er arbejdsstyrken get med 2 milliarder mennesker, som arbejder for en meget lav ln. Indledningsvist kan vi konstatere, at det umiddelbart gr godt. Danmark er i dag et af verdens mest velstende lande. Ogs nr vi korrigerer for, at prisniveauerne er forskellige fra land til land, dvs. at kbekraften af 1 kr. ikke er den samme, kommer Danmark ud som et af de lande, der har den hjeste indkomst pr. indbygger. (slide 4). Enkelte af de lande, vi normalt sammenligner os med, ligger hjere end os, men de fleste ligger lavere. Og lande som Kina og Indien er  trods deres rivende vkst  stadig langt bagefter. Vi kan oven i kbet glde os over, at dansk konomi i disse r befinder sig i et kraftigt opsving  mske lidt for kraftigt efter Nationalbankens smag, men det er en anden historie. (slide 5). Beskftigelsen er i vkst, arbejdslsheden er p det laveste niveau i 30 r, og i mange brancher er der en udtalt mangel p ledige hnder. Samtidig har virksomhederne en god indtjening, lnmodtagerne en stabil fremgang i reallnnen, og Danmark har et stort overskud p betalingsbalancen. S der er ikke meget, der tyder p, at globaliseringen har sat dansk konomi under pres  snarere tvrtimod. Der er naturligvis mange virksomheder, der har mttet omstrukturere, indskrnke og mske endog lukke under det stigende konkurrencepres udefra, men samtidig er der dukket nye virksomheder op, som udnytter mulighederne p den globale markedsplads. Inden euforien tager overhnd skal man huske, at den danske konomi i disse r er begunstiget af srlige forhold. De senere rs store stigning i ejendoms- og jordpriser har get formuerne og vret med til at stte skub i forbrug og investeringer. Dertil kommer, at olie- og gasproduktionen i disse r er stor. (slide 6). Det har betydet, at Danmark som helhed har tjent betyde- 3 ligt p de stigende oliepriser. (slide 7). Det er uvist, hvor meget olie, der gemmer sig i vores undergrund, men at gevinsten er midlertidig er uomtvisteligt, og det er sandsynligt, at bidraget til landets konomi inden lnge vil begynde at aftage. Det er derfor, at det er s vigtigt, at de store ekstraordinre indtgter fra Nordsen, som staten har i disse r, bruges til at afdrage gld og ikke anvendes til lbende drift. Udbyttet af vore vrdier i undergrunden bliver p den mde spredt over flere generationer. Selv nr der tages hjde for de srlige forhold fra ejendomsmarked og energi er det dog svrt at n til anden konklusion end, at Danmark har en god konkurrenceevne. Vi klarer os godt og drager fordel af globaliseringen. For nogle er den konomiske succes et paradoks i lyset af forskellige srtrk ved dansk konomi. For det frste er den offentlige sektor stor. (slide 8). Det offentlige udgiftstryk er hjere end i alle andre (vestlige) lande  og vores skattetryk overgs kun af svenskerne  s lnge det varer. Mange har gennem rene argumenteret, at den store offentlige sektor lgger beslag p en stor del af de samlede resurser, s det hmmer de private erhvervs udfoldelsesmuligheder. Og skattetrykket bliver fremhvet som hmmende for initiativ og virkelyst. For det andet er indkomstfordelingen i Danmark jvnere end i andre lande. (slide 9). Og hvor der fra 1980 til 2000 var en international tendens til stigende indkomstulighed, faldt uligheden  om end kun svagt  herhjemme. Den indkomstfremgang, der er opnet over de seneste rtier, er alts ikke kun kommet et ftal til gode, men er blevet spredt bredt ud over den danske befolkning. Man kan stde p den opfattelse, at en jvn indkomstfordeling er med til at dmpe initiativ og virkelyst. For det tredje er vores lnomkostninger blandt de hjeste i verden. (slide 10). Internationale opgrelser viser, at det i dag kun er Norge, der har hjere lnomkostninger end os. Og forskellen mellem lnomkostningerne i Danmark og i udlandet er endda vokset i de sidste 10 r. Nogle vil mske vre tilbjelige til at sammenligne dansk konomi med en humlebi, der som bekendt ikke skulle kunne flyve? Et forhold, som ind imellem bliver fremhvet i debatten, er, at den danske vkst i bruttonationalproduktet i de sidste 10-15 r ikke har vret imponerende efter international mlestok. Det er rigtigt  men det er ikke ndvendigvis et udtryk for, at vi har klaret os drligere end andre. Vores relativt lave konomiske vkst hnger sammen med to forhold: Demografi og produktivitet. I Danmark er befolkningen i den arbejdsdygtige alder steget mindre end i andre lande, fx USA. En mindre tilgang til arbejdsmarkedet giver lavere vkst, uden at det er udtryk for en ringere konomisk udvikling. Der er jo frre til at dele resultatet. 4 Med produktivitet er det mere komplekst. Alts hvad fr vi ud af en given indsats. Som konomer er vi ofte tilbjelige til at argumentere, at en hj produktivitetsvkst er udtryk for styrke og en lav produktivitetsvkst for svaghed. Det forudstter imidlertid, at produktivitetsforskellen ikke modsvares af et fald i prisen p produktion med hj produktivitetsvkst i forhold til produktionen med lav produktivitetsvkst. I det seneste rti er det imidlertid i hj grad det, der er sket. Finland og Sverige har en stor itproduktion og har vret kendetegnet ved hj produktivitetsvkst. Men en effektiv international konkurrence har frt til, at priserne p it-produktion samtidig er faldet. I Danmark er it-produktionen ret beskeden, og danske virksomheder har gennemgende ikke oplevet lignende prisfald. Forskellen afspejles i bytteforholdet, dvs. et indeks for forholdet mellem eksport- og importpriser. (slide 11). I Finland og Sverige er bytteforholdet faldet, mens det er steget i Danmark. Man bliver alts ikke ndvendigvis rig af en hj produktivitetsvkst, men den kan vre ndvendig for at overleve. Jeg tror, at I i landbruget er dem, der bedst kender til dette fnomen. For at f et mere retvisende billede br BNP-vkstraterne korrigeres for forskelle i bytteforhold. Gres det, ser man, at Danmark har klaret sig ganske udmrket sammenlignet med Sverige og Finland. (slide 12). Konkurrenceevne har mange dimensioner. Tidligere var der en tendens til isr at fokusere p lnkonkurrenceevne. Ln er stadig en vsentlig parameter, men udviklingen har vist, at den ikke kan st alene. Forskellige organisationer udarbejder nogle bredere opgrelser af konkurrenceevnen. De forsger at inddrage en lang rkke af de rammevilkr, som har betydning for virksomheders konkurrenceevne. Det er ikke perfekte ml, men de fortjener opmrksomhed, fordi de tager et bredere perspektiv p konkurrenceevne. Et flles kendetegn ved disse opgrelser er, at Danmark er placeret som et land med en rigtig god konkurrenceevne. Et eksempel er Economist Intelligence Unit, der de seneste to r har rangeret dansk konomi som den mest konkurrencedygtige i verden. Et andet er World Economic Forums Global Competitiveness Indicator. Her blev Danmark i efterret placeret som nr. 4 p den globale rangliste. (slide 13). Foran os var kun to nordiske lande, Sverige og Finland, samt Svejts. De tre nordiske lande giver sledes baghjul til ikke blot USA og vores EUpartnere, men i endnu hjere grad til lande som Kina og Indien. Det indbyder til at se nrmere p, hvad der giver den gode placering. (slide 14). Indikatoren er opbygget af over 100 delindikatorer, som er samlet i 9 kategorier, der igen er samlet i tre hovedgrupper. 5 Med det store antal af indikatorer kan man ikke udpege enkeltstende rsager til, at Danmark rangeres i den internationale top. Danmark tilhrer top10 i alle 9 kategorier, s fravret af decideret svage omrder er en del af forklaringen. (slide 15). Hvis man studerer de mange indikatorer, tegner der sig tre styrkepositioner: For det frste har Danmark  sammenlignet med andre lande  effektive institutioner. Korruptionen og kriminaliteten er lav. Vores retssystem er velfungerende. Den private ejendomsret respekteres. Vores politikere betragtes som plidelige. Og den offentlige sektor er effektiv. Man kan sige, at vi har en veludviklet social kapital. Jeg vil ikke lgge skjul p, at det glder en gammel bureaukrat. Det overses ofte, hvor meget gode institutioner betyder for udviklingen af en markedskonomi. For det andet er dansk konomi strk. En rkke olielande rangeres ganske vist bedre end Danmark i opgrelsen, men kun enkelte lande blandt de 20 mest konkurrencedygtige har bedre konomiske ngletal. Inflation og rente er lav, og der er overskud p de offentlige finanser. Det skaber en stabil ramme, hvor virksomheder og lnmodtagere kan koncentrere sig om at producere og udvikle uden bekymring for, om morgendagen bringer uventede regninger. Og for det tredje er Danmark godt placeret p en rkke omrder, hvor den offentlige sektor er storproducent. Den danske befolknings sundhedstilstand er gennemgende god  om end vores gennemsnitlige levetid fortsat halter lidt efter bl.a. de vrige nordiske lande. Vores uddannelsessystem, inkl. efteruddannelsen, vurderes positivt. Et af de forhold, der trkker op, er, at en relativt stor andel af befolkningen fr en videregende uddannelse. (slide 16). Endeligt anses infrastrukturen, som omfatter bl.a. transport, el, vand og affald, for velfungerende. S sagt lidt forenklet kan man sige, at nok har vi en stor offentlig sektor, men den bidrager ogs p en rkke omrder positivt til vores konkurrenceevne. Der fokuseres ofte p Danmarks hje skattetryk, og det trkker da ogs ned i konkurrenceevnen i World Economic Forums opgrelse. Der er nppe tvivl om, at vores skattetryk isoleret set pvirker konomien negativt, frst og fremmest arbejdsudbuddet gennem de hje marginalskatter. En nylig OECD-analyse indikerer, at jo hjere marginalskat, des lavere gennemsnitlig arbejdstid. (slide 17). Til gengld er der ikke tegn p, at skattetrykket i nvnevrdigt omfang afholder folk fra at vre p arbejdsmarkedet. Den danske erhvervsdeltagelse hrer sledes til blandt de hjeste. (slide 18). Opgrelsen fra World Economic Forum viser, at man skal passe p ensidigt at fokusere p skattetrykket. Vsentlige dele af den offentlige aktivitet understtter landets konkurrenceevne og bidrager til at gre vores institutioner mere effektive. Det er da ogs vrd at bemrke, at bde Finland og Sverige, der som nvnt ligger foran os p ranglisten, ogs har store offentlige sektorer. 6 Nr Danmark rangeres som et srdeles konkurrencedygtigt land, er det ikke ensbetydende med, at vi p alle omrder er blandt de mest konkurrencedygtige. De danske lnninger er hje og m derfor ledsages af en tilsvarende hj produktivitet. I takt med den stigende realln samt de politiske og teknologiske ndringer har en rkke virksomheder, isr i fremstillingsindustrien, flyttet produktion til lande med et langt lavere lnniveau. Det har vret en medvirkende rsag til, at fremstillingsvirksomhedernes andel af beskftigelsen er aftaget de seneste 10 r. (slide 19). Det er en udvikling, som naturligvis indebrer omkostninger for bl.a. den enkelte lnmodtager, som skal finde nyt job. Oftest gr det heldigvis ret hurtigt. I det seneste rti har de private serviceerhverv sledes opsuget al den arbejdskraft, der er blevet til overs fra industri og landbrug. Samfundskonomisk giver det en gevinst, fordi vi flytter arbejdskraft over i erhverv, hvor indtjeningen er hjere. Isr tidligere var der ofte politiske krav om sttte til erhverv i tilbagegang. Nr sttten blev givet, frte det typisk alene til, at "pinen blev trukket i langdrag". Erhvervet endte alligevel med at mtte indskrnke. Staten havde spildt nogle penge, og erhvervenes konkurrenceevne var om noget blevet svkket, fordi en ndvendig omstilling var blevet forsinket. Et eksempel p omstilling ses inden for fremstillingssektoren. I 1970 var bekldningsindustrien langt strre end medicinalindustrien  bde mlt ved beskftigelse og vrditilvkst. (slide 20). I dag forholder det sig lige omvendt. Et lavproduktivt erhverv har indskrnket, mens et hjproduktivt erhverv har ekspanderet. Udviklingen i bekldningsindustrien er i vrigt interessant. Industrien er p ingen mde forsvundet fra det danske landkort. (slide 21). Udenrigshandelen med tekstiler var sidste r s stor som nogensinde fr p trods af, at produktionen er faldet. Det afspejler, at virksomhederne i bekldningsbranchen forsger at "skumme flden": De koncentrerer deres indsats, hvor aflnningen er strst, og det er i dag primrt inden for design og forretningsstyring. En konkurrencedygtig markedskonomi er afhngig af at have en fleksibel arbejdsstyrke, som i takt med, at de konomiske rammer ndres, finder fra erhverv i nedgang til erhverv i opgang. Der er vi ret godt stillet. Omstningen p jobmarkedet i Danmark er internationalt set hj. (slide 22). Det afspejler bl.a., at jobbeskyttelsen herhjemme er mindre end i mange af de vrige EU-lande. Til gengld er der et bredt accepteret socialt sikkerhedsnet. Tjenesteerhvervenes stigende betydning for dansk konomi ses i tjenesteeksporten, der er vokset hastigt i de seneste 10 r. (slide 23). Baggrunden for den bratte stigning er ikke kun organisk vkst. Gunstige fragtrater inden for stransport og opkb af udenlandske rederier har trukket i samme retning. 7 Meget tyder p, at de meget hje fragtrater har vret et forbigende fnomen. Det er grnseoverskridende virksomhedshandler til gengld ikke. Danske virksomheder opkbes af udenlandske, og udenlandske opkbes af danske. Det er en del af globaliseringen. Det er nppe tilfldigt, at selskaber som Mrsk og Danske Bank, men smnd ogs dansk landbrug, i de senere r har ekspanderet i udlandet. Ud over godt kbmandskab handler det om at udnytte strke kompetencer, og til det hrer ofte logistik og evnen til at styre komplekse processer. Danske virksomheder str godt i den globale konkurrence i dag. Hvis vi ogs vil st godt i morgen, kan vi ikke hvile p laurbrrene. Regeringen fremlagde i forret en strre globaliseringsplan med en lang rkke initiativer. De skal sikre, at Danmark ogs i fremtiden har en strk konkurrence- og sammenhngskraft, s vi kan fastholde vores position som et af verdens mest velstende samfund uden store skel mellem rig og fattig. Planen udpeger fire indsatsomrder: (slide 24)  Uddannelse i verdensklasse  Strk og nyskabende forskning  Flere vkstivrksttere  Omstilling og fornyelse Uddannelsesomrdet skal styrkes fra folkeskolens start over ungdomsuddannelserne og de videregende uddannelser til voksen- og efteruddannelsen. Forskning og innovation skal fremmes gennem en kombination af strre resurser og en forstrket konkurrence. Udfordringerne er store og mangfoldige. Men hvis vi fastholder mange rs god dansk tradition for at se problemerne i jnene i stedet for at stikke hovedet i busken, vil Danmark ogs fremover kunne drage fordel af udviklingen i den globale konomi.

Title: Speech at the Danish Bankers Association's annual meeting
text: The spoken word applies Speech to the Danish Bankers Association's annual meeting 5 December 2007 Governor Nils Bernstein For several years, the global financial system has been characterized by progress and high growth in business volume. The innovation has been significant, and many new products and business concepts have been added. Earnings have been top notch. The return on equity among the largest global banks has been steadily increasing for a number of years, reaching over 20% on average in the first half of 2007. Progress halted quite abruptly within a few days during the summer holidays. It had long been known that the U.S. housing market was fragile. Losses were increasing on home loans to less creditworthy households  so-called sub-prime loans. However, the assessment was that this market did not have a size that could have an impact on global financial stability. Furthermore, the emergence of new financial instruments had apparently helped to spread the risk of loss on sub-prime loans to many different investors. This assessment did not hold true. Investment firms had invested in sub-prime loans wrapped as structured bonds. The investments were made for borrowed funds in the form of the issuance of short-term securities. It turned out that large banks were closely associated with these companies via liquidity guarantees or ownership. The risk of loss on sub-prime loans was thus also with the banks to an opaque extent. Therefore, uncertainty arose as to who ultimately bore the risk of loss on sub-prime loans. In a very short period of time, some of the most liquid markets with the highest rating came to a standstill. It became difficult to issue short-term securities, guaranteed by gold-rimmed banks. Across most of the world, banks concentrated on securing their own liquidity and were hesitant to lend excess liquidity to other banks  especially on maturities beyond a few days. Two German banks got into difficulties as a result of exposures to investment firms. A British bank was brought to its knees. Not by sub-prime loans, but because the bank's business model was based on continuous access to finance in the money and capital markets. We experienced the rare sight of seeing depositors queuing outside a bank to withdraw their deposits. It was the beginning of the liquidity crisis that has affected the money and capital markets in much of the world since July. 2 month. The central banks of the Us, the euro area and the UK periodically provide security liquidity to the market in the fourth month to stabilise short-term interest rates and improve the functioning of the money market. Considerable uncertainty remains as to the extent of the losses and their future developments. From time to time, new skeletons pour out of the closets in the form of announcements from banks about several losses on sub-prime loans. Stock prices have fallen significantly for banks exposed to sub-prime loans. Financial markets are marked by fears that the losses will spread to other parts of the U.S. home loan market. The uncertainty means that the difference between unsecured and secured money market rates on longer maturities remains abnormally large in many countries. Finally, the liquidity crisis has led banks in the euro area and the US to tighten credit conditions for several customer groups. What is the significance of the financial turmoil for Denmark? I will focus on two matters. Firstly, how has the development affected the Danish financial system? Second, what does the turmoil mean for the business cycle? At the very short end of the money market, the international financial turmoil has not limited Danish banks' willingness to lend kroner to each other. There are indications of some increase in liquidity preparedness, but there have been no signs of tensions in short-term money market rates, and Danmarks Nationalbank has not needed to conduct extraordinary refinancing operations on this occasion. Danmarks Nationalbank's normal refinancing operations take place through a so-called open window. The demand for loans and certificates of deposit is met at the interest rate set by Danmarks Nationalbank. The counterparties can thus compose their own liquidity vis-197s to Danmarks Nationalbank within a fairly broad framework. The development in the banks' balances with Danmarks Nationalbank does not indicate that liquidity preparedness has increased to a greater extent along this path. The longer unsecured money market rates in dollars have risen as a result of the international turmoil. However, the movements in the spread between unsecured and secured money market interest rates have been lower in Denmark compared to developments in the euro area and in particular the United States. Even under normal conditions, turnover in this segment of the Danish money market is relatively limited. But the rise in interest rates has of course had an impact on the wide range of financial products linked to Cibor and similar interest rates. Danish banks have from time to time had difficulty taking out loans in dollars. The phenomenon is not isolated In Danish. The same has happened to banks in other European countries. Danmarks Nationalbank cannot provide liquidity facilities to cover loan needs in foreign currencies. Role of Danmarks Nationalbank 3 relates primarily to crown liquidity. Financial institutions with significant business volume in foreign currency must themselves ensure to maintain a liquidity preparedness in the currencies in question. All in all, the Danish money market has performed relatively well during the turmoil. In the end, it reflects that the Danish financial system is in good shape. However, the international turmoil has not gone without a trace across Denmark. The accounts for the third quarter showed that the Danish banks were also engaged in investment companies, liquidity guarantees and structured bonds. However, the exposures and losses were relatively limited. Danish banks' lending has grown rapidly in recent years. In some institutes, we have seen growth rates of over 30 per cent. Earnings have been good and losses have been low. In particular, the home loans in the form of the so-called mortgages have grown significantly. Loan growth has been so strong that a large deposit deficit of more than 400 mia.kr has built up, i.e. the amount by which bank lending exceeds customers' deposits. The Danish banks are thus dependent on financing on the money and capital markets. Developments abroad over the summer have shown that it can be risky to base the business base on this kind of financing. The price of market financing can change rapidly, and markets can "dry out". The international liquidity crisis has provided an opportunity to test liquidity preparedness and look at business strategy in light of this. It is not quite as easy as before for Danish banks to finance growth via the money and capital markets. Financing has become more expensive, and the increasing financing costs for the banks will undoubtedly show up in the banks' earnings and prices to customers. Loan growth remains high, but it is declining. Some financial institutions have switched to a less aggressive business strategy and put expansion plans on hold. Others have expressed intentions to reduce exposures to international investment firms, liquidity guarantees and structured bonds due to reputational risks. Developments have shown that strategies based on double-digit growth rates cannot be easily extended. The strong growth in lending to companies carries a greater risk of losses for financial institutions. That risk is increasing, but from a very low level. You can never rule out the prospect of unpleasant surprises, but the business cycle is still good. And the accounts for the third quarter also showed that earnings remain high in the financial institutions. In general, solvency is good and write-downs are low. From this perspective, it is Danmarks Nationalbank's assessment today that the international unrest can serve as a "useful" 4 fright for the banks in Denmark. The necessary adjustments to the new conditions can be made in time without great costs for the vast majority of institutions and for the economy as a whole. What does the financial turmoil mean for the business cycle? Growth in the world economy has been unusually high in recent years. But the turmoil in the financial markets has raised concerns about the continued development. Growth has slowed in the United States, although the crisis in the US housing market and the consequent financial turmoil have not yet seriously affected the rest of the economy. The recovery looks to continue in Europe and Asia for the time being, just as the business cycle is positive in Africa and Latin America. The price of oil has risen sharply in recent months, dampening the growth outlook while increasing inflationary pressures. International organizations have so far only downgraded their growth estimates relatively modestly  with the exception of the United States, where growth in 2008 is now estimated at below 2 percent  but not recession. There is a clear concern that the uncertainty associated with financial markets and the downturn in the housing market  not just in the US  is spreading to the rest of the economy, dragging growth further down in the US and also hitting Europe. From a Danish perspective, the outlook in the sales markets remains good, albeit declining. The Danish economy is still in a strong boom with a hot labour market and capacity pressures in large parts of the economy. The unemployment rate continues to surprise positively. The tight labour market means that capacity pressures remain high despite expectations of some moderation in demand growth. The pressure has resulted in a sharp upt upt in imports and in recent quarters also in higher wage increases and in increased domestic price pressures. This reflects the fact that wages and prices usually react with a significant delay to the business cycle. A possible setback may therefore be protracted if the cost level has initially risen too high compared to abroad. The current heating of the economy involves a great risk of such a course. For the sake of fixed exchange rate policy, the level of interest rates in Denmark is aligned with the euro area, which is not as far ahead in the business cycle as Denmark. The expected rise in interest rates has recently failed to materially as a result of the turmoil in the financial markets. 5 In this situation, it will be quite remarkable if the government continues to plan an expansionary fiscal policy for 2008. In connection with the preparation of the new finance law for 2008, the government should reassess fiscal policy with the aim of taking the pressure off the economy. A postponement of this could increase the requirements at a later stage. The coming spring offers collective bargaining in the public labour market. It can be seen that public employees have created expectations of significant wage increases. The labour shortages and focus on the quality of public services in recent years have supported these expectations. Several political parties have expressed sympathy for an extraordinary salary boost for larger or smaller groups of public employees through the allocation of a special pool for this. I would strongly caution against wage negotiations in the public labour market being made a matter for the Danish Parliament in advance. The risk of political overbidding is imminent and early interference by the political parties makes a real negotiation between the parties in the public labour market impossible. A very unfortunate precedent can be set. In order for it not to be too easy, there must also be collective bargaining in the financial sector in the spring. It must be appropriate on this occasion to draw attention to the signals that the negotiations in this area can send to the rest of the labour market. With these words, I would like to end by thanking the Danish Bankers Association for a good cooperation and look forward to a continuation in the same good way.
text_original: Det talte ord glder Tale til Finansrdets rsmde 5. december 2007 Nationalbankdirektr Nils Bernstein Det globale finansielle system har gennem flere r vret prget af fremgang og hj vkst i forretningsomfanget. Innovationen har vret betydelig, og der er kommet mange nye produkter og forretningskoncepter til. Indtjeningen har vret i top. Egenkapitalforrentningen blandt de strste globale banker har vret stt stigende i en rrkke og nede over 20 pct. i gennemsnit i frste halvr af 2007. Fremgangen standsede ganske brat i lbet af nogle f dage i sommerferien. Det havde lnge vret kendt, at det amerikanske boligmarked var skrbeligt. Tabene var stigende p boligln til mindre kreditvrdige husstande  skaldte sub-prime ln. Vurderingen var imidlertid, at dette marked ikke havde en strrelse, som kunne have konsekvenser for den globale finansielle stabilitet. Endvidere havde fremkomsten af nye finansielle instrumenter tilsyneladende medvirket til at f spredt tabsrisikoen p sub-prime ln ud til mange forskellige investorer. Denne vurdering holdt ikke stik. Investeringsselskaber havde investeret i sub-prime ln indpakket som strukturerede obligationer. Investeringerne var foretaget for lnte midler i form af udstedelse af kortfristede vrdipapirer. Det viste sig, at store banker var tt forbundet med disse selskaber via likviditetsgarantier eller ejerskab. Tabsrisikoen p sub-prime ln var dermed ogs hos bankerne i et uigennemskueligt omfang. Der opstod derfor usikkerhed om, hvem der i sidste ende bar tabsrisikoen p sub-prime ln. I lbet af ganske kort tid gik nogle af de mest likvide markeder med den hjeste rating i st. Det blev svrt at udstede kortfristede vrdipapirer, garanteret af guldrandede banker. Over det meste af verden koncentrerede banker sig om at sikre egen likviditet og var tvende med at udlne overskudslikviditet til andre banker  navnlig p lbetider ud over nogle f dage. To tyske banker kom i vanskeligheder som flge af eksponeringer over for investeringsselskaber. En britisk bank blev bragt i kn. Ikke af sub-prime ln, men fordi bankens forretningsmodel var baseret p lbende adgang til finansiering p penge- og kapitalmarkederne. Vi oplevede det sjldne syn at se indskydere st i k uden for en bank for at hve deres indskud. Det var begyndelsen p den likviditetskrise, som med vekslende intensitet har prget penge- og kapitalmarkederne i en stor del af verden siden juli 2 mned. Centralbankerne i USA, euroomrdet og Storbritannien tilfrer p fjerde mned med jvne mellemrum likviditet mod sikkerhed til markedet for at stabilisere de korte renter og forbedre pengemarkedets funktion. Der hersker fortsat betydelig usikkerhed om tabenes omfang og den fremtidige udvikling heri. Fra tid til anden vlter nye skeletter ud af skabene i form af meddelelser fra banker om flere tab p sub-prime ln. Aktiekurserne er faldet betydeligt for banker, som er eksponeret over for sub-prime ln. De finansielle markeder er prget af frygt for, at tabene spreder sig til andre dele af markedet for amerikanske boligln. Usikkerheden medfrer, at forskellen mellem usikrede og sikrede pengemarkedsrenter p lngere lbetider fortsat er unormal stor i mange lande. Endelig har likviditetskrisen fet banker i euroomrdet og USA til at stramme kreditvilkrene over for flere kundegrupper. Hvilken betydning har den finansielle uro for Danmark? Jeg vil fokusere p to forhold. For det frste: hvorledes har udviklingen pvirket det danske finansielle system? For det andet: hvad betyder uroen for konjunkturerne? I den helt korte ende af pengemarkedet har den internationale finansielle uro ikke begrnset danske bankers villighed til at lne kroner ud til hinanden. Der er indikationer p en vis forgelse af likviditetsberedskabet, men der har ikke vret tegn p spndinger i de korte pengemarkedsrenter, og Nationalbanken har ikke haft behov for at gennemfre ekstraordinre markedsoperationer i den anledning. Nationalbankens normale markedsoperationer sker gennem et skaldt bent vindue. Eftersprgslen efter ln og indskudsbeviser imdekommes til den rente, som er fastsat af Nationalbanken. Modparterne kan sledes selv sammenstte deres likviditet over for Nationalbanken inden for ret vide rammer. Udviklingen i penge- og realkreditinstitutternes mellemvrender med Nationalbanken tyder ikke p, at likviditetsberedskabet er forget i strre omfang ad denne vej. De lngere usikrede pengemarkedsrenter i kroner er steget som flge af den internationale uro. Bevgelserne i spndet mellem usikrede og sikrede pengemarkedsrenter har dog vret lavere i Danmark sammenlignet med udviklingen i euroomrdet og navnlig USA. Selv under normale forhold er omstningen i dette segment af det danske pengemarked forholdsvis begrnset. Men rentestigningen har naturligvis haft betydning for den lange rkke af finansielle produkter, som er knyttet til Cibor og lignende rentesatser. Danske pengeinstitutter har fra tid til anden haft vanskeligt ved at optage ln i dollar. Fnomenet er ikke isoleret dansk. Det samme er sket for banker i andre europiske lande. Nationalbanken kan ikke stille likviditetsfaciliteter til rdighed for at dkke lnebehov i fremmed valuta. Nationalbankens rolle 3 knytter sig frst og fremmest til kronelikviditet. Pengeinstitutter med betydelig forretningsomfang i fremmed valuta m selv srge for at opretholde et likviditetsberedskab i de pgldende valutaer. Alt i alt har det danske pengemarked klaret sig forholdsvist godt under uroen. I sidste ende afspejler det jo, at det danske finansielle system er i god form. Den internationale uro er dog ikke get sporlst henover Danmark. Regnskaberne for tredje kvartal viste, at de danske pengeinstitutter ogs var engageret i investeringsselskaber, likviditetsgarantier og strukturerede obligationer. Eksponeringerne og tabene var dog relativt begrnsede. Danske pengeinstitutters udln er vokset kraftigt gennem de senere r. I nogle institutter har vi set vkstprocenter p over 30 pct. Indtjeningen har vret god, og tabene har vret lave. Navnlig boliglnene i form af de skaldte prioritetsln er vokset betydeligt. Vksten i udlnene har vret s strk, at der er opbygget et stort indlnsunderskud p mere end 400 mia.kr., alts det belb, hvormed bankernes udln overstiger kundernes indln. De danske pengeinstitutter er sledes afhngige af finansiering p penge- og kapitalmarkederne. Udviklingen i udlandet henover sommeren har vist, at det kan vre risikabelt at basere forretningsgrundlaget p den form for finansiering. Prisen p markedsfinansiering kan ndre sig hurtigt, og markederne kan "trre ud". Den internationale likviditetskrise har givet anledning til at teste likviditetsberedskabet af og se p forretningsstrategien i lyset heraf. Det er ikke helt s nemt som tidligere for danske pengeinstitutter at finansiere vksten via penge- og kapitalmarkederne. Finansieringen er blevet dyrere, og de stigende finansieringsomkostninger for pengeinstitutterne vil givetvis vise sig i pengeinstitutternes indtjening og priser over for kunder. Udlnsvksten er fortsat hj, men den falder. Nogle pengeinstitutter har skiftet til en mindre aggressiv forretningsstrategi og sat ekspansionsplanerne i bero. Andre har udtrykt intentioner om at reducere engagementerne i internationale investeringsselskaber, likviditetsgarantier og strukturerede obligationer som flge af omdmmerisici. Udviklingen har vist, at strategier baseret p tocifrede vkstrater ikke uden videre kan forlnges. Den strke udlnsvkst til virksomhederne indebrer en strre risiko for, at pengeinstitutterne lider tab. Den risiko er stigende, men fra et meget lavt niveau. Man kan jo aldrig udelukke, at der dukker ubehagelige overraskelser op, men konjunkturerne er endnu gode. Og regnskaberne for tredje kvartal viste ogs, at indtjeningen fortsat er hj i pengeinstitutterne. Generelt er solvensen god, og nedskrivningerne er lave. Set i det perspektiv er det Nationalbankens vurdering i dag, at den internationale uro kan tjene som en "nyttig" 4 forskrkkelse for pengeinstitutterne i Danmark. De ndvendige tilpasninger til de nye forhold kan foretages i tide uden store omkostninger for de allerfleste institutter og for samfundskonomien som helhed. Hvad betyder den finansielle uro for konjunkturerne? Vksten i verdenskonomien har vret usdvanlig hj i de senere r. Men uroen p de finansielle markeder har skabt bekymring for den fortsatte udvikling. Vksten er aftaget i USA, selv om krisen p det amerikanske boligmarked og den afledte finansielle uro endnu ikke for alvor har ramt resten af konomien. Opsvinget ser forelbig ud til at fortstte i Europa og Asien, ligesom konjunkturerne tegner positivt i Afrika og Latinamerika. Olieprisen er steget kraftigt de seneste mneder og lgger en dmper p vkstudsigterne og har samtidig get inflationspresset. De internationale organisationer har indtil videre kun nedjusteret deres vkstskn forholdsvis beskedent  med undtagelse af USA, hvor vksten i 2008 nu sknnes til under 2 pct.  men ikke recession. Der udtrykkes en tydelig bekymring for, at usikkerheden knyttet til de finansielle markeder og nedgangen p boligmarkedet  ikke kun i USA  spreder sig til resten af konomien og dermed trkker vksten yderligere ned i USA og ligeledes rammer Europa. Set i et dansk perspektiv er udsigterne p afstningsmarkederne fortsat gode, om end aftagende. Dansk konomi befinder sig stadig i en strk hjkonjunktur med et hedt arbejdsmarked og kapacitetspres i store dele af konomien. Ledigheden overrasker fortsat positivt. Det stramme arbejdsmarked betyder, at kapacitetspresset forbliver hjt trods forventning om en vis afdmpning af eftersprgselsvksten. Presset har resulteret i en kraftig opgang i importen og i de seneste kvartaler ogs i hjere lnstigninger og i get indenlandsk prispres. Det afspejler, at ln og priser normalt reagerer med en betydelig forsinkelse p konjunkturudviklingen. Et eventuelt tilbageslag kan derfor blive langstrakt, hvis omkostningsniveauet i udgangspunktet er kommet for hjt op i forhold til udlandet. Den aktuelle ophedning af konomien indebrer en stor risiko for et sdant forlb. Renteniveauet i Danmark er af hensyn til fastkurspolitikken afstemt til euroomrdet, som ikke er s langt fremme i konjunkturforlbet som Danmark. Den forventede rentestigning er p det seneste udeblevet som flge af uroen p finansmarkederne. 5 I denne situation vil det vre ret bemrkelsesvrdigt, hvis regeringen fortsat planlgger en ekspansiv finanspolitik for 2008. Regeringen br i forbindelse med udarbejdelsen af den ny finanslov for 2008 revurdere finanspolitikken med sigte p at tage presset af konomien. En udskydelse heraf vil kunne ge kravene p et senere tidspunkt. Det kommende forr byder p overenskomstforhandlinger p det offentlige arbejdsmarked. Det kan konstateres, at der hos de offentligt ansatte er skabt forventninger om markante lnstigninger. De senere rs mangel p arbejdskraft og fokus p kvaliteten af offentlige ydelser har understttet disse forventninger. Flere politiske partier har udtrykt sympati for et ekstraordinrt lnlft til strre eller mindre grupper af offentligt ansatte gennem afsttelse af en srlig pulje hertil. Jeg vil strkt advare mod, at lnforhandlinger p det offentlige arbejdsmarked p forhnd gres til et anliggende for Folketinget. Risikoen for politisk overbud er overhngende og tidlig indblanding fra de politiske partier umuliggr en reel forhandling mellem parterne p det offentlige arbejdsmarked. Der kan skabes en meget uheldig prcedens. For at det ikke skal vre for nemt, skal der ogs til forret vre overenskomstforhandlinger i den finansielle sektor. Det m vre p sin plads ved denne lejlighed at gre opmrksom p de signaler, forhandlingerne p dette omrde kan sende til resten af arbejdsmarkedet. Med disse ord vil jeg slutte med at takke Finansrdet for et godt samarbejde og ser frem til en fortsttelse p samme gode vis.

Title: Speech at the Danish Employers' Association's Employment Conference
text: Speech by Governor Nils Bernstein at the Danish Employers' Association's Employment Conference on 15 September 2010 THE SPOKEN WORD APPLIES DANMARKS NATIONALBANK Challenges and perspectives for the Danish economy and labour market Thank you for the invitation to speak here today. The world economy is once again on the rise. The so-called emerging economies, led by China, have experienced virtually no crisis, but only a brief period of flattening of growth. (Planche 2  International Growth). In developed countries, on the other hand, there has been talk of the worst recession of the post-war period, with marked declines in GDP and increases in unemployment. Denmark has been among the countries where growth has fallen the most. (Planche 3  Growth Europe). That's because we came from a situation of overheating. The expected growth in the Danish economy over the next few years is broadly in line with our neighbouring countries. However, growth is expected to be lower than in Sweden. The Swedes also came from a strong boom, but they have benefited from a falling exchange rate in the short term. Where Sweden really stands out, however, is that it has shown great discipline in economic policy, not least fiscal policy. Among other things, they have been able to manage the municipalities' finances. An indicator of the progress of the world economy is world trade, which is almost back at the pre-crisis level (planche 4 - world trade). There has been growing concern about the outlook for the U.S. economy for some time, but the latest figures suggest it's still moving forward there, albeit slowly. The U.S. continues to grapple with major balance problems. The trade deficit has begun to grow again after a narrowing during the crisis, and the federal budget deficit is over 10 percent of GDP. In Germany and Sweden, on the other hand, the recovery is stronger than previously assessed. In Germany, growth in the second quarter was the strongest since reunification. As these two countries are also our largest export markets, this is good news for the Danish economy. 2 The latest forecasts from the IMF and the OECD project a moderation in global growth in the second half of the year and into 2011, but not sufficient to justify a postponement of the consolidation of public finances. In its latest July forecast, the IMF expects growth in the world as a whole to fall from 4.6% this year to 4.3% next year. The spring market focus was mainly on public debt problems mainly in the so-called GISP countries, i.e. Greece, Ireland, Spain and Portugal. It has now shifted to heightened concerns about whether the recovery will be self-sustaining once the very expansionary fiscal policy comes to an end. In most advanced economies, consumers are still reluctant to spend more money. High unemployment and falling value of wealth increase savings. The problem of the high national debt in many countries has not disappeared. In fact, the yield requirement for Greek government bonds is today as high as when the crisis raged in the spring. (Planche 5  State Span). The same goes for Portugal and Ireland. High interest rates are a significant growth damper. The debt theme will certainly continue to come into the markets' focus at intervals. The debt situation has necessitated a marked tightening of fiscal policy in many countries. Fiscal policy tightening takes place mainly on the expenditure side in the form of reductions in subsidies, transfer payments and, in some cases, government salaries. Expenditure on education and health is only to a lesser extent affected. The same goes for taxes. Many countries have implemented, or are in the case of, quite extensive structural reforms of, among other things, the pension system and the labour market. It supports growth in the longer term. Denmark is apparently in the swing (Planche 6  public debt) with a relatively low debt ratio. When I say "apparently", it is because Denmark is also characterized by probably having the highest tax burden in the world. Virtually all tax bases are taxed to the utmost compared to the situation in other countries. This applies to income tax, VAT, excise duties, registration taxes, etc. The so-called Laffer curve shows the fundamental correlation between tax rate and tax revenue (Planche 7  Laffer curve). At a tax rate of zero, the proceeds are, of course, zero, and the same is true at a tax rate of 100 per cent, for whom will work to earn taxable income if the net salary is zero. In between, there must be a peak. One could draw a third dimension, namely the political and popular will to accept high taxes. I am merely mentioning the housing tax in passing. Where Denmark is located depends on the type of tax, but for some taxes we are given close to the peak. Here, behavioural reactions to increased taxation will make the extra proceeds that can be collected disproportionately small. My point is that there is little room for building further public 3 debts, which, after all, must be repaid with interest. This means that the most significant part of the consolidation must take place on the expenditure side. It is obvious that we in this country have difficulties in managing public spending. Planche 8  Public Consumption). For a number of years, Denmark has been working with medium-term plans in determining fiscal policy. This means that targets have been set for, among other things, the growth in public consumption. They're just pretty much never adhered to, as evidenced by the plaque. The excesses have even often been significant. This is due, as far as I can judge, to a combination of the absence of effective management tools regarding municipalities and regions' spending, and a lack of strength to hold back when it comes down to it. I'm not saying it's easy  quite the opposite. There is an insatiable pressure for higher government spending, which is hard to rein in. There is no indication that the pressure is lessening, even as the level of spending increases. The latest so-called convergence programme for the Danish economy sets out a "benchmark" for public consumption's share of cyclical GDP of 26 3/4 per cent. With the increase in recent years, we are well above that level of spending. The targets for spending growth in the coming years must be described as very ambitious, but necessary. If it is not possible to increase the tax burden, the growth in public consumption must come down if we are not to get into a runaway debt spiral. A declining workforce and an increasing number of people outside the workforce are exacerbating the problem. It is important to understand that even if we were to bring down the general government deficit in the coming years and technically achieve fiscal sustainability in 2015, significant problems remain. The deficits will grow again after 2015, and this will persist for several decades (Planche 9  long-term budget balance). The markets are unlikely to accept that. The problem with the demographic development is not particularly Danish. It is found in all mature economies. What is special for Denmark is that we are close to having stretched our level of taxation to the limit. *** I will now turn to how the Danish labour market has coped with the crisis. The recorded unemployment rate, seasonally adjusted, has been flat over the past year or so. Since bottoming out in the summer of 2008, unemployment has risen 60,000 (Planche 10  labour market). It's surprisingly little given the depth of the crisis we've been through and are now hopefully on our way out of. Employment as recorded in the national accounts has fallen by 165,000 people since it peaked. The workforce has declined by over 90,000. 4 The decline in employment has occurred exclusively in the private sector, while public employment has increased by 15,000 people. It's quite significant. It is common for the labour force to decline as the employment outlook worsens, but this time it is an unusually strong reaction  much stronger than during previous recessions. Part of the explanation is that part of the foreign labor that came to the country during the boom, especially from Eastern Europe, has gone back home. More young people have embarked on an education instead of short-term betting on making money, and those who were already studying with a side job are now studying full-time. As the number of people on permanent support has increased only moderately, there must be a reasonable hope that the increased sensitivity of the labour force to the business cycle is not only in the downward direction, but that vacant hands can be procured fairly quickly when it becomes needed again. That's also what happened during the recent boom. I've marked some entries with an asterisk or an asterisk in parentheses. These are the people I think you can count or partially include when calculating the pressure on the labour market  in other words: the unemployed, who help to dampen wage increases. The number of activated people who are not included in the registered unemployment rate has been continuously increasing over the past two years. A contributing factor may be that municipalities today have a financial incentive to activate. The development has meant an increased spread between the registered unemployment rate and the gross unemployment rate, where the activated are included (Planche 11  unemployment). That's different from the last recession of 2002-2003. Also, the sample-based LFS unemployment rate has increased significantly more than the recorded one, but has also flattened out lately. Previously, the registered unemployment rate and the LFS unemployment also followed each other. However, since 2006, both gross unemployment and LFS unemployment have moved away from the registered unemployment rate. This reflects, among other things, that there are a significant number of people outside the unemployment benefit and cash benefit system who respond that they are ready to take a job. Some of these are learners. All in all, we must note that the registered unemployment rate has lost some of its worth as an indicator of labour market pressures. Gross unemployment must be a better measure, but perhaps not fully comprehensive. All in all, I don't think it's realistic that the unemployment rate at home will come down significantly in the next few years. We are probably close to the so-called "structural unemployment". That is, a level of unemployment that is compatible with sustainable wage growth. *** 5 Construction activity and employment increased significantly as a share of the overall economy during the recent recovery to a level significantly above the historical level (Planche 12  employment in industry and construction). Since its peak, employment in construction has fallen by a fifth. These jobs will not all come back, although the business cycle will improve in the coming years. It is a capacity issue more than a competitiveness issue. There is simply no need for construction to the extent that we saw during the boom. A large part of the dismissed must therefore find jobs in other industries or - in the case of foreign labour - go home. Employment in industry has been declining for many years, but increased during the boom. However, the crisis has also meant the loss of many jobs in the industry. Realistically, we cannot expect a large part of the jobs lost in the industry to come back. How many people will be able to find jobs in industry in the near forward depends, among other things, on our competitiveness. For a number of years, it has been eroded by relatively high Danish wage increases at the same time as weak productivity growth (Planche 13  wages). The Danish rate of wage growth is on the way down, but this is also the case with our competitors, so there is no prospect of any significant competitiveness improvement along the way. For a long time, Danish productivity growth has been extremely weak - both in relation to historical growth and in relation to foreign countries (Planche 14 productivity). However, productivity has risen nicely over the past few quarters. Low productivity growth, coupled with relatively high wage increases, has resulted in a marked deterioration in competitiveness over the past 10 years (Planche 15  Competitiveness). Even with the recent improvement, partly as a result of a weakening of the effective krone exchange rate, we have lost almost 20% since 2000. Increased productivity is central to the continued expansion of our prosperity, but it cannot balance public spending and revenues. Growth in real wages in the private sector is turning into corresponding increases in public wages and in social transfers. The alternative would be an increased inequality in society, which is hardly politically realistic - not least given the number of beneficiaries. As regards public services, there will be a strong desire from experience for them to follow the general development of wealth in society. Increased private sector productivity and thus increased output per hour of work effort will therefore not fundamentally improve the fiscal sustainability problem. The recently published report from the Government's Growth Forum points to a large number of the problems facing the Danish economy, including the relatively low growth in productivity. It's not a new diagnosis. But it is important that there is a broad consensus on the issues. The next thing is: What can we do about it? It's immediately harder to answer. There you seem 6 at least not to be a quick fix. Perhaps the low growth in productivity is just an indication that we are a mature economy with a large service sector, much of which is public. An important question is whether potential production  understood as the level of production that is compatible with stable price and wage developments and normal capacity utilisation  will eventually return to the same growth trajectory as before the crisis. It's doubtful. The contribution of industry and construction to the total potential output will in any case be less, so some will have to find new jobs in, for example, the service sector, where the trend growth in productivity has historically been lower than in industry. *** The adjustments in the Danish labour market during the crisis testify to considerable flexibility in the labour supply. But there are differences between the sectors. In a flexible labour market, employment at enterprises will quickly adapt to changes in demand and, consequently, the need for labour. The fluctuations in productivity measured as production per employed person should therefore be small  the denominator quickly adapts to the numerator in the fraction. Seen over a longer period, the variation in productivity has also been less in Denmark than in most other countries. Only the UK and the US are lower. If we look at the industry in isolation, the adjustment has come promptly (Planche 16  productive industry). The workforce has been adapted to the declining demand and productivity maintained. It's as we'd expect. If we take as a starting point the broader demarcation, "the private urban industries", which also includes the service sector and construction, a different picture emerges (Planche 17  productivity urban occupations). Especially in the services sector, the adjustment to the sluggish times has been somewhat more sluggish, with almost three years of direct decline in productivity as a result. In recent quarters, however, the trend has reversed and production has been increased without new hires. The difference in the adjustment pattern in industry and service sector is reflected in regional unemployment trends. The industry is most strongly represented outside the big cities, while service industries are urban and especially capital based. But it is not because things have gone better there, but primarily because they have held on to labour that has not been fully exploited. I guess there's also a size aspect. Industrial companies are typically larger in terms of turnover and workforce than service companies. Thus, it is the large companies that have behaved the most in accordance with the flexicurity system. Internationally, during the crisis, there has been a big difference in the adjustment rate of labour markets. While employment in the United States has been rapidly adjusted to the decline in production, the reverse has been the case in, for example, 7 Germany, where companies have kept their employees through reduced working hours, among other things. As an element of the spring collective agreements, a severance allowance was introduced here in Denmark for dismissed people with a minimum of three years' seniority. It will thus be more expensive for companies to adjust employment in the case of future cyclical downturns. It's a first step away from the flexicurity model. *** (Planche 18  Compilation). In American politics, the phrase "it's the economy, stupid" has become common property. So it is in this country. We face two main problems, weak growth and lack of sustainability of public finances. Both problems are compounded by the fact that in the coming decades we will have demographics against us, with a decreasing number of working people compared to the entire population. There is therefore a need for measures that increase the share of people in the labour market. Fewer on transfer income, later withdrawal, or longer working hours. In other words, we need to be somewhat more diligent. The problem is recognized by more and more. In fairness, it should also be said that the problem has been addressed. But more needs to be done. And I have no doubt that more will be done. The day we as citizens experience the consequences of population development on the quality of public services, it becomes a requirement. And the longer we wait with the adaptation, the greater the task becomes. Competitiveness, among many other things, is a matter of wages in relation to productivity. Here we are also facing problems that I have touched on. If we are to have full employment and a large enough private sector to finance welfare, wages and productivity must be balanced. But productivity and competitiveness do not remedy the sustainability problem for public finances, as I have mentioned. The latest report from the government's Growth Forum makes the diagnosis. Now we are eagerly awaiting the cure. Thanks for the attention.
text_original: Nationalbankdirektr Nils Bernsteins tale ved Dansk Arbejdsgiverforenings beskftigelseskonference 15. september 2010 DET TALTE ORD GLDER DANMARKS NATIONALBANK Udfordringer og perspektiver for dansk konomi og arbejdsmarked Tak for indbydelsen til at tale her i dag. Verdenskonomien er igen p vej frem. De skaldte vkstkonomier med Kina i spidsen har stort set ikke oplevet nogen krise, men kun en kort periode med udfladning af vksten. (Planche 2  international vkst). I industrilandene har der derimod vret tale om den vrste recession i efterkrigstiden med markante fald i BNP og stigning i arbejdslsheden. Danmark har vret blandt de lande, hvor vksten er faldet mest. (Planche 3  vkst Europa). Det skyldes, at vi kom fra en situation med overophedning. Den forventede fremgang i den danske konomi de nste par r er i det store og hele p linje med vore nabolande. Vksten ventes dog at blive lavere end i Sverige. Svenskerne kom ogs fra en strk hjkonjunktur, men de har p kort sigt nydt godt af en faldende valutakurs. Der hvor Sverige for alvor skiller sig ud er imidlertid, at man har udvist stor disciplin i den konomiske politik, ikke mindst finanspolitikken. Man har bl.a. vret i stand til at styre kommunernes konomi. En indikator p fremgangen i verdenskonomien er verdenshandelen, der nsten er tilbage p niveauet fra fr krisen (planche 4 - verdenshandel). Der har i nogen tid vret stigende bekymring for udsigterne for amerikansk konomi, men de seneste tal tyder dog p, at det stadig gr fremad ogs der - om end langsomt. USA kmper fortsat med store balanceproblemer. Handelsunderskuddet er begyndt at vokse igen efter en indsnvring under krisen, og det fderale budgetunderskud er p over 10 pct. af BNP. I Tyskland og Sverige tegner opsvinget derimod strkere end tidligere vurderet. I Tyskland var vksten i 2. kvartal den kraftigste siden genforeningen. Da disse to lande samtidig er vore strste eksportmarkeder, er det godt nyt for dansk konomi. 2 I de seneste prognoser fra IMF og OECD ventes en afdmpning af den globale vkst i 2. halvr og ind i 2011, men ikke tilstrkkeligt til, at det kan retfrdiggre en udsttelse af konsolideringen af de offentlige finanser. IMF venter i sin seneste prognose fra juli, at vksten i verden under t falder fra 4,6 pct. i r til 4,3 pct. nste r. Forrets markedsfokus l primrt p de offentlige gldsproblemer hovedsagelig i de skaldte GISP-lande, dvs. Grkenland, Irland, Spanien og Portugal. Det har nu skiftet til get bekymring for om opsvinget vil vre selvbrende, nr den meget ekspansive finanspolitik fr en ende. I de fleste avancerede konomier er forbrugerne stadig tilbageholdende med at bruge flere penge. Hj arbejdslshed og faldende vrdi af formuerne ger opsparingen. Problematikken omkring den hje statsgld i mange lande er ikke forsvundet. Afkastkravet til grske statsobligationer er faktisk i dag liges hjt som da krisen rasede i forret. (Planche 5  statsspnd). Det samme glder for Portugal og Irland. Hje renter er en vsentlig vkstdmper. Gldstemaet vil givet ogs fremover komme i markedernes fokus med mellemrum. Gldssituationen har ndvendiggjort en markant opstramning af finanspolitikken i mange lande. Stramningerne af finanspolitikken finder fortrinsvist sted p udgiftssiden i form af reduktion af subsidier, overfrselsindkomster og i nogle tilflde ogs offentlige lnninger. Udgifter til uddannelse og sundhed er kun berrt i mindre grad. Det samme glder skatterne. Mange lande har gennemfrt - eller er ved at gennemfre ganske omfattende strukturelle reformer af bl.a. pensionssystemet og arbejdsmarkedet. Det understtter vksten p lngere sigt. Danmark ligger tilsyneladende lunt i svinget (Planche 6  offentlig gld) med en forholdsvis lav gldskvote. Nr jeg siger "tilsyneladende", er det fordi Danmark samtidig er kendetegnet ved formentlig at have det hjeste skattetryk i verden. Stort set samtlige skattebaser bliver beskattet til det yderste set i forhold til situationen i andre lande. Det glder indkomstskat, moms, punktafgifter, registreringsafgifter osv. Den skaldte Lafferkurve viser den principielle sammenhng mellem skattesats og skatteprovenu (Planche 7  Lafferkurve). Ved en skattesats p nul er provenuet naturligvis nul, og det samme glder ved en skattesats p 100 pct., for hvem vil arbejde for at tjene skattepligtig indkomst, hvis nettolnnen er nul. Der imellem m der vre et toppunkt. Man kunne indtegne en tredje dimension, nemlig den politiske og folkelige vilje til at acceptere hje skatter. Jeg nvner blot boligbeskatningen i forbifarten. Hvor Danmark befinder sig afhnger af skattearten, men for nogle skatter er vi givet tt p toppunktet. Her vil adfrdsreaktioner p get beskatning gre, at det ekstra provenu, der kan hentes, er uforholdsmssigt lille. Min pointe er, at der ikke er megen plads til opbygning af yderligere offentlig 3 gld, som jo skal tilbagebetales med renter. Det betyder, at den vsentligste del af konsolideringen m ske p udgiftssiden. Det er benbart, at vi her i landet har vanskeligt ved at styre de offentlige udgifter. Planche 8  offentligt forbrug). Danmark har i en lngere rrkke arbejdet med mellemfristede planer i fastlggelsen af finanspolitikken. Dvs. der er stillet ml op for bl.a. vksten i det offentlige forbrug. De bliver bare stort set aldrig overholdt, som det fremgr af planchen. Overskridelserne har endda ofte vret betydelige. Dette skyldes s vidt jeg kan bedmme en kombination af fravr af effektive styringsredskaber vedrrende kommunerne og regionernes udgifter, og manglende styrke til at holde igen, nr det kommer til stykket. Jeg siger ikke det er nemt  tvrtimod. Der er et umtteligt pres for hjere offentlige udgifter, som det er svrt at tjle. Der er ikke noget, der tyder p, at presset bliver mindre, selv om udgiftsniveauet stiger. I det seneste skaldte konvergensprogram for dansk konomi opstilles et "pejlemrke" for det offentlige forbrugs andel af det konjunkturrensede BNP p 26 3/4 pct. Med de seneste rs stigning ligger vi et stykke over det udgiftsniveau. Mlene for udgiftsvksten de kommende r m betegnes som meget ambitise, men ndvendige. Hvis det ikke er muligt at forge skattetrykket, m vksten i det offentlige forbrug ned, hvis vi ikke skal komme ud i en lbsk gldsspiral. En vigende arbejdsstyrke og et stigende antal personer uden for arbejdsstyrken skrper problemstillingen. Det er vsentligt at forst, at selv om vi mtte f det offentlige underskud ned de kommende r og rent teknisk opn finanspolitisk holdbarhed i 2015, er der stadig betydelige problemer. Underskuddene vil nemlig vokse igen efter 2015, og det vil vare ved i flere rtier (Planche 9  langsigtet budgetbalance). Det vil markederne nppe acceptere. Problemet med den demografiske udvikling er ikke specielt dansk. Det findes i alle modne konomier. Det der er specielt for Danmark er, at vi er tt ved at have spndt vores beskatningsniveau til det yderste. *** Jeg vil nu vende mig mod, hvordan det danske arbejdsmarked har klaret krisen. Den registrerede ledighed, ssonkorrigeret, har ligget fladt det seneste rs tid. Siden bunden i sommeren 2008 er ledigheden steget 60.000 (Planche 10  arbejdsmarkedet). Det er overraskende lidt i lyset af dybden af den krise, vi har vret igennem og nu forhbentlig er p vej ud af. Beskftigelsen som opgjort i nationalregnskabet er faldet med 165.000 personer, siden den toppede. Arbejdsstyrken er faldet med over 90.000. 4 Faldet i beskftigelsen er udelukkende sket i den private sektor, mens den offentlige beskftigelse er steget med 15.000 personer. Det er ganske markant. Det er almindeligt, at arbejdsstyrken falder, nr beskftigelsesudsigterne forvrres, men denne gang er der tale om en ualmindelig kraftig reaktion  meget kraftigere end under tidligere lavkonjunkturer. Noget af forklaringen er, at en del af den udenlandske arbejdskraft, der kom til landet under hjkonjunkturen, isr fra steuropa, er taget hjem igen. Flere unge er get i gang med en uddannelse i stedet for kortsigtet at satse p at tjene penge, og de, der allerede studerede med et bijob, studerer nu p fuld tid. Da antallet af personer p varig forsrgelse kun er steget moderat, m der vre et begrundet hb om, at den gede flsomhed i arbejdsstyrken over for konjunkturerne, ikke blot glder i nedadgende retning, men at der ret hurtigt kan skaffes ledige hnder, nr der igen bliver behov for det. Det var ogs det, der skete, under det seneste opsving. Jeg har markeret nogle poster med en stjerne eller en stjerne i parentes. Det er de personer, jeg mener, man kan medregne eller delvis medregne, nr man skal opgre presset p arbejdsmarkedet  sagt med andre ord: De ledige, der er med til at lgge en dmper p lnstigningerne. Antallet af aktiverede, der ikke indgr i den registrerede ledighed, har vret uafbrudt stigende over de seneste to r. En medvirkende rsag kan vre, at kommunerne i dag har et konomisk incitament til at aktivere. Udviklingen har betydet et get spnd mellem den registrerede ledighed og bruttoledigheden, hvor de aktiverede medregnes (Planche 11  ledighed). Det er forskelligt fra den seneste lavkonjunktur i 2002-2003. Ogs den stikprvebaserede AKU-ledighed er steget markant mere end den registrerede, men er ogs fladet ud p det seneste. Tidligere fulgte den registrerede ledighed og AKU-ledigheden ogs hinanden. Men siden 2006 har bde bruttoledigheden og AKU-ledigheden bevget sig bort fra den registrerede ledighed. Det afspejler bl.a., at der er et betydeligt antal personer uden for dagpenge- og kontanthjlpssystemet, som svarer, at de er parate til at tage et arbejde. En del af disse er uddannelsessgende. Alt i alt m vi konstatere, at den registrerede ledighed har mistet noget af sit vrd som indikator for presset p arbejdsmarkedet. Bruttoledigheden m vre et bedre ml, men mske heller ikke fuldt dkkende. Alt i alt tror jeg ikke, at det er realistisk, at ledigheden herhjemme kommer vsentligt ned de kommende par r. Vi er formentlig tt p den skaldte "strukturelle ledighed". Dvs. et ledighedsniveau som er foreneligt med en holdbar lnudvikling. *** 5 Aktiviteten og beskftigelsen i byggeriet steg markant som andel af den samlede konomi under det seneste opsving til et niveau vsentligt over det historiske (Planche 12  beskftigelse i industri og byggeri). Siden toppunktet er beskftigelsen i byggeriet faldet med en femtedel. Disse job kommer ikke alle igen, selv om konjunkturerne forbedres de kommende r. Det er et kapacitetssprgsml mere end et konkurrenceevnesprgsml. Der er simpelthen ikke behov for byggeri i det omfang, vi s under hjkonjunkturen. En stor del af de afskedigede m derfor finde job i andre brancher eller - hvis der er tale om udenlandsk arbejdskraft - rejse hjem. Beskftigelsen i industrien har vret faldende gennem mange r, men steg under hjkonjunkturen. Krisen har imidlertid ogs betydet tab af mange job i industrien. En stor del af de tabte arbejdspladser i industrien kan vi realistisk set heller ikke forvente kommer igen. Hvor mange, der frem over vil kunne finde job i industrien, afhnger bl.a. af vor konkurrenceevne. Den er gennem en lngere rrkke blevet udhulet af relativt hje danske lnstigninger samtidig med svag vkst i produktiviteten (Planche 13  ln). Den danske lnstigningstakt er p vej ned, men det er ogs tilfldet hos vore konkurrenter, s der er ikke udsigt til nogen nvnevrdig konkurrenceevneforbedring ad den vej. Den danske produktivitetsvkst har i lang tid vret srdeles svag - bde i forhold til den historiske vkst og i forhold til udlandet (Planche 14 produktivitet). Produktiviteten er dog steget pnt de seneste par kvartaler. Den lave vkst i produktivitet sammenholdt med forholdsvis hje lnstigninger har givet sig udslag i en markant forringelse af konkurrenceevnen over de seneste 10 r (Planche 15  konkurrenceevne). Selv med den seneste forbedring, bl.a. som flge af en svkkelse af den effektive kronekurs, har vi tabt knap 20 pct. siden 2000. get produktivitet er centralt for en fortsat udbygning af vor velstand, men den kan ikke bringe balance mellem de offentlige udgifter og indtgter. Vkst i reallnningerne i den private sektor slr ud i tilsvarende stigninger i de offentlige lnninger og i overfrselsindkomsterne. Alternativet ville vre en get ulighed i samfundet, hvilket nppe er politisk realistisk - ikke mindst i betragtning af modtagernes antal. Hvad angr de offentlige serviceydelser, vil der erfaringsmssigt vre et strkt nske om, at de flger den generelle velstandsudvikling i samfundet. get produktivitet i den private sektor og dermed get produktion pr. times arbejdsindsats vil derfor ikke grundlggende forbedre det finanspolitiske holdbarhedsproblem. I den nyligt udkomne rapport fra regeringens Vkstforum peges der p en lang rkke af de problemer, som dansk konomi str overfor, herunder den forholdsvis lave vkst i produktiviteten. Det er ikke nogen ny diagnose. Men det er vigtigt, at der er bred enighed om problemerne. Det nste er s: Hvad kan vi gre ved det? Det er straks svrere at svare p. Der synes i 6 hvert fald ikke at vre noget hurtigt fix. Mske er den lave vkst i produktiviteten blot udtryk for, at vi er en moden konomi med en stor servicesektor, hvoraf en stor del er offentlig. Et vigtigt sprgsml er, om den potentielle produktion - forstet som det produktionsniveau, som er foreneligt med en stabil pris- og lnudvikling og normal kapacitetsudnyttelse  p sigt kommer tilbage p samme vkstbane som fr krisen. Det er tvivlsomt. Bidraget fra industrien og byggeriet til den samlede potentielle produktion vil i alt fald vre mindre, s en del m finde nyt job i fx servicesektoren, hvor trendvksten i produktiviteten historisk har vret lavere end i industrien. *** Tilpasningerne p det danske arbejdsmarked under krisen vidner om betydelig fleksibilitet i arbejdsudbuddet. Men der er forskelle mellem sektorerne. P et fleksibelt arbejdsmarked vil beskftigelsen p virksomhederne hurtigt tilpasse sig ndringer i eftersprgsel og dermed behovet for arbejdskraft.
