Udsvingene i produktiviteten mlt som produktion pr. beskftiget skulle derfor vre sm  nvneren tilpasser sig hurtigt til tlleren i brken. Set over et lngere forlb har variationen i produktiviteten da ogs vret mindre herhjemme end i de fleste andre lande. Kun Storbritannien og USA ligger lavere. Ser vi p industrien isoleret, er tilpasningen kommet prompte (Planche 16  produktivtet industri). Arbejdsstyrken er blevet tilpasset til den faldende eftersprgsel og produktiviteten opretholdt. Det er, som vi ville forvente. Tager vi udgangspunkt i den bredere afgrnsning, "de private byerhverv", der ogs indeholder servicesektoren og byggeriet, fremkommer der et andet billede (Planche 17  produktivitet byerhverv). Isr i servicesektoren har tilpasningen til de slje tider vret noget mere trg med nsten tre r med direkte fald i produktiviteten til flge. De seneste kvartaler er udviklingen dog vendt, og produktionen er blevet get uden nyansttelser. Forskellen i tilpasningsmnstret i industri og servicesektor afspejler sig i den regionale ledighedsudvikling. Industrien er strkest reprsenteret uden for de store byer, mens serviceerhverv er by- og isr hovedstadsbaseret. Men det er alts ikke, fordi det er get bedre der, men primrt fordi man har holdt fast p arbejdskraft, der ikke har vret fuldt udnyttet. Der er vel ogs et strrelsesaspekt. Industrivirksomhederne er typisk strre for s vidt angr omstning og arbejdsstyrke end servicevirksomhederne. Det er sledes de store virksomheder, som har optrdt mest i overensstemmelse med flexicurity-systemet. Internationalt har der under krisen vret stor forskel p arbejdsmarkedernes tilpasningshastighed. Mens beskftigelsen i USA lynhurtigt er blevet tilpasset produktionsnedgangen, har det omvendte vret tilfldet i fx 7 Tyskland, hvor virksomhederne har holdt p deres ansatte bl.a. gennem nedsat arbejdstid. Som et element i forrets overenskomster indfrtes her i Danmark en fratrdelsesgodtgrelse til afskedigede med minimum tre rs anciennitet. Det bliver dermed dyrere for virksomhederne at tilpasse beskftigelsen ved fremtidige konjunkturtilbageslag. Det er et frste skridt bort fra flexicuritymodellen. *** (Planche 18  opsamling). I amerikansk politik er udtrykket "it is the economy, stupid" blevet almen eje. Sdan er det ogs her i landet. Vi str over for to hovedproblemer, en svag vkst og manglende holdbarhed p de offentlige finanser. Begge problemer skrpes af, at vi de kommende rtier fr demografien imod os, med et faldende antal erhvervsaktive i forhold til hele befolkningen. Der er derfor behov for tiltag, der ger andelen som er p arbejdsmarkedet. Frre p overfrselsindkomst, senere tilbagetrkning, eller lngere arbejdstid. Vi skal med andre ord vre noget flittigere. Problemet erkendes af stadig flere. Retfrdigvis skal det vel ogs siges, at der er taget hul p problemet. Men mere skal gres. Og jeg er ikke i tvivl om, at mere vil blive gjort. Den dag vi som borgere oplever konsekvenserne af befolkningsudviklingen p kvaliteten af de offentlige ydelser, bliver det et krav. Og jo lngere vi venter med tilpasningen, jo strre bliver opgaven. Konkurrenceevne er blandt mange andre ting et sprgsml om ln i forhold til produktivitet. Her str vi ogs over for problemer, som jeg har vret inde p. Hvis vi skal have fuld beskftigelse og en tilstrkkelig stor privat sektor til at finansiere velfrden, m ln og produktivitet afbalanceres. Men produktivitet og konkurrenceevne afhjlper ikke holdbarhedsproblemet for de offentlige finanser, som jeg har nvnt. Den seneste rapport fra regeringens Vkstforum stiller diagnosen. Nu venter vi spndt p kuren. Tak for opmrksomheden.

Title: Speech at the Mortgage Credit Council's annual meeting
text: Nils Bernstein Speech at the Danish Mortgage Bankers Association's annual meeting on 27 April 2006 The Danish economy is in good shape. It is the result of many years of effort and, above all, a very broad political consensus on the fundamental framework for the economy. One does not have to look far outside the country's borders to find examples to the contrary. The big challenge in the short term is to maintain the good times and avoid the economy boiling over. And in the long term, to maintain the balance between the workforce and the rest of the population. The large surpluses on the public finances largely reflect the strong growth, but also extraordinarily large revenues from pension income taxation and corporate tax, including from the North Sea. This type of revenue cannot fund permanent spending increases or tax breaks. The healthy economy must be preserved, and that in itself can be a challenge when we know that the number of 25-60 year olds, the core of today's workforce, will fall by almost 20,000 people a year for the next 10 years. Let me continue with a repetition: In Denmark, we have a fixed exchange rate policy in relation to the euro. In doing so, we are participating in the euro area's efforts to keep inflation close to  but not above  2%. The fixed exchange rate policy has been one of the instruments for achieving and maintaining the good Danish economy. It has ensured steady progress in real wages for wage earners and pensioners and promoted long-term planning in the country's businesses. As you know, you cannot both blow and have flour in your mouth  at least not with good results. Therefore, the fixed exchange rate policy also implies that Danmarks Nationalbank cannot take into account the interest costs of homeowners, house prices for that matter or the cyclical situation more generally when determining Danmarks Nationalbank's lending rate. It is only the currency ratio that determines the interest rate difference between the Danish lending rate and the leading interest rate in the euro area. If there is a persistent trend towards currency outflows, we raise the lending rate without taking into account either the day of the week or the time of day. This is clearly explained in descriptions of Danish monetary policy over the years. Nevertheless, it came as a surprise to some in the market when Danmarks Nationalbank raised its lending rate by 10 basis points in mid-February. Danmarks Nationalbank reacted to a significant currency outflow, and the interest rate hike meant that the currency movements again 2 get in balance. The option to trade when necessary will also be used in the future if currency conditions warrant it. The mortgage banks and the rest of the financial sector are in good shape and make a lot of money. This is partly a result of great activity in the housing market, where the low interest rates, together with other conditions, have driven prices upwards and boosted new construction. Prices of semi-detached and terraced houses have increased by 24 per cent in the past year. Condominiums have increased even more. Price increases have been unevenly distributed across the country, with particularly large increases in the metropolitan area and in the larger provincial cities. So are the strong price increases indicative of a price bubble that is about to burst? Hardly in general. With the prospect of continued high employment, there is no reason to expect house prices to plummet. In addition to the favourable development in employment and real incomes, the price increases so far can be mainly explained by the low interest rate, new forms of borrowing, including loans with deferred amortisation and interest rate adjustment, as well as strong desires to live in certain areas where the supply of housing is limited. Finally, there is the property value tax freeze, which has particularly consequential on prices in the particularly attractive places where the progressive property value tax has or would have an impact. Despite the recent increase, interest rates, both nominal and real, remain very low. With the prospect of better business cycles in Europe and continued high energy prices, it is a widespread expectation in the capital market that interest rates will rise further in the coming period. This will mean lower house prices than usual, perhaps also slightly falling prices, but as long as the favourable cyclical situation persists, there is no prospect of significant general price declines. But as with so much else in this world, we can't be sure. A combination of significantly higher interest rates and unemployment could cause house prices to fall more dramatically. But today this is not the most likely course of events. The surge in real estate prices has created some very large capital gains. If a large part of these gains are translated into consumption, the risk of the economy boiling over increases. The opportunity is there. In 2005, the value of household homes increased by about 500 mia.kr. In comparison, total private consumption was about 750 mia.kr. So for many households, the increase in the value of their real estate has been quite a bit greater than the after-tax income. Fortunately, households have generally managed rising home values cautiously. The increase in home values can probably only explain an "additional consumption" of 7-8 mia.kr. The price increases have instead been knocked out into rising wealth. Even excluding the value of the homes, wealth actually increased in 2005. There was a large borrowing in e.g. mortgage banks, but the loans were largely used to buy financial claims, including for pension savings. 3 Households have embraced the new types of lending. Taken together, its use is not a cause for concern. If interest rates on adjustable-rate loans rise by 1 percentage point, household interest expenses on mortgages will increase by an average of 1.2 percent of gross income. For a household income of DKK 500,000, this corresponds to DKK 6,000 per year before tax. However, there will always be vulnerable groups who have tightened the bow too hard. But it does not have a scope, so it can threaten financial stability. However, there is good reason in the current situation to think carefully so that you do not end up in the vulnerable group. History has shown that Danish mortgage credit is a good system. It has been possible to carry out significant product development within the framework of the system. The Danish Mortgage Credit Council's annual meeting is a good opportunity to mention some of the good characteristics of the Danish mortgage system. The regulatory framework such as loan limits and balance sheet principle make it a very secure system, which the rating agencies emphasize in their assessment. The system has also created a large and liquid bond market. Not least, it gives the individual Dane access to finance the home in a very transparent manner based on the capital market interest rate on the issued bonds plus contributions. Product development in housing finance will undoubtedly continue. Within the coming year, we are likely to have a new formation in the bond field. Denmark must have adapted the regulatory framework for particularly safe bonds  so-called "covered bonds". Due to special security requirements attached to covered bonds, these bonds can be particularly attractive to investors, and thus can also benefit borrowers. The special security requirements of EU legislation will be easier for banks to meet, while it will be significantly more difficult for mortgage banks unless they lower the loan limits. It goes without saying that this can change the competitive relations between banking institutions and mortgage banks. It is Danmarks Nationalbank's opinion that any price advantages of "covered bonds" should benefit borrowers. This is best done by giving both banks and mortgage banks in the legislation framework to issue "covered bonds", so that there are many  and including large  intermediaries of housing finance, and by this product development taking place within a framework that continues to create safe and transparent housing finance on capital market terms. It is therefore important to thoroughly rework the forthcoming rules, including their consequences, so as to establish a legal basis for covered bonds, which creates the necessary framework for a secure housing financing system on the basis of gold-rimmed bonds. 4 Competition is good. It is clear that there is intense competition for the development of new products in the financial system. From time to time, there are also success stories about price competition, for example on the fees for electronic stock trading. Here it became easier for users to see through the market and vote with their feet. When you look at earnings in the financial system, I'm sure there's room for more of those kinds of success stories. With this kindly meant encouragement, I would like to end by thanking you for the good cooperation between the Danish Mortgage Credit Council, the sector's companies and Danmarks Nationalbank.
text_original: Nils Bernstein Tale p Realkreditrdets rsmde 27. april 2006 Dansk konomi er i god gnge. Det er resultatet af mange rs indsats og vel frst og fremmest en meget bred politisk enighed om de fundamentale rammer for samfundskonomien. Man behver ikke kigge langt uden for landets grnser for at finde eksempler p det modsatte. Den store udfordring p kort sigt er at fastholde de gode tider og undg, at konomien koger over. Og p langt sigt at bevare balancen mellem arbejdsstyrken og resten af befolkningen. De store overskud p de offentlige finanser afspejler i hj grad den strke vkst, men ogs ekstraordinrt store indtgter fra pensionsafkastbeskatning og selskabsskat, herunder fra Nordsen. Denne type indtgter kan ikke finansiere permanente udgiftsforgelser eller skattelettelser. Den sunde konomi skal bevares, og det kan i sig selv blive en udfordring, nr vi ved, at antallet af 25-60 rige, kernen i dagens arbejdsstyrke, falder med knap 20.000 personer om ret i de kommende 10 r. Lad mig fortstte med en gentagelse: I Danmark frer vi fastkurspolitik i forhold til euroen. Dermed deltager vi i euroomrdets bestrbelser p, at holde inflationen tt ved  men ikke over 2 pct. Fastkurspolitikken har vret et af instrumenterne til at opn og fastholde den gode danske konomi. Den har sikret rolig fremgang i reallnnen for lnmodtagere og pensionister og fremmet en langsigtet planlgning i landets virksomheder. Man kan som bekendt ikke bde blse og have mel i munden  i alt fald ikke med godt resultat. Fastkurspolitikken indebrer derfor ogs, at Nationalbanken ikke kan tage hensyn til boligejernes renteudgifter, boligpriserne for den sags skyld eller konjunktursituationen mere generelt, nr Nationalbankens udlnsrente fastlgges. Det er udelukkende valutaforholdene, som bestemmer renteforskellen mellem den danske udlnsrente og den toneangivende rente i euroomrdet. Er der en vedvarende tendens til udstrmning af valuta, hver vi udlnsrenten uden at tage hensyn til hverken dagen i ugen eller tidspunktet p dagen. Det er tydeligt forklaret i beskrivelser af den danske pengepolitik gennem rene. Ikke desto mindre kom det som en overraskelse for nogle i markedet, da Nationalbanken medio februar hvede sin udlnsrente med 10 basispunkter. Nationalbanken reagerede p en betydelig valutaudstrmning, og renteforhjelsen betd, at valutabevgelserne igen 2 kom i balance. Muligheden for at handle, nr det er ndvendigt, vil ogs blive brugt i fremtiden, hvis valutaforholdene tilsiger det. Realkreditinstitutterne og den vrige finansielle sektor er i god form og tjener mange penge. Det er bl.a. et resultat af stor aktivitet p boligmarkedet, hvor den lave rente sammen med andre forhold har drevet priserne opad og sat gang i nybyggeriet. Priserne p parcel- og rkkehuse er det seneste r steget med 24 pct. Ejerlejligheder er steget endnu mere. Prisstigningerne har vret ujvnt fordelt over landet med srligt store stigninger i hovedstadsomrdet og i de strre provinsbyer. Er de strke prisstigninger s tegn p en prisboble, der er ved at sprnges? Nppe generelt. Med udsigt til fortsat hj beskftigelse er der ingen grund til at vente, at boligpriserne vil styrtdykke. Ud over den gunstige udvikling i beskftigelse og realindkomster kan prisstigningerne indtil nu i hovedtrk forklares med den lave rente, nye lneformer, herunder ln med afdragsfrihed og rentetilpasning samt strke nsker om at bo i bestemte omrder, hvor udbuddet af boliger er begrnset. Endelig er der fastfrysningen af ejendomsvrdiskatten, som isr har haft betydning for priserne de srligt attraktive steder, hvor den progressive ejendomsvrdiskat har eller ville f betydning. Trods den seneste stigning er renten, bde nominelt og realt, fortsat meget lav. Med udsigt til bedre konjunkturer i Europa og fortsat hje energipriser, er det en udbredt forventning i kapitalmarkedet, at renten vil stige yderligere i den kommende tid. Det vil betyde lavere huspriser end ellers, mske ogs let faldende priser, men s lnge den gunstige konjunktursituation varer ved, er der ikke udsigt til betydelige generelle prisfald. Men som med s meget andet her i verden kan vi ikke vre sikre. En kombination af vsentligt hjere rente og arbejdslshed kan f boligpriserne til at falde mere dramatisk. Men det er i dag ikke det mest sandsynlige forlb. De voldsomme prisstigninger p fast ejendom har skabt nogle meget store kapitalgevinster. Hvis en stor del af disse gevinster omsttes i forbrug, ges risikoen for, at konomien koger over. Muligheden er der. I 2005 steg vrdien af de boliger, som husholdningerne ejer, med ca. 500 mia.kr. Til sammenligning var det samlede private forbrug ca. 750 mia.kr. S for mange husstande har vrdistigningen p deres faste ejendom vret en del strre end arbejdsindkomsten efter skat. Husholdningerne har heldigvis generelt forvaltet de stigende boligvrdier forsigtigt. Stigningen i boligvrdierne kan formentlig kun forklare et "merforbrug" p 7-8 mia.kr. Prisstigningerne er i stedet slet ud i stigende formue. Selv fraregnet vrdien af boligerne steg formuen faktisk i 2005. Der var en stor lntagning i bl.a. realkreditinstitutter, men lnene blev i stor udstrkning anvendt til at kbe finansielle fordringer, herunder til pensionsopsparing. 3 Husholdningerne har taget de nye udlnstyper til sig. Set under t giver anvendelsen heraf ikke anledning til bekymring. Stiger renten p rentetilpasningsln med 1 procentpoint, vil husholdningernes renteudgifter til realkreditln i gennemsnit stige med 1,2 procent af bruttoindkomsten. For en husstandsindkomst p 500.000 kr. svarer det til 6.000 kr. om ret fr skat. Der vil dog altid vre udsatte grupper, som har spndt buen for hrdt. Men det har ikke et omfang, s det kan true den finansielle stabilitet. Der er imidlertid god grund til i den nuvrende situation at tnke sig omhyggeligt om, s man ikke ender i den udsatte gruppe. Historien har vist, at dansk realkredit er et godt system. Det har vret muligt at foretage en betydelig produktudvikling inden for systemets rammer. Realkreditrdets rsmde er en god anledning til at nvne nogle af de gode egenskaber ved det danske realkreditsystem. De lovgivningsmssige rammer s som lnegrnser og balanceprincip gr det til et meget sikkert system, hvilket ratingbureauerne lgger vgt p i deres vurdering. Systemet har ogs skabt et stort og likvidt obligationsmarked. Ikke mindst giver det den enkelte dansker adgang til at finansiere boligen p en meget gennemsigtig facon baseret p kapitalmarkedsrenten p de udstedte obligationer plus bidrag. Produktudviklingen inden for boligfinansiering vil utvivlsomt fortstte. Inden for det kommende r vil vi sandsynligvis f en nydannelse p obligationsomrdet. Danmark skal have tilpasset de lovgivningsmssige rammer for srligt sikre obligationer  skaldte "covered bonds". P grund af srlige sikkerhedskrav, der er knyttet til "covered bonds", kan disse obligationer vre srligt attraktive for investorer, og kan dermed ogs vre til fordel for lntagere. De srlige sikkerhedskrav i EU-lovgivningen vil pengeinstitutterne umiddelbart have nemmere ved at imdekomme, mens det vil vre betydeligt vanskeligere for realkreditinstitutterne, medmindre de snker lnegrnserne. Det siger sig selv, at dette kan ndre konkurrenceforholdene mellem pengeinstitutter og realkreditinstitutter. Det er Nationalbankens opfattelse, at eventuelle prismssige fordele ved "covered bonds" br komme lntagerne til gode. Det sker bedst ved, at bde pengeinstitutter og realkreditinstitutter i lovgivningen fr rammer til at udstede "covered bonds", s der er mange  og heriblandt store  formidlere af boligfinansiering, og ved at denne produktudvikling sker inden for rammer, som fortsat skaber sikker og gennemsigtig boligfinansiering p kapitalmarkedsvilkr. Det er derfor vigtigt med en grundig gennemarbejdning af de kommende regler, herunder konsekvenserne heraf, sledes at der etableres et lovgrundlag for "covered bonds", som skaber den ndvendige ramme for et sikkert boligfinansieringssystem p basis af guldrandede obligationer. 4 Konkurrence er godt. Det er tydeligt, at der er intens konkurrence om udvikling af nye produkter i det finansielle system. Fra tid til anden kommer der ogs succeshistorier om priskonkurrence, eksempelvis p gebyrerne for elektronisk aktiehandel. Her blev det nemmere for brugerne at gennemskue markedet og stemme med fdderne. Nr man ser p indtjeningen i det finansielle system, er jeg sikker p, at der er plads til flere af den slags succeshistorier. Med denne venligt mente opmuntring vil jeg gerne slutte af med at takke for det gode samarbejde mellem Realkreditrdet, sektorens virksomheder og Nationalbanken.

Title: Speech at a conference on the occasion of the 125th anniversary of the entry into force of the Savings Bank Act
text: Nils Bernstein Presentation at conference on the occasion of the 125th anniversary of the entry into force of the first Savings Bank Act d0 The Savings Bank Act of 1880 Thank you for the invitation to participate in the commemoration of the 125th anniversary of the entry into force of the first Savings Bank Act. I have been asked to say something about Danmarks Nationalbank's tasks in connection with financial stability under a main heading called "Financial crises". Financial crises can be very costly. A survey by two economists, Hoggarth and Saporta, covering 43 financial crises in developed and less developed countries, shows that socio-economic losses amounted on average to around 15 per cent of GDP. It can also be costly to bail out individual large banks in order to avoid societal collapse. A domestic example of this was the rescue plan that was to help the Farmer's Bank in 1922-23. It cost the treasury DKK 40 million d0 an amount that, according to Sbfren Mbfrch at that time, corresponded to 2/3 of the state budget's total social expenditure. What, then, are Danmarks Nationalbank's tasks regarding financial stability? Going back to the Danmarks Nationalbank Act of 1936, it states that it is Danmarks Nationalbank's task to "maintain a safe money system in this country and to facilitate and regulate money turnover and credit provision". That we have such a task regarding financial stability is thus clear enough. However, it doesn't say how we lift it. And that's probably also quite wise, since it's something that changes over time. At Danmarks Nationalbank, we have chosen to define financial stability as a condition that exists: When the financial system is sufficiently resilient so that any problems in the sector do not spread and prevent financial markets from acting as intermediaries of capital and financial services. Thus, it is the function of the financial system that is in focus. That money is communicated smoothly in our society as a prerequisite for a well-functioning Danish economy, but also as a basis for the effective implementation of a market-oriented monetary policy. 2 It is important to avoid problems in financial companies not only for depositors and shareholders, but also for society. Because problems in a bank tend to rub off on other institutions d0 if only on the reputation. Depositors and investors may lose confidence. The tue can overturn the load. What exactly are we doing at Danmarks Nationalbank to solve this task? I will give examples of this work below and conclude with a challenge. First, we try to analyze the main risks to the financial sector. It also includes situations that may arise with very little probability, but which may entail great societal costs. We do stress tests of the financial system, where we calculate how much adversity there is room for with the existing buffers. The analyses are published in our annual publication, Financial Stability, in order to create dialogue with authorities, financial institutions and other sector representatives on risks and developments in the financial sector. Some call it "open mouth" operations. In our latest financial stability report, we concluded, based on analyses and stress tests, that the financial institutions remain robust and that nothing can immediately be seen on the horizon that could threaten financial stability in Denmark. We have gradually become accustomed to the fact that the results of financial institutions grow to new heights every year. An important factor in this regard is the high loan growth, a growth that has not been seen higher since the mid-1980s. As shown in Figure 1, the period of high loan growth in the mid-fiurs was followed by a gradual deterioration in credit quality, with increased losses and provisions in the subsequent period. This is not to say that history will be repeated. In the opposite direction, the new capital adequacy rules, Basel II, which will be introduced from the turn of the year 2007, have contributed to an increased focus on credit risk management in financial institutions. When we at Danmarks Nationalbank assess the banks' credit risk, we take as our starting point a bankruptcy model, which is built up on the basis of 400,000 annual accounts submitted by Danish companies from 1995 to 2002. The model corresponds to the models that will underlie the banks' calculation of capital requirements under Basel II if the advanced methods are used. The bankruptcy model is used to estimate the bankruptcy probability of a company. Our analysis based on the bankruptcy model shows, as shown in Figure 2, that there is a certain tendency for banks that have had high loan growth in recent years to also have higher credit risk in the loan portfolio. There are also exceptions, but there is still a need to pay attention to 3 the correlation between high loan growth and the risk of increased losses subsequently. Another topical theme we have addressed is the high gross debt of Danish households when compared with other countries. In Figure 3, the debt is set in relation to GDP. The high gross debt, combined with the widespread use of adjustable-rate loans, makes households more vulnerable to rising interest rates. We have calculated how much household interest expenses on mortgages will increase if interest rates rise. On average, interest expenses on mortgages will increase by 1.2% of gross household income if interest rates rise by 1 percentage point, but there is a big difference between households. There are some households that will be it if interest rates rise by a few percentage points. It may well cause losses in banks and mortgage banks. But taken together, it is our assessment that the development in homeowners' interest rate sensitivity is not a threat to the functioning of the financial system and thus financial stability. Put a little on the point, it can be said that it is not necessarily a financial stability problem that a number of households cannot meet their obligations to their credit institution. In Denmark, we have had a visit from the IMF in the past year in connection with a so-called FSAP, financial sector assessment program. As in other member states, the IMF has carried out an assessment of the layout of the Danish financial system. A report on this will be published within a month's time. In connection with FSAP, stress tests were carried out to assess whether the Danish financial system is resilient to changes in the business cycle. This has been done, among other things, on the basis of Danmarks Nationalbank's macro model, Mona, and a stress test module that we have estimated. The worst stress scenario used by the IMF involves a slowdown in the domestic economy, exacerbated by a monetary tightening by the ECB. House prices fall by 30% and GDP by 3% over a 3-year period. A harsh cocktail! The result of Danmarks Nationalbank's stress test is shown in Figure 4, where the blue line is the actual historical losses in the banks, while the yellow line is the model calculations of the historical course, and the dotted line is the expected development, given the stress scenario. The banks' average losses will thus increase to almost 1.5 per cent of loans and guarantees according to the calculations, i.e. somewhat below the large losses and provisions in the early 90s, which on average reached 2.5 per cent. The Danish financial system thus looks reasonably robust on average. However, this does not exclude that individual banks will receive significantly higher losses, just as in the early 90s there were banks with losses of more than 10 per cent. 4 Stress testing is an area that we will make more of in our work on financial stability. The ambition is to gain more knowledge about how banks affect each other and the economy in stressful situations. Another task for Danmarks Nationalbank in connection with financial stability is the monitoring that we in Denmark have a safe and efficient financial infrastructure that can be safely used in the execution of payments, securities transactions and other financial transactions. It is Danmarks Nationalbank's task to monitor payment and settlement systems in Denmark. It is now also established by law. Part of the IMF's FSAP was an assessment of the most important parts of the Danish financial infrastructure in relation to international standards. The IMF made a few recommendations for changes. As a starting point, Danmarks Nationalbank will - in cooperation with the system managers - ensure that the necessary improvements are implemented. Although we will not uncritically follow all recommendations. An example of the latter is the IMF's recommendation for the establishment of a security pool to ensure the settlement of securities trades and retail payments even in the case when the largest participant is unable to settle the payments. Danmarks Nationalbank considers that the most important safeguard is the participants' easy and flexible access to liquidity combined with the participants' large holdings of securities that can be provided as collateral for loans in Danmarks Nationalbank. We therefore consider that in the current situation it is unnecessary to take separate measures to ensure the dismantling of the Danish systems. A third area we work with is the situations where the financial system is affected by dramatic events from the outside. It can be terrorist acts, it can be large-scale disease outbreaks, natural disasters and the like, where the financial system is threatened with collapse. Danmarks Nationalbank chairs a working group to establish coordination of financial institutions' business continuity plans in such cases. Finally, there is Danmarks Nationalbank's task as "lender of last resort". Danmarks Nationalbank can provide loans to banks that urgently need liquidity and cannot provide liquidity in the market, even if the bank is solvent. Fortunately, this function is only rarely needed. Should it get to the point where there is a need to save a bank in crisis, the starting point for Danmarks Nationalbank will be to find a market-based solution. 5 Nothing unequivocal can be said in advance about Danmarks Nationalbank's role. This will depend on a specific assessment of the situation and the consequences d0 directly or indirectly d0 for the Danish banking system and Danish society. But you can look at what Danmarks Nationalbank has done in the past. In a number of cases, Danmarks Nationalbank has had a role in connection with public interventions in distressed financial institutions d0 financially d0 but also with expertise. The starting point has been that there have been situations that could have negative consequences for the Danish banking system, or that foreign banks would lose confidence in Danish banks. Initially, there was talk of providing a liquidity contingency so that calm could be obtained about the bank in question. But Danmarks Nationalbank has also entered into guarantees to creditors together with the private banks - often on the basis of a state guarantee. Danmarks Nationalbank's participation has in several cases resulted in a solution with the participation of private banks. A classic example of a "lender of last resort" episode was in the summer of 1992, when rumors of difficulties arose for Unibank. It was Denmark's second largest bank and in particular a bank with an impact on the Danish banking system. The episode coincided with the banking crisis in the other Nordic countries and is mentioned in Danmarks Nationalbank's report for 1992: "Rumours of difficulties for Unibank arose early in the summer. The Danish Financial Supervisory Authority immediately refuted the rumours, but in order to counter any liquidity problems abroad for Danish banks as a result of rumours of a solvent financial institution, Danmarks Nationalbank agreed on a liquidity contingency plan with Unibank, cf. the press release of 21 June 1992." Unibank, as you know, managed. Let me conclude by pointing out a challenge we face. In the area of financial institutions, financial integration is more advanced in the Nordic countries than in the rest of the EU, and most large banks have branches or subsidiaries in other Nordic countries. The most prominent example is Nordea, which has significant market shares in each of the Nordic countries (except Iceland) d0 in the case of Denmark, up to a quarter of the deposits. It is EU legislation that has contributed to the harmonisation of the foundations of financial business and removed barriers to cross-border establishment. It is part of the process of creating a single financial market in the EU. 6 Today, Nordea is organised with subsidiaries in the countries, and thus it remains the national authorities that are responsible for the supervision and supervision of the company in each of the countries. In the case of Nordea Denmark, it is the responsibility of the Danish Financial Supervisory Authority. This will change if Nordea d0 as announced a few years ago d0 were to choose to merge into one bank with branches in the countries. In such a case, it is the authorities in the home country d0 as announced, Sweden d0 who will predominantly be responsible for the activities in Denmark, just as it is the Danish authorities that currently supervise, for example, Danske Bank's activities in the branch in Sweden. Such is EU law. The legislation fits a situation where a bank has a relatively small branch in another country. However, the authorities in Sweden cannot be responsible for how Nordea affects the financial stability in Denmark. It remains a Danish responsibility that the financial system can function d0 even if we do not have insight into up to a quarter of the Danish banking market. That is why we at Danmarks Nationalbank have advocated that in the case of large branches that may affect the financial stability of another country, there is a need for more binding cooperation between the authorities of the home and host member states than is provided for in EU legislation. Both supervisors and central banks in the Nordic countries have concluded cooperation agreements on cross-border financial companies. We have a long tradition of cooperating in the Nordic region, and we can probably agree to gain the necessary insight into the current large branches of Nordic banks and vice versa. But the system should also be well thought out to handle business integration north/south in the EU. And here the tradition of cooperation is probably less than between the Nordic countries. To this end, there may be a need to rethink EU legislation so that countries can continue to take care of maintaining financial stability themselves d0 also with the presence of large foreign branches, which in themselves can affect the financial system. There is a need for EU law to have a legal handle that provides host Member State authorities with the necessary insight into a large branch of a foreign bank. Of course, this is not something that is straight up, but changes to EU legislation take time and we do not know when the need will arise. This is an issue that we, in cooperation with the other Danish authorities, will continue to work on.
text_original: Nils Bernstein Indlg ved konference i anledning af 125-ret for ikrafttrden af den frste sparekasselov  Sparekasseloven af 1880 Tak for indbydelsen til at deltage i markeringen af 125-ret for ikrafttrden af den frste sparekasselov. Jeg er blevet bedt om at sige noget om Nationalbankens opgaver i forbindelse med finansiel stabilitet under en hovedoverskrift, der hedder "Finansielle kriser". Finansielle kriser kan vre meget omkostningsfulde. En opgrelse foretaget af to konomer, Hoggarth og Saporta, der dkker 43 finansielle kriser i udviklede og mindre udviklede lande, viser, at de samfundskonomiske tab i gennemsnit belb sig til omkring 15 pct. af BNP. Det kan ogs vre omkostningsfuldt at redde enkeltstende store banker for derved at undg et samfundsmssigt sammenbrud. Et hjemligt eksempel herp var den redningsplan, der skulle hjlpe Landmandsbanken i 1922-23. Den kostede statskassen 40 millioner kr.  et belb der iflge Sren Mrch p davrende tidspunkt svarede til 2/3 af statsbudgettets samlede sociale udgifter. Hvad er s Nationalbankens opgaver vedrrende finansiel stabilitet? Gr man tilbage til Nationalbankloven fra 1936, hedder det, at det er Nationalbankens opgave at "opretholde et sikkert pengevsen her i landet samt at lette og regulere pengeomstning og kreditgivning". At vi har en sdan opgave vedrrende finansiel stabilitet er sledes klart nok. Der str imidlertid ikke noget om, hvorledes vi lfter den. Og det er jo nok ogs ganske klogt, da det er noget, der ndrer sig over tid. Vi har i Nationalbanken valgt at definere finansiel stabilitet som en tilstand, der eksisterer: Nr det finansielle system er tilstrkkeligt robust, s eventuelle problemer i sektoren ikke spreder sig og hindrer de finansielle markeder i at fungere som formidlere af kapital og finansielle tjenesteydelser. Det er alts funktionen af det finansielle system, der er i fokus. At pengene formidles smidigt i vores samfund som en forudstning for en velfungerende dansk konomi, men ogs som grundlag for en effektiv gennemfrelse af en markedsorienteret pengepolitik. 2 Det er vigtigt at undg problemer i finansielle virksomheder, ikke kun for indskyderne og aktionrerne, men ogs for samfundet. For problemer i en bank har det med at smitte af p andre institutter  om ikke andet s p omdmmet. Indskydere og investorer kan miste tilliden. Tuen kan vlte lsset. Hvad gr vi konkret i Nationalbanken for at lse denne opgave? Jeg vil i det flgende komme med eksempler p dette arbejde og slutte af med en udfordring. For det frste forsger vi at analysere de vsentligste risici for den finansielle sektor. Det omfatter ogs situationer, der kan opst med meget lille sandsynlighed, men som kan medfre store samfundsmssige omkostninger. Vi laver stresstests af det finansielle system, hvor vi regner p, hvor meget modgang der er plads til med de eksisterende stdpuder. Analyserne bliver offentliggjort i vores rlige publikation, Finansiel stabilitet, med henblik p at skabe dialog med myndigheder, pengeinstitutter og andre sektorreprsentanter om risici og udvikling i den finansielle sektor. Nogle kalder det "open mouth" operations. I vores seneste finansielle stabilitetsrapport konkluderede vi p baggrund af analyser og stresstest, at de finansielle institutter fortsat er robuste, og at der ikke umiddelbart kan anes noget i horisonten, som kan true den finansielle stabilitet i Danmark. Vi har efterhnden vnnet os til, at pengeinstitutternes resultater vokser til nye hjder hvert r. En vigtig faktor i den forbindelse er den hje udlnsvkst, en vkst der ikke er set hjere siden midten af 1980'erne. Som det fremgr af figur 1, blev perioden i midtfirserne med hj udlnsvkst fulgt af en gradvis forringelse af kreditkvaliteten med gede tab og hensttelser i den efterflgende periode. Dermed ikke vre sagt, at historien vil gentages. I modsat retning trkker det, at de nye kapitaldkningsregler, Basel II, som indfres fra rsskiftet 2007, har medvirket til et get fokus p kreditrisikostyring i pengeinstitutterne. Nr vi i Nationalbanken skal vurdere bankernes kreditrisiko, tager vi udgangspunkt i en konkursmodel, som er opbygget p baggrund af 400.000 rsregnskaber, som danske virksomheder har aflagt fra 1995 til 2002. Modellen svarer til de modeller, som vil ligge til grund for bankernes beregning af kapitalkrav under Basel II, hvis de avancerede metoder anvendes. Konkursmodellen bruges til at ansl en virksomheds konkurssandsynlighed. Vores analyse p baggrund af konkursmodellen viser, som det fremgr af figur 2, at der er en vis tendens til, at pengeinstitutter, der har haft hj udlnsvkst de senere r, ogs har hjere kreditrisiko i udlnsportefljen. Der er ogs undtagelser, men der er fortsat behov for at vre opmrksom p 3 sammenhngen mellem hj udlnsvkst og risikoen for gede tab efterflgende. Et andet aktuelt tema, vi har behandlet, er de danske husholdningers hje bruttogld, nr vi sammenligner med andre lande. I figur 3 er glden sat i forhold til BNP. Den hje bruttogld sammenholdt med den udbredte anvendelse af rentetilpasningsln gr husholdningerne mere srbare overfor stigende renter. Vi har regnet p, hvor meget husholdningernes renteudgifter p realkreditln vil stige, hvis renten stiger. I gennemsnit vil renteudgifterne p realkreditln stige med 1,2 pct. af husholdningens bruttoindkomst, hvis renten stiger med 1 procentpoint, men der er stor forskel mellem husholdninger. Der er nogle husholdninger, der vil komme til at sidde hrdt i det, hvis renten stiger med nogle procentpoint. Det kan godt give tab i banker og realkreditinstitutter. Men set under et er det vores vurdering, at udviklingen i boligejernes renteflsomhed ikke er en trussel mod det finansielle systems funktion og dermed den finansielle stabilitet. Sat lidt p spidsen kan man sige, at det ikke ndvendigvis er et finansielt stabilitets-problem, at en rkke husholdninger ikke kan opfylde deres forpligtelser over for deres kreditinstitut. I Danmark har vi i det forlbne r haft besg af IMF i forbindelse med en skaldt FSAP, Financial Sector Assessment Program. IMF har  ligesom i andre medlemslande  gennemfrt en vurdering af indretningen af det danske finansielle system. Der bliver offentliggjort en rapport herom i lbet af en mneds tid. I forbindelse med FSAP blev der gennemfrt stresstest for at vurdere, om det danske finansielle system er robust overfor ndringer i konjunkturerne. Det er bl.a. sket p baggrund af Nationalbankens makromodel, Mona, og et stresstest modul, som vi har estimeret. Det vrste stress-scenario, som anvendes af IMF, indebrer en afmatning af den indenlandske konomi, som forvrres af en pengepolitisk stramning fra ECB. Huspriserne falder med 30 pct. og BNP med 3 pct. over en 3 rig periode. En skrap cocktail! Resultatet af Nationalbankens stresstest fremgr af figur 4, hvor den bl linje er de faktiske, historiske tab i bankerne, mens den gule linje er modelberegningerne af det historiske forlb, og den stiplede linje er den forventede udvikling, givet stress-scenariet. Pengeinstitutternes gennemsnitlige tab vil sledes stige til knap 1,5 pct. af udln og garantier iflge beregningerne, dvs. noget under de store tab og hensttelser i begyndelsen af 90'erne, der gennemsnitligt nede op p 2,5 pct. Det danske finansielle system ser sledes rimeligt robust ud i gennemsnit. Det udelukker dog ikke, at enkelte banker fr vsentligt hjere tab, ligesom der i begyndelsen af 90'erne var banker med tab p mere end 10 pct. 4 Stresstest er et omrde, som vi vil gre mere ud af i vores arbejde med finansiel stabilitet. Det er ambitionen i hjere grad at f en viden om, hvorledes pengeinstitutterne pvirker hinanden og samfundskonomien i stresssituationer. En anden opgave for Nationalbanken i forbindelse med finansiel stabilitet er overvgningen af, at vi i Danmark har en sikker og effektiv finansiel infrastruktur, som trygt kan anvendes ved gennemfrelsen af betalinger, vrdipapirhandler og andre finansielle transaktioner. Det er Nationalbankens opgave at overvge betalings- og afviklingssystemer i Danmark. Det er nu ogs fastslet ved lov. En del af IMF's FSAP var en vurdering af de vsentligste dele af den danske finansielle infrastruktur i forhold til internationale standarder. IMF kom med enkelte anbefalinger til ndringer. Nationalbanken vil som udgangspunkt - i samarbejde med de systemansvarlige - srge for, at de ndvendige forbedringer bliver gennemfrt. Selvom vi ikke ukritisk vil flge alle anbefalinger. Et eksempel p det sidste er IMF's anbefaling om etablering af en sikkerhedspool til at sikre afviklingen af vrdipapirhandler og detailbetalinger selv i det tilflde, hvor den strste deltager ikke er i stand til at afvikle betalingerne. Nationalbanken finder, at den vsentligste sikring er deltagernes lette og fleksible adgang til likviditet kombineret med deltagernes store beholdninger af vrdipapirer, der kan stilles til sikkerhed for ln i Nationalbanken. Vi vurderer derfor, at det i den nuvrende situation er undvendigt med srskilte tiltag til at sikre afviklingen i de danske systemer. Et tredje omrde, vi arbejder med, er de situationer, hvor det finansielle system pvirkes af dramatiske hndelser udefra. Det kan vre terrorhandlinger, det kan vre omfattende sygdomsudbrud, naturkatastrofer og lignende, hvor det finansielle system trues af sammenbrud. Nationalbanken har formandskab for en arbejdsgruppe, som skal etablere koordination af finansielle institutters forretningsviderefrelsesplaner i sdanne tilflde. Endelig er der Nationalbankens opgave som "lender of last resort". Nationalbanken kan yde ln til pengeinstitutter, der har akut behov for likviditet, og som ikke kan skaffe likviditeten i markedet, selvom pengeinstituttet er solvent. Den funktion er der heldigvis kun sjldent brug for. Skulle det komme s langt, at der er behov for at redde en bank i krise, vil udgangspunktet for Nationalbanken vre, at der skal findes en markedsbaseret lsning. 5 Der kan ikke p forhnd siges noget entydigt om Nationalbankens rolle. Det vil afhnge af en konkret vurdering af situationen og konsekvenserne  direkte eller indirekte  for det danske banksystem og det danske samfund. Men man kan jo se p, hvad Nationalbanken tidligere har gjort. Nationalbanken har i en rkke tilflde haft en rolle i forbindelse med offentlige indgreb i ndlidende pengeinstitutter  finansielt - men ogs med ekspertise. Udgangspunktet har vret, at der har vret tale om situationer, som kunne f negative flger for det danske banksystem, eller at udenlandske banker ville miste tillid til danske banker. Der har i frste omgang vret tale om at stille et likviditetsberedskab til rdighed, sledes at der kunne opns ro om den pgldende bank. Men Nationalbanken har ogs indget i garantier over for kreditorerne sammen med de private banker - ofte p baggrund af en statsgaranti. Nationalbankens deltagelse har i flere tilflde udvirket en lsning med deltagelse af private banker. Et efterhnden klassisk eksempel p en "lender of last resort" episode var i sommeren 1992, hvor der opstod rygter om vanskeligheder for Unibank. Der var tale om Danmarks anden strste bank og i srdeleshed en bank med betydning for det danske banksystem. Episoden faldt sammen med bankkrisen i de vrige nordiske lande og er omtalt i Nationalbankens beretning for 1992: "Der opstod tidligt p sommeren rygter om vanskeligheder for Unibank. Finanstilsynet afkrftede straks rygterne, men for at imdeg eventuelle likviditetsproblemer i udlandet for danske pengeinstitutter som flge af rygtedannelser om et solvent pengeinstitut aftalte Nationalbanken et likviditetsberedskab med Unibank, jf. pressemeddelelse af 21. juni 1992." Unibank klarede sig som bekendt. Lad mig slutte af med at pege p en udfordring, vi str overfor. P pengeinstitutomrdet er den finansielle integration mere fremskreden i de nordiske lande end i resten af EU, og de fleste store banker har filialer eller datterselskaber i andre nordiske lande. Det mest prominente eksempel er Nordea, som har vsentlige markedsandele i hvert af de nordiske lande (bortset fra Island)  for Danmarks vedkommende op mod en fjerdedel af indlnene. Det er EU-lovgivningen, der har medvirket til harmonisering af grundlaget for finansiel virksomhed og fjernet hindringer for etablering p tvrs af landegrnser. Det er et led i processen mod skabelse af et indre finansielt marked i EU. 6 Nordea er i dag organiseret med datterselskaber i landene, og dermed er det fortsat de nationale myndigheder, som har ansvar for tilsyn med og overvgning af virksomheden i hvert af landene. For Nordea Danmarks vedkommende er det Finanstilsynets ansvar. Dette vil ndre sig, hvis Nordea  som det blev annonceret for nogle r siden - skulle vlge at fusionere til n bank med filialer i landene. I et sdan tilflde er det myndighederne i hjemlandet  som annonceret, Sverige  der altovervejende vil have ansvaret for aktiviteterne i Danmark, ligesom det er de danske myndigheder, der i dag frer tilsyn med fx Danske Banks aktiviteter i filialen i Sverige. Sdan er EU-lovgivningen. Lovgivningen passer til en situation, hvor en bank har en forholdsvis lille filial i et andet land. Men myndighederne i Sverige kan ikke have ansvaret for, hvorledes Nordea pvirker den finansielle stabilitet i Danmark. Det er fortsat et dansk ansvar, at det finansielle system kan fungere  ogs selv om vi ikke mtte have indsigt i op til en fjerdedel af det danske bankmarked. Det er derfor, at vi fra Nationalbankens side har gjort os til talsmand for, at nr der er tale om store filialer, der kan pvirke den finansielle stabilitet i et andet land, s er der behov for et mere forpligtende samarbejde mellem hjemlandets og vrtslandets myndigheder, end der er forudsat i EUlovgivningen. Bde tilsyn og centralbanker i de nordiske lande har indget samarbejdsaftaler om grnseoverskridende finansielle virksomheder. Vi har en lang tradition for at samarbejde i Norden, og vi kan formentlig aftale os frem til at f den forndne indsigt i hervrende store filialer af nordiske banker og vice versa. Men systemet br ogs vre gennemtnkt til at kunne hndtere virksomhedsintegration nord/syd i EU. Og her er traditionen for samarbejde nok mindre end imellem de nordiske lande. Til det brug kan der vre behov for at gentnke EU-lovgivningen, sledes at landene fortsat selv kan tage vare p at fastholde den finansielle stabilitet  ogs med tilstedevrelsen af store udenlandske filialer, der i sig selv kan pvirke det finansielle system. Der er behov for, at EU-lovgivningen har et legalt hndtag, som sikrer vrtslandets myndigheder den forndne indsigt i en stor filial af en udenlandsk bank. Det er selvflgelig ikke noget, der er lige op over, men ndringer af EUlovgivning tager tid, og vi ved ikke, hvornr behovet opstr. Det er en problemstilling, som vi i samarbejde med de vrige danske myndigheder vil arbejde videre med.

Title: Speech at the Occupational Pensions Conference
text: Nils Bernstein The role of the pension sector in the economy. Speeches at the Occupational Pensions Conference 2006, 26 October 2006 1. Introduction Thank you for the invitation to give Danmarks Nationalbank's view of the pension sector's position in the economy. Someone might ask what Danmarks Nationalbank knows about the pension sector? Isn't it like with women and football? The metaphor of women and football is not my own, but is taken from an article in the sector's member magazine "Insurance" from 2002, after Danmarks Nationalbank and the Economic Council had been critical of the pension sector's nominal interest rate guarantees. It was pointed out at the time in the article that Danmarks Nationalbank and the Wise Men did not understand the totality of the pension system and that we were too partial in our analyses. That is, of course, a point of view that I will not readily reject. But even though the pension sector does not belong to Danmarks Nationalbank's core area, there are several interfaces: (powerpointslide) A safe money System Macroeconomic Development Financial Stability Efficient Capital Markets But before I get into the touchpoints, I want to give my perspective on the pension sector in Denmark. 2. Perspective on the pension sector In Salmonsen's conversational lexicon of 1923, one can read: "that in the past it was believed that human life should not be subject to assessment, nor to insurance. Quite differently, the development has shaped itself for dependents and, in particular, life annuities. By these interest insurances, as in the case of life insurance, a price was not placed on human life, and the sale of annuities was therefore not considered an immoral business." 2 Today, both life insurance and annuities are an integral part of pension companies, and the pension sector is an important part of the economy and does not engage in what is considered immoral activity. The consequences of the sector's actions are of great importance for the individual citizen. This is due to the wide spread of pension savings among employees and the self-employed, but also the size of the accumulated assets managed. If we go back just 15 years, the Danes' total pension savings (in the pension companies) amounted to almost DKK 350 billion, corresponding to 40 percent of the gross domestic product. Large parts of the population only had the prospect of old-age pension and ATP plus any private savings, e.g. in the form of home equity. Why isn't it like that today? Why isn't it the public coffers that provide the pension? Back in the 60s and 70s, the prevailing (but not sole) view was that pensions should at all times be taken out of contemporary production. The more there should be for the pensioners, the less could become the working people in the same years, and therefore it made little sense for society as such to save for retirement. In any case, the consumption possibilities of the working people and pensioners had to be adapted via fiscal policy to the current consumption possibilities. Of course, society's economic capacity and thus the possibilities of providing a decent pension depended on society's fortunes  but it was not obvious that they depended on whether the savings were more private than public. Against this background, it was widely believed that pensions could most appropriately be based on the "pay as you go" principle, i.e. individual generations finance the predecessors' pension through taxation. It also gave the degree of freedom that there could be some redistribution between the well-off and the less well-off in society. This way of looking at pension financing was also confirmed by the experience of the Social Pension Fund. It was, as you know, conceived in 1970 as a cyclical policy instrument. And as long as pension contributions had to be paid to the fund alone, it did not cause much political problems. However, no concrete proposals were ever made for a supplementary pension financed by the Social Pension Fund. Instead, part of the fund's income was used, inter alia, to finance the housing benefit. They were faced with a communication-impossible task, namely, on the one hand, the consideration of the economy when it came to making supplementary pensions, and on the other hand, the pensioners' expectation of payment from the fund. 3 After a few years, it was decided to cease making any further contributions to the fund. And then there was the balance of payments. The deficits constantly put limits on activity, and in the years when it was worst, we also sent 4 per cent of the year's production abroad to pay interest on the external debt. On the other hand, this meant that if we got receivables instead of debts, then we could enjoy more than we provided. This explains why the political side began to see pension savings as a means of increasing the total savings in society without thinking much about what would happen when pensions were to be paid. Indeed, it was the social consideration for the balance of payments that was one of the reasons why the government in 1987 concluded the so-called joint declaration with the social partners on the establishment of occupational pensions in the collective agreements. A joint declaration that 4 years later resulted in an actual collective agreement between LO and DA, which introduced compulsory pension savings. The fact that the schemes became private is probably due to several factors. The most decisive factor, in my opinion, was that the tax burden in Denmark had already reached about 50 per cent in the mid-80s. There was a broad political recognition that there would be unsustainable distortions in society if there was a further increase in the tax burden. Although I am aware of this not being considered, it can also be emphasised that a pension system based on individual contributions is more robust to developments in the European Union with an increasing number of migrant workers. So out of the almost undisputed need for increased savings in society and the employees' desire for a pension that better aligned with the income to which one had become accustomed came the Danish mix of a pension system. It has in many ways served us well and in any case helped to solve the problem of insufficient savings in society. In fact, multi-tier pension systems such as the Danish one are highlighted in several international contexts as a good benchmark to meet the challenges of the coming decades with an increasing share of pensioners in relation to the total population. Our pension system is three-tiered, consisting firstly of old-age pensions and ATP, then the compulsory occupational pensions, and finally the private pensions, including capital pensions. To this can be added free values in homes and summer cottages and other savings. The system is also three-tiered on the funding side. It is a combination of tax financing, forced savings and voluntary savings. This is precisely why the individual 4 citizen's risks to the future pension size spread out across several strands, making the system robust. There has been a boom in retirement savings throughout the 1990s and into the new millennium. It started with the collective bargaining in 1991, where employees and employers agreed that 0.9 per cent of the salary should be deposited on a pension savings. The employees had to pay 1/3, while the employers had to pay 2/3. Since then, there has been a constant increase in pension payments in the subsequent collective bargaining negotiations. Today, the payments for many employees amount to more than 10 per cent of their basic salary, and the occupational pension schemes - i.e. apart from ATP, Lonmodtagernes Dyrtidsfond and Den Special Pensionsopsparing - today manage a fortune of approximately DKK 1,300 billion, corresponding to almost 85 percent of gross domestic product. As shown in Figure 1, this is almost a 4-fold increase over 15 years. In comparison, deposits in Danish banks have doubled in the same period. Figure 1 "Pension wealth in pension companies" The expansion and construction of occupational pension schemes has also meant that more people today have a pension savings in addition to the ordinary old-age pension and ATP. In 2002, 85 per cent of all full-time employees paid money into an occupational pension scheme. And for the workforce as a whole, about 75 percent pay pension contributions. Figure 2 "Labour force by pension contribution as a percentage of gross salary" However, there are significant differences between the proportion of wages saved for retirement. But, as the figure shows, this proportion is increasing. This is a positive development for the individual, who has the prospect of a larger disposable amount as a pensioner, but also for Danish society. In the longer term, the demographic trend with an increasing proportion of pensioners in relation to the working share of the population will mean that payments from pension funds will gradually catch up and probably overtake the payments. In isolation, this will strengthen state finances. This is due to the fact that there is a right to deduct pension payments against tax liability on payment. This has resulted in a balance sheet inflating society, as part of the pension funds managed by the pension companies are merely deferred tax, and with the movement towards positive net payments, the state's tax asset will eventually be redeemed. 5 On the other hand, this development will provide greater consumption opportunity in society in relation to production compared to today. Whether this will give rise to real balance problems, time will tell. But then think of a situation where it had not been possible to increase pension savings. If, instead, the pension should have been based mainly on the current tax payments! 3. A secure money system Going back to the National Bank Act of 1936, it follows from  1 that: (powerpointslide) "Danmarks Nationalbank ... has as the country's central bank to task ... to maintain a secure money system in this country and to facilitate and regulate money circulation and credit." A prerequisite for a safe money system is low inflation. In Denmark, since 1982, we have chosen to pursue the goal of low and stable inflation by pursuing a fixed exchange rate policy. Maintaining a fixed exchange rate is therefore today one of Danmarks Nationalbank's most important tasks. The fixed exchange rate policy is a cornerstone of economic policy in Denmark. Danmarks Nationalbank's stated goal is to hold the krone firmly against the euro. Danmarks Nationalbank has two instruments to manage the exchange rate, partly intervention using the foreign exchange reserve and partly the short-term interest rate. The foreign exchange reserve is used to handle minor fluctuations in supply and demand for Danish kroner, while the interest rate is only used if there are imbalances of a more persistent nature. As players in the international capital markets, pension funds can influence the exchange rate through the purchase and sale of securities. It is therefore important for Danmarks Nationalbank to keep itself informed of what the sector is doing. With large portfolio restructurings, we sometimes see significant inflows and outflows of currency, which without intervention from Danmarks Nationalbank can lead to inappropriate exchange rate movements. A capital import of 10 mia.kr. strengthens on average the crown by 12 cents per 100 euros. Our analyses show that the pension sector's trading in foreign securities contributes to the explanation of changes in the krone exchange rate. Interestingly, the sector seems to have gained increasing importance for the krone exchange rate in recent years. Our analyses also show that portfolio investments to and from the euro area affect the krone exchange rate more than similar portfolio investments to and from the rest of the world. This indicates that market participants to a lesser extent 6 exchange rate hedges investments to and from the euro area as a result of the Danish fixed exchange rate policy towards the euro. It is not a problem that pension funds are making portfolio restructurings. They are a natural part of the free movement of capital, which is a prerequisite for the efficient functioning of the capital market. And fortunately, we at Danmarks Nationalbank have skilled people who monitor movements in the foreign exchange market on a daily basis and are therefore also ready to react if the krone should move too far in one direction or the other. At the same time, we can welcome the credibility that the Danish fixed exchange rate policy enjoys - nationally as well as internationally. Let me take this opportunity to debunk a myth. The fact that the Danish economy is fundamentally in good shape with declining government debt and a savings surplus does not cause problems in terms of maintaining the Danish fixed exchange rate policy. At most, there may be short-term movements in the exchange rate as a result of portfolio restructuring. The opposite situation  namely a weak economy  could be a problem. 4. Macroeconomic development - from debtor to creditor nation Confidence in the Danish fixed exchange rate policy is not only Danmarks Nationalbank's profit. It is part of the story that Denmark up through the 1980s got a handle on fiscal policy and slowly and with some dents along the way turned a structural deficit on the current account into surplus. A sustainable fiscal policy and a clear division of labor in economic policy improve the ability of the Central Bank to meet its goal. In Denmark, the division of labour is explicitly formulated: monetary policy is designed to ensure a stable exchange rate of the krone against the euro, while a specific Danish need to stabilise the business cycle rests with fiscal policy. As regards the favourable development of the balance of payments, there is no ingending in the fact that the pension sector has also played a role, in particular through increased savings. The Danes' increasing pension savings through, among other things, occupational pension schemes have  as I have already mentioned  had an impact on the economic development in Denmark in recent years. Whereas the socio-economic debate was previously concentrated on the lack of savings in society with deficits in both the current account of the balance of payments and the public finances, today we are in a situation of savings surplus. Figure 3 Balance of payments and government budget balance One of the driving forces behind this development has been the increased pension savings in society. 7 However, it must be borne in mind that savings in society would hardly have turned positive if the real interest rate after tax had not also  for most people  become positive and thus created an incentive for savings. And here, fixed exchange rate policy has played a crucial role in reining in inflation expectations. Whether the total savings in a society actually increase when compulsory retirement savings are introduced depends, of course, on whether these payments displace other forms of savings. Calculations made by the Ministry of Economic and Business Affairs suggest that the increased pension payments have fully impacted the total savings. That is, other savings have not been displaced by the Danes' increasing pension savings. The development with greater savings has led To Denmark becoming a net creditor abroad at the end of 2005 for the first time since World War II. Figure 4 Danish external debt as a percentage of GDP 5. Pension companies and financial stability We at Danmarks Nationalbank have chosen to define financial stability as a condition that exists: (powerpointslide) When the financial system is sufficiently resilient so that any problems in the sector do not spread and prevent financial markets from acting as intermediaries of capital and financial services. Thus, it is the function of the financial system that is in focus. That the money is conveyed smoothly in our society. The pension sector is part of the financial system and can affect financial stability in Denmark. Unlike banks, however, the impact of pension companies on financial stability is more indirect. Pension companies are characterised by long-term obligations that cannot be terminated overnight. Thus, the risk of a "run"  i.e. a situation where pension savers try quickly and at the same time to withdraw money from a pension company  is virtually non-existent. Let me stress that financial stability cannot simply be defined as the absence of "runs". It is a necessary, but certainly not a sufficient condition. As I mentioned, it is the function of the financial system that is in focus, and here trust is the alpha and omega. It is important that pension savers have confidence in the pension companies  i.e. feel convinced that there is also money in the coffers when the pension is to be paid. And the best way to ensure that is by 8 the assets and liabilities of pension funds fluctuate at the same rate as economic conditions change. "Traffic lights" Today, pension companies have become more focused on risk management and hedging than was the case 5 to 10 years ago. In Denmark, the Danish Financial Supervisory Authority has prepared risk scenarios - the so-called "traffic lights" - which are instant events that are used to test the pension companies' resilience to a negative market development. The basic idea behind the traffic lights is to illustrate the investment and insurance risks of pension companies, so that pension companies have time to react to a changed risk picture before it is too late. This has certainly contributed to making the Danish pension sector more resilient to financial and insurance risks. At the same time, it has been a necessity in an increasingly globalized world, where external shocks also propagate to the Danish economy. At the same time, the construction of new and more complicated financial products places great demands on the pension sector, but also on the authorities. It is important that the management of pension funds understands the underlying risks that a given investment or obligation entails. Otherwise, one day you risk waking up to an unpleasant surprise. An example where it went wrong is LTCM in 1998. Long Term Capital Management, a major U.S. hedge fund, specialized in building large leveraged positions across multiple markets financed by borrowing in a wide variety of U.S. and European financial institutions. LTCM intended to leverage imperfections in the market. The success of the strategy depended on a number of assumptions about the underlying market correlations and volatilities. But with Nobel laureates Myron Scholes and Robert Merton, things couldn't go wrong! But it could. As it turned out, the underlying assumptions did not hold true in turbulent market conditions, and LTCM had to turn the key in 1998 after losing 4.6 billion in less than 4 months. Although Danish pension companies hardly make as risky investments, it illustrates very well that what does not seem very risky in advance may turn out to be the following. However, there is a byproduct of stress tests like the traffic lights. In turbulent market conditions, such as we experienced in the autumn of 2001, for example, pension companies are forced to simultaneously undertake large 9 portfolio restructurings so as not to get in trouble with the FSA's "traffic lights". This risks reinforcing an already negative spiral. And in a declining market, you never get the best prices for your assets. The solution, of course, is not to abolish the "traffic lights", but instead to try to avoid a situation where they can cause inconveniences. Specifically, this means that companies must adjust reserve structure for risk-taking. The sector's responsibility The growing Danish pension wealth places demands on the sector to continue to be responsible in terms of investment behaviour, but also for product offerings and marketing. Both commercial as well as occupational pension funds have increasingly wanted customers to switch to market-rate products, i.e. products where returns are more directly linked to market developments in the financial markets. This pushes a larger part of the investment risk onto the individual pension saver. One of the arguments that pension companies often use when selling a "market product" is that the return is typically better than with a traditional retirement savings. I don't want to rule that out that's the case, but there's rarely any "free lunch." A greater expected return must necessarily be associated with more risk. If the customer understands and accepts this context, there is no problem. The problem arises in those cases when advertising and "skillful" marketing make customers choose products whose associated risks they do not understand! It is therefore important that pension companies are aware of the adviser responsibility they have. There is no sure answer as to how interest rates and stock prices will evolve in the future. The pension company may have expectations for the development, but no one knows how it will go. So what was good advice ex ante may well turn out not to be that ex post. The same can be said about advice, which is based on tax aspects. Thus, no one can know how the tax system will be screwed up in 20-30 years in relation to the individual's income composition. Clearly, the crisis in the pension sector that followed the 2000-2002 stock downturn gave many companies a bit of a shell shock. Falling stock prices combined with lower interest rates and rising life expectancy was a dangerous cocktail. 10 One of the challenges for the industry has therefore been to avoid facing a similar situation. Many have tried with just a solution based on individual products, where the pension savers themselves bear most of the risks. It's a remarkable development. Insurers are trying to avoid selling insurance  to put it a bit on the line  both insurance in relation to market development, but also insurance in relation to life expectancy (here I am thinking of the wide prevalence of instalment pensions). Otherwise, it should be in this area that companies have a comparative advantage in terms of pension savings compared to the rest of the financial sector. 6. Rounding out I have spoken of the pension sector as a single entity, which is far from the case. Overall, it can be divided into two almost equal parts, the occupational pension funds, which are customer-owned, and the commercial pension companies, which are typically part of a larger financial group. The commercial pension companies compete for customers on similar terms to other financial companies. This means that they are basically trying to convince customers that their product is best for the price. Occupational pension funds live quieter lives. Their members often have no choice as to which pension fund they will use. It is determined on the basis of a collective agreement. If one wants to look at market share for the Life and Pensions sector, it only makes sense to look at the part of the industry where pension customers or companies have a real choice in terms of pension provider. Calculated in this way, the 5 largest pension companies accounted for about 90 percent of the market at the end of 2005, whether we look at gross premiums or balance sheet totals. Figure 5 Market shares of the market-based pension companies Competition is good! But if you look at the costs of pension companies, the Danish Financial Supervisory Authority writes in its report "Market development 2005 for life insurance companies and lateral pension funds" that the average costs in the collective bargaining schemes are less than in the market-oriented companies. This is an interesting observation, as competition should increase efficiency and push the cost level downwards. I'm sure the market-based companies have a lot of good explanations for why this isn't the case, so I won't go into that. 11 I can only state that costs opposite returns are a quantity that can often be predicted with relatively high certainty based on historical observations. Thus, empirical studies have shown that costs are characterized by a significant degree of persistence. In Danish, this means that a company with high costs today has a high probability of also having high costs tomorrow. The same applies if the company has a low cost. And even very small differences in cost ratios can in the course of a working life turn into several hundred thousand dollars for the individual in pure savings at the time of retirement. It underscores the importance of focusing on costs, but also the need for transparency so that customers can see what they are paying and what they are paying for. - 0 - Today, the pension sector is a crucial part of the Danish economy, and nothing suggests that this picture will change in the future. As the major war cohorts retire and life expectancy for the population increases, Danish society will experience some structural changes where the need for a well-functioning pension sector will obviously be present. It is therefore positive that the pension sector has received increasing focus on risk management and hedging, and that an increasingly large proportion of Danes are saving for their own pension.

Et sikkert pengevsen Gr man tilbage til Nationalbankloven fra 1936 flger det af  1, at: (powerpointslide) "Danmarks Nationalbank  har som landets centralbank til opgave  at opretholde et sikkert pengevsen her i landet samt at lette og regulere pengeomstning og kreditgivning." I modstning til banker er pensionsselskabers pvirkning af den finansielle stabilitet dog mere indirekte. Trafiklys Pensionsselskaberne har i dag fet mere fokus p risikostyring og risikoafdkning, end hvad der var tilfldet for 5 til 10 r siden. I Danmark har Finanstilsynet udarbejdet risikoscenarier - de skaldte "trafiklys" - som er jeblikshndelser, der bruges til at teste pensionsselskabernes modstandskraft overfor en negativ markedsudvikling. Grundtanken bag trafiklysene er at anskueliggre pensionsselskabernes investerings- og forsikringsmssige risici, sledes at pensionsselskaberne fr tid til at reagere p et ndret risikobillede, fr det er for sent. Det har helt sikkert bidraget til at gre den danske pensionssektor mere robust overfor finansielle og forsikringsmssige risici. Det har samtidig vret en ndvendighed i en stadig mere globaliseret verden, hvor eksterne choks ogs forplanter sig til den danske konomi. Konstruktionen af nye og mere komplicerede finansielle produkter stiller samtidig store krav til pensionssektoren, men ogs til myndighederne. Det er vigtigt, at pensionsselskabernes ledelse forstr de underliggende risici, som en given investering eller forpligtelse medfrer. Ellers risikerer man en dag at vgne op til en ubehagelig overraskelse. Et eksempel, hvor det gik galt, er LTCM i 1998. Long Term Capital Management, der var en stor amerikansk hedge fund, havde specialiseret sig i at opbygge store gearede positioner p tvrs af flere markeder finansieret ved lntagning i en lang rkke amerikanske og europiske finansielle institutioner. LTCM havde til hensigt at udnytte imperfektioner i markedet. Strategiens succes afhang af en rkke antagelser om de underliggende markedskorrelationer og volatiliteter. Men med nobelpristagerne Myron Scholes og Robert Merton kunne det ikke g galt! Men det kunne det. For det skulle nemlig vise sig, at de underliggende antagelser ikke holdt stik under turbulente markedsforhold, og LTCM mtte i 1998 dreje nglen om efter at have tabt 4,6 mia. dollar p mindre end 4 mneder. Selv om danske pensionsselskaber nppe foretager liges risikable investeringer, illustrerer det meget godt, at hvad der ikke synes srlig risikabelt p forhnd, kan vise sig at vre det efterflgende. Der er dog et biprodukt ved stresstest som trafiklysene. Under turbulente markedsforhold, som vi fx oplevede i efterret 2001, bliver pensionsselskaberne tvunget til samtidigt at foretage store 9 portefljeomlgninger for ikke at komme i karambolage med Finanstilsynets "trafiklys".
